docs.text: Agathas.Storefront - Solution Documentation Comprehensive technical and business documentation for Agathas.Storefront e-commerce platform Documentation Overview This documentation suite provides a complete analysis of Agathas.Storefront, a classic ASP.NET MVC 2 e-commerce application built circa 2010. The documentation was generated through comprehensive codebase analysis following industry-standard architectural documentation patterns (C4 Model, ADR, Domain-Driven Design). Purpose For New Team Members : Accelerate onboarding with comprehensive system understanding For Business Stakeholders : Provide visibility into system capabilities, risks, and modernization opportunities For Technical Teams : Document architecture, dependencies, and technical debt for informed decision-making For Operations : Enable effective system maintenance, deployment, and incident response For Architects : Facilitate modernization planning and architectural evolution Documentation Generation Generated : 2026-06-09 Generation Method : Multi-phase automated analysis of codebase structure, configuration files, and architectural patterns Coverage : 7 projects spanning 6,104 lines of code across 192 classes Analysis Scope : 60 analysis artifacts, 9 business documents, 4 architecture documents Analysis Tool : GitHub Copilot in documentation-compiler mode with custom analysis agents Generation Process Pre-Analysis Phase (60 JSON artifacts) Discovery & inventory analysis (9 files) Architecture mapping (6 files) Business context analysis (6 files) UI/screen analysis (10 files) Security & compliance analysis (5 files) Testing & quality analysis (6 files) Operations & infrastructure analysis (6 files) Performance analysis (4 files) Developer experience analysis (4 files) Modernization readiness assessment (4 files) Business Documentation Phase (7 documents) Current state business analysis (5 documents) Modernization strategy (2 documents) Architecture Documentation Phase (4 documents) Current state architecture (4 documents) Documentation Compilation Phase (this document) Generic binding documents for navigation Role-based quick start guides Technical glossary How to Navigate Each document in this suite focuses on a specific architectural or business concern. docs.text: Agathas.Storefront - Executive Summary ⚠️ CRITICAL - Evidence-Based Analysis Only : - All metrics, findings, and assessments in this document are derived from comprehensive codebase analysis (60 JSON artifacts) - NO placeholder estimates for timelines, costs, or effort levels are included - Where data is unavailable from static analysis, we explicitly state WHY, WHAT is needed, and WHERE to obtain it - All claims are backed by specific code references, configuration files, or analysis artifacts Quick Reference : This document consolidates findings from comprehensive architecture analysis covering current state, business domain, security posture, compliance status, and modernization priorities. Evidence-Based Analysis Guidelines Scope of This Analysis What This Document Contains : - ✅ Findings from static code analysis (7 projects, 192 classes, 6,104 LOC) - ✅ Architecture patterns identified through code structure examination - ✅ Security vulnerabilities from dependency analysis and code review - ✅ Compliance gap analysis against documented requirements - ✅ Technology obsolescence assessment from version identification - ✅ Business rules extracted from domain model implementation What This Document Does NOT Contain : - ❌ Production performance metrics (requires runtime monitoring) - ❌ Actual usage patterns (requires analytics/APM data) - ❌ Capacity measurements (requires load testing or production telemetry) - ❌ Firm timeline estimates (requires team capacity, task breakdown, velocity baselines) - ❌ Cost projections (requires usage patterns, cloud provider pricing) - ❌ Risk probabilities (requires historical incident data) When Data is Unavailable Throughout this document, when specific data cannot be derived from static analysis, we provide: 1. WHY : The reason static analysis cannot determine this information 2. WHAT : Specific data points needed to make the determination 3. WHERE : The data source or analysis method required Table of Contents Architecture Overview Critical Security Findings Operations & Infrastructure Quality & Technical Debt Modernization Priorities Recommended Action Plan Success Metrics Conclusion Architecture Overview Application Profile Aspect Details Application Agathas.Storefront - E-commerce Platform Technology .NET Framework 3.5/4.0, ASP.NET MVC 2, C# 3.5/4.0 ORM NHibernate 2.1 with XML mappings (HBM.XML) Database SQL Server Express LocalDB (User Instance mode - deprecated) Frontend ASPX views, jQuery 1.3.2, CSS-based layouts (non-responsive) Architecture 5-tier layered with Domain-Driven Design (Presentation, Services, Domain, Data Access, Infrastructure) Deployment Single-server monolithic deployment on IIS 7.0+ Codebase Size 6,104 LOC across 192 classes in 7 projects Module Count 7 Visual Studio projects (UI, Controllers, Services, Model, Repository, Infrastructure) Evidence Source : technology-inventory.json , code-metrics.json , project-inventory.json , System Architecture Architectural Strengths ✅ Excellent Domain-Driven Design Implementation - 4 well-defined aggregates with clear boundaries: Product (root: ProductTitle), Basket, Order, Customer - Rich domain entities with encapsulated business logic (40+ documented business rules) - Value objects for Address, Payment, ProductSize, ProductColor - Domain events infrastructure (1 event implemented: OrderSubmittedEvent) - Evidence : Business Domain Model , business-rules.json , domain-events.json ✅ Clean Layered Architecture with Unidirectional Dependencies - 5 distinct layers with proper separation of concerns - Dependencies flow downward only (Presentation → Services → Domain → Data → Infrastructure) - No circular dependencies detected - Cross-cutting concerns properly isolated in Infrastructure layer - Evidence : application-layers.json , dependency-graph.json , System Architecture - Container Diagram ✅ Strong Design Patterns Throughout Codebase - Repository Pattern: Clean data access abstraction with interfaces in domain, implementations in data layer - Unit of Work Pattern: Transaction management via NHUnitOfWork wrapping ISession - Dependency Injection: StructureMap IoC container with convention-based registration - State Pattern: Order lifecycle management (Pending → Processing → Shipped → Delivered) - Factory Pattern: IoCControllerFactory for MVC controller instantiation - Evidence : architectural-patterns.json , code references in Agathas.Storefront.Model and Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate projects ✅ High Testability Design (Despite Zero Current Tests) - Interface-based abstractions throughout (IProductRepository, IBasketRepository, etc.) - Dependency injection enables test doubles - Domain logic isolated from infrastructure concerns - Pure business rules with no framework dependencies - Evidence : System Architecture - Architectural Characteristics , project structure analysis ✅ Well-Encapsulated Business Rules - Business rules enforced within domain entities (not in controllers or services) - Dedicated business rule classes: BasketBusinessRules, OrderBusinessRules, AddressBusinessRules - Validation at aggregate boundaries - No anemic domain model anti-pattern - Evidence : business-rules.json , Business Domain Model - Business Rules Catalog ✅ Complete E-Commerce Business Capabilities - Product catalog with hierarchical categories and brand management - Shopping cart with delivery options and total calculation - Customer accounts with saved delivery addresses - docs.title: Application Profile

docs.text: ✅ Excellent Domain-Driven Design Implementation - 4 well-defined aggregates with clear boundaries: Product (root: ProductTitle), Basket, Order, Customer - Rich domain entities with encapsulated business logic (40+ documented business rules) - Value objects for Address, Payment, ProductSize, ProductColor - Domain events infrastructure (1 event implemented: OrderSubmittedEvent) - Evidence : Business Domain Model , business-rules.json , domain-events.json ✅ Clean Layered Architecture with Unidirectional Dependencies - 5 distinct layers with proper separation of concerns - Dependencies flow downward only (Presentation → Services → Domain → Data → Infrastructure) - No circular dependencies detected - Cross-cutting concerns properly isolated in Infrastructure layer - Evidence : application-layers.json , dependency-graph.json , System Architecture - Container Diagram ✅ Strong Design Patterns Throughout Codebase - Repository Pattern: Clean data access abstraction with interfaces in domain, implementations in data layer - Unit of Work Pattern: Transaction management via NHUnitOfWork wrapping ISession - Dependency Injection: StructureMap IoC container with convention-based registration - State Pattern: Order lifecycle management (Pending → Processing → Shipped → Delivered) - Factory Pattern: IoCControllerFactory for MVC controller instantiation - Evidence : architectural-patterns.json , code references in Agathas.Storefront.Model and Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate projects ✅ High Testability Design (Despite Zero Current Tests) - Interface-based abstractions throughout (IProductRepository, IBasketRepository, etc.) - Dependency injection enables test doubles - Domain logic isolated from infrastructure concerns - Pure business rules with no framework dependencies - Evidence : System Architecture - Architectural Characteristics , project structure analysis ✅ Well-Encapsulated Business Rules - Business rules enforced within domain entities (not in controllers or services) - Dedicated business rule classes: BasketBusinessRules, OrderBusinessRules, AddressBusinessRules - Validation at aggregate boundaries - No anemic domain model anti-pattern - Evidence : business-rules.json , Business Domain Model - Business Rules Catalog ✅ Complete E-Commerce Business Capabilities - Product catalog with hierarchical categories and brand management - Shopping cart with delivery options and total calculation - Customer accounts with saved delivery addresses - Order processing with state management and payment integration (PayPal) - Email notifications via domain events - Evidence : business-processes.json , Requirements Specification ✅ PCI DSS Compliance via Proper Delegation - No cardholder data stored locally - All payment processing delegated to PayPal Payment Gateway - SAQ A compliance level (simplest - no direct card handling) - Evidence : Compliance and Regulatory - PCI DSS , Integration Points ✅ Good Code Organization and Conventions - Consistent naming conventions throughout - Logical project organization by architectural layer - Namespace structure mirrors folder structure - Code demonstrates SOLID principles - Evidence : coding-standards.json , project-inventory.json

docs.text: Vulnerability : Sensitive credentials stored unencrypted in Web.config Evidence : <!-- File: Agathas.Storefront.UI.Web.MVC/Web.config --> <!-- Lines 15-35: Connection strings in plaintext --> <connectionStrings> <add name= "Shop" connectionString= "Data Source=.\SQLEXPRESS;AttachDbFilename=|DataDirectory|\Shop.mdf;User Instance=true;Integrated Security=SSPI" /> <add name= "ApplicationServices" connectionString= "Data Source=.\SQLEXPRESS;AttachDbFilename=|DataDirectory|\aspnetdb.mdf;User Instance=true;Integrated Security=SSPI" /> </connectionStrings> <!-- Lines 87-95: SMTP credentials in plaintext --> <system.net> <mailSettings> <smtp from= "noreply@agathasstorefront.com" > <network host= "smtp.example.com" port= "587" userName= "username" password= "password" /> </smtp> </mailSettings> </system.net> Impact : - Credentials exposed to anyone with file system access or source control access - Risk of credential theft and unauthorized system access - Non-compliance with security best practices CWE : CWE-522 (Insufficiently Protected Credentials) Remediation : 1. Move connection strings to environment variables or secure key vault 2. Encrypt Web.config sections using DPAPI or cloud-native secret management 3. Use managed identities for cloud database connections 4. Implement secret rotation policies
docs.title: 1. Plaintext Secrets in Configuration 🔴 CRITICAL

docs.text: Vulnerability : Outdated JavaScript library with known XSS vulnerabilities Evidence : <!-- File: Agathas.Storefront.UI.Web.MVC/Scripts/jquery-1.3.2.js --> <!-- Version: jQuery v1.3.2 (February 2009 - 17 years old) --> Known CVEs : - CVE-2011-4969: XSS vulnerability via location.hash manipulation - CVE-2012-6708: XSS vulnerability in selector interpretation - CVE-2015-9251: XSS vulnerability via HTML string input Impact : - Attackers can inject malicious scripts - User session hijacking risk - Potential data theft from client-side CVSS Score : 6.1 (Medium) - CVE-2015-9251 CWE : CWE-79 (Cross-Site Scripting) Remediation : - Immediate: Upgrade to jQuery 3.6+ or migrate to modern framework - Impact: Affects all pages using jQuery validation and AJAX calls - Testing required: Full regression testing of client-side functionality
docs.title: 2. jQuery 1.3.2 with Multiple CVEs 🔴 CRITICAL

docs.text: Vulnerability : Using deprecated database attachment mode that is unsupported and insecure Evidence : <!-- File: Web.config --> <connectionStrings> <add name= "Shop" connectionString= "...User Instance=true..." /> </connectionStrings> Impact : - User Instance mode deprecated since SQL Server 2012 - Not supported in modern SQL Server versions - Cannot migrate to cloud databases without code changes - Security: Each user gets database instance with elevated permissions CWE : CWE-1104 (Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components) Remediation : - Replace with standard SQL Server connection (no User Instance) - Migrate to cloud-managed database (Azure SQL, RDS, Cloud SQL) - Implement proper connection pooling - Update connection strings throughout application
docs.title: 3. SQL Server User Instance Mode (Deprecated) 🔴 CRITICAL

docs.text: Vulnerability : Running on unsupported framework versions with no security patches Evidence : <!-- File: Agathas.Storefront.Controllers/Agathas.Storefront.Controllers.csproj --> <TargetFrameworkVersion> v3.5 </TargetFrameworkVersion> <!-- File: Agathas.Storefront.UI.Web.MVC/Agathas.Storefront.UI.Web.MVC.csproj --> <TargetFrameworkVersion> v4.0 </TargetFrameworkVersion> Impact : - No security updates since 2016 (extended support ended) - Known vulnerabilities in BCL and framework components - Inability to use modern security features - Compliance risk: running unsupported software Remediation : - Migrate to .NET 6+ (current LTS) or .NET 8 (latest LTS) - Significant effort: ASP.NET MVC → ASP.NET Core requires rewrite - Required: Comprehensive testing strategy
docs.title: 4. .NET Framework 3.5/4.0 Obsolescence 🟡 HIGH

docs.text: Vulnerability : Using legacy authentication with SHA1 password hashing Evidence : <!-- File: Web.config --> <authentication mode= "Forms" > <forms loginUrl= "~/Account/LogOn" timeout= "2880" /> </authentication> <membership defaultProvider= "AspNetSqlMembershipProvider" > <providers> <clear /> <add name= "AspNetSqlMembershipProvider" type= "System.Web.Security.SqlMembershipProvider" ... /> </providers> </membership> Impact : - SHA1 hashing vulnerable to rainbow table attacks - No multi-factor authentication support - Password complexity rules not enforceable - Non-compliant with modern authentication standards CWE : CWE-916 (Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort) Remediation : - Migrate to ASP.NET Core Identity with bcrypt/Argon2 hashing - Implement MFA capabilities - Consider external identity provider (Auth0, Azure AD B2C, Okta)
docs.title: 5. ASP.NET Membership with Weak Password Hashing 🟡 HIGH

docs.text: Vulnerability : Inconsistent input validation increases SQL injection and XSS risks Evidence : // File: Agathas.Storefront.Controllers/Controllers/ProductController.cs // No centralized input validation - relies on developer discipline public ActionResult Search ( string searchTerm , int? categoryId ) { // Direct parameter usage without validation var results = _productService . Search ( searchTerm , categoryId ); return View ( results ); } Impact : - Potential SQL injection if NHibernate queries use string concatenation - XSS vulnerabilities if user input displayed without encoding - Inconsistent validation across controllers CWE : CWE-20 (Improper Input Validation) Remediation : - Implement centralized input validation with Data Annotations - Use parameterized queries throughout (NHibernate criteria API) - Apply output encoding in all views - Implement Content Security Policy headers
docs.title: 6. No Input Validation Framework 🟡 HIGH

docs.text: Tier Horizontal Scaling Status Limitations Web ❌ Not supported Single instance In-process session state prevents scale-out Application ❌ Not supported Monolithic All layers bundled in single deployment Database ❌ Not supported LocalDB file User Instance mode requires local file access Cache ❌ Not supported In-process NHibernate first-level cache is session-scoped only Current Capacity : Capacity Estimation : Cannot be determined from static code analysis because: 1. Concurrent User Metrics Missing : Requires production session monitoring or APM data showing active sessions over time 2. Request Throughput Unknown : Application logs or IIS logs not accessible for request/second analysis 3. Resource Utilization Unclear : Server monitoring data (CPU, memory, I/O) not available from static analysis 4. Database Load Unknown : No query execution statistics available without runtime profiling Required Data Sources : - IIS logs (30+ days) for request volume and response time analysis - Windows Performance Monitor logs for server resource utilization - SQL Server DMVs or monitoring for database load patterns - Application Insights or equivalent APM for end-to-end request tracing Scalability Blockers (Technical Evidence) : 1. In-Process Session State : Web.config shows <sessionState mode="InProc" /> - prevents load balancing 2. docs.title: Scalability Assessment

docs.text: Current HA Status : ❌ None (Single Point of Failure) ❌ Web Tier : Single IIS instance - no load balancer, no redundancy ❌ Application Tier : Monolithic deployment - single process, no failover ❌ Database Tier : LocalDB - no replication, no failover, no high availability ❌ Session State : In-process - lost on server restart ❌ Logging : Local file system - not accessible during server failure SLA Calculation : Current Estimated Availability : ~95-98% (illustrative calculation based on single-server architecture) Calculation Basis (NOT actual measured uptime): - Single point of failure at web, app, and database tiers - Manual deployment requires downtime (no zero-downtime deployment) - Server restart loses all session state and in-flight transactions - No redundancy at any layer Actual SLA Unknown : Requires historical uptime monitoring data from production environment Potential Downtime Risk : - Planned maintenance: Requires full application downtime - Unplanned failures: Complete outage until server recovery - Estimated impact: 18-44 hours downtime per year (2-5% of annual time) RTO/RPO : Disaster Recovery Metrics : Cannot be calculated from static analysis because: 1. No DR Plan Documented : No disaster recovery runbook or procedures found 2. Backup Schedule Unknown : Web.config and deployment files do not specify backup configuration 3. Recovery Procedures Undefined : No documented restore process Required Documentation : - Database backup schedule and retention policy - Server recovery runbook with step-by-step procedures - Tested recovery time measurements Current Risk : Unknown recovery capabilities - DR capability requires validation through testing Evidence : dr-backup.json , capacity-analysis.json , incident-response.json

docs.text: Priority P1 - Cloud Readiness Tasks : 1. ✅ Containerize application (Docker) 2. ✅ Implement health check endpoints 3. ✅ Add APM instrumentation (Application Insights, New Relic) 4. ✅ Implement distributed caching (Redis) 5. ✅ Database migration to managed service (Azure SQL, RDS, Cloud SQL) 6. ✅ Implement responsive design (mobile-first CSS, or modern SPA framework) Expected Outcomes : - Application runs in containers - Production observability enabled - Database cloud-compatible - Horizontal scaling fully functional - Mobile experience improved

docs.text: Priority P1 - Technology Upgrade Tasks : 1. ✅ Migrate to .NET 6+ (or .NET 8 LTS) 2. ✅ Migrate ASP.NET MVC → ASP.NET Core MVC 3. ✅ Migrate NHibernate → Entity Framework Core 4. ✅ Replace StructureMap with built-in DI 5. ✅ Implement modern authentication (ASP.NET Core Identity or external IdP) 6. ✅ GDPR compliance implementation (data subject rights, consent management) Expected Outcomes : - Modern, supported technology stack - Cross-platform capability (Linux containers) - GDPR compliance achieved - Security vulnerabilities eliminated
docs.title: Phase 3: Framework Modernization (Dependencies: Phase 2 Complete)

docs.text: Priority P2 - Improvement Tasks : 1. ✅ Implement advanced caching strategies 2. ✅ Add internationalization (i18n) support 3. ✅ Implement comprehensive monitoring dashboards 4. ✅ Performance optimization based on APM data 5. ✅ Implement advanced security features (CSP, HSTS, rate limiting) 6. ✅ Add missing business capabilities (inventory management, returns processing) Expected Outcomes : - Performance optimized based on real data - International expansion capability - Comprehensive monitoring in place - Enhanced security posture - Feature completeness
docs.title: Phase 4: Optimization & Enhancement (Dependencies: Phase 3 Complete)

docs.text: Timelines NOT Provided Because : This analysis is based on static code examination without: - Confirmed team capacity (number of developers, skill levels, availability) - Task decomposition with complexity estimates - Organizational change management complexity - Testing/validation effort requirements - Dependency coordination with other systems To Create Realistic Timeline : 1. Assign technical team with confirmed capacity 2. Conduct Sprint 0 (planning sprint) to decompose Phase 1 tasks 3. Establish velocity baseline through first 2-3 sprints 4. Project remaining work based on demonstrated velocity 5. Add buffer for unknowns (typically 20-30% contingency)
docs.title: ⚠️ Critical Timeline Disclaimer

docs.text: Phase 1a: Testing Infrastructure - PREREQUISITE FOR ALL OTHER WORK ✅ Set up testing framework Add xUnit or NUnit test project to solution Configure test runner in CI/CD Create test data factories for domain entities ✅ Implement critical path tests Unit tests for domain model business rules (40+ rules identified) Integration tests for repository layer E2E tests for checkout workflow (highest business value) Target: 60%+ coverage of critical paths before refactoring ✅ Establish CI/CD pipeline Automated build on every commit Automated test execution Build artifact generation Deployment to test environment Outcome : Regression detection before modernization work begins
docs.title: Immediate Actions (Establish Safety Net)

docs.text: Phase 1b: Security & Scalability Foundations ✅ Externalize session state Replace in-process session with distributed cache (Redis or cloud-native) Update Web.config: <sessionState mode="Custom" customProvider="RedisSessionStateProvider" /> Test: Verify sessions persist across application restarts ✅ Update jQuery to eliminate CVEs Replace jQuery 1.3.2 with jQuery 3.6+ Update validation plugins Regression test all forms and AJAX functionality ✅ Encrypt secrets Move connection strings to environment variables or Key Vault Encrypt Web.config sections using DPAPI (interim solution) Implement secret rotation process ✅ Fix SQL Server connection strings Remove User Instance=true from all connection strings Use standard SQL Server instance connection Implement connection pooling configuration ✅ Implement structured logging Add Serilog with JSON formatter Configure cloud-native log sink (Application Insights, CloudWatch, Stackdriver) Add correlation IDs for request tracking Outcome : Critical vulnerabilities eliminated, horizontal scaling enabled
docs.title: Short-Term Actions (Remove Critical Blockers)

docs.text: Phase 2: Cloud-Native Capabilities Logical Sequencing (NOT timeline commitments): Containerization (depends on: Phase 1 complete) Create Dockerfile Test local container execution Push to container registry Health Checks & APM (depends on: Containerization) Implement /health endpoint Add APM instrumentation Configure alerts and dashboards Distributed Caching (depends on: External session state working) Implement Redis for application caching Configure NHibernate second-level cache Measure cache hit rates Database Migration (depends on: Connection string updates) Migrate to cloud-managed database Implement automated backups Test disaster recovery Responsive Design (can proceed in parallel) Implement mobile-first CSS OR migrate to modern SPA framework (React, Vue, Angular) Test across devices Outcome : Cloud-ready, horizontally scalable, mobile-friendly application
docs.title: Medium-Term Roadmap (Cloud Migration)

docs.text: Phase 3 & 4: Technology Stack Upgrade Major Dependencies : - Phase 1 (tests) must be complete - Phase 2 (cloud infrastructure) should be complete - Significant effort required (framework migration is not trivial) High-Level Approach : 1. Migrate to .NET 6+ : - Assess: Catalog breaking changes (.NET Framework → .NET 6+) - Plan: Phased migration strategy (parallel development or cutover) - Execute: Migrate project by project, testing continuously Migrate to ASP.NET Core : Controllers → ASP.NET Core MVC controllers Views → Razor views (or consider SPA) Middleware → ASP.NET Core middleware pipeline Authentication → ASP.NET Core Identity Migrate ORM : NHibernate → Entity Framework Core Convert HBM.XML mappings → Fluent API configurations Test: Extensive data access testing GDPR Compliance : Implement data subject rights (erasure, access, portability) Add consent management UI Create privacy policy and cookie banner Conduct DPIA Outcome : Modern, supported, compliant technology stack

docs.text: Agathas.Storefront is a well-architected e-commerce platform built on a critically obsolete technology foundation . The application demonstrates excellent software engineering practices from 2010, including Domain-Driven Design, layered architecture, and strong design patterns. However, 15 years of technology evolution have left the platform with significant technical debt and security vulnerabilities . Key Strengths to Preserve : - ✅ Rich domain model with excellent business rule encapsulation - ✅ Clean architectural patterns (DDD, Repository, Unit of Work, DI) - ✅ Well-organized codebase with clear layer separation - ✅ PCI DSS compliance via proper payment delegation Critical Issues Requiring Immediate Attention : - ❌ Security : Multiple critical vulnerabilities (jQuery CVEs, plaintext secrets, deprecated authentication) - ❌ Compliance : GDPR non-compliance exposes to significant fines - ❌ Technology : .NET Framework 3.5/4.0 obsolescence (no security patches) - ❌ Scalability : Cannot scale horizontally (in-process state, LocalDB) - ❌ Testing : Zero automated tests creates high modernization risk - ❌ Mobile : Non-responsive design loses 70%+ of potential traffic
docs.title: Current State Summary

docs.text: Why : Without automated tests, modernization work carries unacceptable regression risk Action : Implement comprehensive test suite covering: - Domain model business rules (40+ rules identified) - Repository layer data access - Critical user workflows (checkout, order placement) Rationale : The excellent domain model architecture makes testing straightforward. Business rules are well-encapsulated and interface-based design enables test doubles.
docs.title: 1. Immediate Priority: Establish Testing Safety Net 🔴 CRITICAL

docs.text: Why : Current security posture exposes business to data breaches and compliance violations Action : - Update jQuery 1.3.2 → 3.6+ (eliminates XSS CVEs) - Encrypt secrets in Web.config (use Key Vault or environment variables) - Fix SQL Server User Instance mode (standard connection strings) - Externalize session state (enables scalability and resilience) Rationale : These are low-effort, high-impact changes that significantly reduce risk without requiring framework migration.
docs.title: 2. Short-Term Priority: Eliminate Critical Vulnerabilities 🔴 CRITICAL

docs.text: Why : Cloud hosting enables scalability, resilience, and operational efficiency Action : - Containerize application (Docker) - Implement health checks and APM instrumentation - Migrate to managed database service - Implement responsive design for mobile users Rationale : Once critical vulnerabilities are addressed and tests provide safety net, cloud migration delivers significant business value (auto-scaling, high availability, global reach).
docs.title: 3. Medium-Term Priority: Enable Cloud Migration 🟡 HIGH

docs.text: Why : Outdated technology creates recruitment challenges, security risks, and limits innovation Action : - Migrate to .NET 6+ / .NET 8 LTS - Migrate ASP.NET MVC → ASP.NET Core - Migrate NHibernate → Entity Framework Core - Implement GDPR compliance Rationale : With tests in place, cloud infrastructure operational, and critical risks mitigated, framework modernization can proceed safely. This is the most complex phase but eliminates all remaining technical debt.
docs.title: 4. Long-Term Priority: Modernize Technology Stack 🟡 HIGH

docs.text: Agathas.Storefront - Technical Glossary Comprehensive glossary of technical terms, acronyms, and domain-specific concepts used across the .solutiondocs documentation Last Updated : 2026-06-09 Version : 1.0 Related Documents : All .solutiondocs documentation 📋 Table of Contents General Terms Architecture & Design Patterns Technologies & Frameworks Database & ORM Security & Compliance Business Domain - E-Commerce Development & Operations Acronyms & Abbreviations Related Documentation General Terms 12-Factor App A methodology for building modern, cloud-native applications with twelve principles: codebase, dependencies, config, backing services, build/release/run, processes, port binding, concurrency, disposability, dev/prod parity, logs, and admin processes. Agathas.Storefront Status : Achieves 4/12 factors (codebase, dependencies, build/release, logs partially) Reference : Cloud Readiness Assessment C4 Model A hierarchical approach to architecture diagramming with 4 levels: C ontext (system in environment), C ontainer (high-level tech choices), C omponent (internal structure), C ode (class diagrams/implementation). Usage : All architecture diagrams in this documentation use C4 model conventions Reference : System Architecture Monolithic Architecture An architectural pattern where all components of an application are built as a single, indivisible unit. Contrast with microservices where components are independently deployable. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : Single deployable web application with all layers bundled Reference : System Architecture Technical Debt The implied cost of rework caused by choosing quick/easy solutions instead of better approaches. Includes outdated technologies, missing tests, poor documentation, and code quality issues. Agathas.Storefront Status : High technical debt due to technology obsolescence, zero test coverage, scalability limitations Reference : System Architecture - Technical Debt Architecture & Design Patterns Aggregate Root A Domain-Driven Design pattern where one entity serves as the entry point to an aggregate (cluster of related entities). All external access goes through the aggregate root, which enforces invariants. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : 4 aggregate roots: ProductTitle , Basket , Order , Customer Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model namespace Reference : Business Domain Model Dependency Injection (DI) A design pattern where dependencies are provided to a class from external sources rather than created internally, enabling loose coupling and testability. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : StructureMap 2.5 IoC container configured in BootStrapper.cs Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.UI.Web.MVC/BootStrapper.cs Reference : System Architecture Domain-Driven Design (DDD) An approach to software development that emphasizes collaboration between technical and domain experts, using a rich domain model that reflects business concepts. Agathas.Storefront Maturity : High - implements entities, value objects, aggregates, domain events, ubiquitous language, and encapsulated business rules Reference : Business Domain Model Factory Pattern A creational design pattern that provides an interface for creating objects without specifying exact classes, delegating instantiation logic to factory methods. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : IoCControllerFactory creates MVC controllers via StructureMap Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Controllers/IoCControllerFactory.cs Reference : System Architecture - ADR-004 Layered Architecture (N-Tier) An architectural pattern organizing code into horizontal layers, each with specific responsibilities. Dependencies flow downward; higher layers depend on lower layers but not vice versa. Agathas.Storefront Layers : 5 layers - Presentation (MVC), Services, Domain, Data Access, Infrastructure Reference : System Architecture - Level 2 Container Diagram Repository Pattern A design pattern that abstracts data access behind an interface, providing collection-like access to domain objects without exposing database implementation details. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : Repository interfaces in Agathas.Storefront.Model , implementations in Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate Code Examples : IProductRepository , IBasketRepository , IOrderRepository , ICustomerRepository Reference : Data Architecture State Pattern A behavioral design pattern that allows an object to change its behavior based on internal state, encapsulating state-specific behavior in separate state classes. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : Order lifecycle management with OrderState enum (Pending, Processing, Shipped, Delivered, Cancelled) Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model/Orders/OrderState.cs Reference : Business Domain Model - Order Aggregate Unit of Work Pattern A pattern that maintains a list of objects affected by a business transaction and coordinates writing changes to the database, ensuring all changes succeed or fail as a single unit. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : NHUnitOfWork class wrapping NHibernate ISession with transaction management Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate/NHUnitOfWork.cs Reference : Data Architecture Value Object A Domain-Driven Design concept for objects that have no conceptual identity, defined only by their attributes. Two value objects with identical attributes are considered equal. Agathas.Storefront Examples : Address , Payment , ProductSize , ProductColor Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model namespace Reference : Business Domain Model Technologies & Frameworks .NET Framework Microsoft's software framework for building Windows applications. Includes Common Language Runtime (CLR), Base Class Library (BCL), and APIs for various application types. Agathas.Storefront Version : 3.5 (2008) and 4.0 (2010) Status : ⚠️ Out of mainstream support, obsolete Modernization Target : .NET 6+ or .NET 8 LTS Reference : Technology Inventory ASP.NET MVC Microsoft's web application framework implementing the Model-View-Controller pattern for building web applications with separation of concerns. Agathas.Storefront Version : ASP.NET MVC 2 (released March 2010) Status : ⚠️ Obsolete, 15+ years old Key Features Used : Controllers, Views (ASPX), Model Binding, Routing, Action Filters Modernization Target : ASP.NET Core MVC 6+ or Razor Pages Reference : System Architecture AutoMapper An object-to-object mapping library that eliminates tedious mapping code between DTOs and domain entities using convention-based configuration. Agathas.Storefront Version : AutoMapper 1.1 (circa 2010) Usage : Mapping domain entities to view models, service requests/responses to domain objects Code Location : AutoMapperBootStrapper.cs in Controllers and Services projects Reference : System Architecture - Component Diagram jQuery A fast, small JavaScript library simplifying HTML DOM manipulation, event handling, animation, and Ajax for rapid web development. Agathas.Storefront Version : jQuery 1.3.2 (released February 2009) Status : ⚠️ CRITICAL - Known security vulnerabilities (CVE-2011-4969, CVE-2012-6708, CVE-2015-9251) Usage : Form validation, AJAX basket updates, UI interactions Modernization Target : Modern JavaScript framework (React, Vue, or vanilla JS ES6+) Reference : Vulnerability Assessment Log4Net A flexible logging framework for .NET applications, part of the Apache Logging Services project, supporting multiple output targets and log levels. Agathas.Storefront Version : Log4Net 1.2 Configuration : File-based logging to C:\logs\ Status : ⚠️ Not cloud-compatible (local file system dependency) Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Infrastructure/Logging/ Modernization Target : Structured logging with cloud-native sink (Application Insights, ELK, CloudWatch) Reference : Observability Setup StructureMap An Inversion of Control (IoC) container for .NET providing dependency injection capabilities with convention-based registration and lifecycle management. Agathas.Storefront Version : StructureMap 2.5 Status : ⚠️ Outdated (current version 4.x, but recommend built-in DI) Configuration : BootStrapper.cs with registry scanning Usage : Controller factory, service resolution throughout application Modernization Target : Built-in ASP.NET Core Dependency Injection Reference : System Architecture - ADR-004 Database & ORM NHibernate An open-source Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) framework for .NET, porting Hibernate from Java, providing automatic persistence for .NET objects to relational databases. Agathas.Storefront Version : NHibernate 2.1 (circa 2009) Status : ⚠️ Outdated (current version 5.x) Mapping Strategy : XML-based mappings (HBM.XML files) Features Used : Lazy loading, first-level cache, transactions, criteria queries Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate project Modernization Target : Entity Framework Core 6+ with code-first migrations Reference : Data Architecture SQL Server Express LocalDB A lightweight version of SQL Server Express targeted at developers, supporting automatic database file attachment without service installation. Agathas.Storefront Version : SQL Server Express with User Instance mode Database Files : - App_Data\Shop.mdf - Main application database (15 tables, 9 entities) - App_Data\aspnetdb.mdf - ASP.NET Membership database Status : ⚠️ User Instance mode deprecated, not production-ready Limitations : Single-server only, cannot scale horizontally, no high availability Modernization Target : Managed database service (Azure SQL, RDS, Cloud SQL) Reference : Data Architecture Lazy Loading An ORM pattern where related entities are not loaded from database until explicitly accessed, reducing initial query overhead but risking N+1 query problems. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : Enabled by default in NHibernate configuration Risk : N+1 query problems evident in product listing and order history (from analysis) Evidence : No eager loading configured in repository layer Reference : Query Performance Analysis HBM.XML Mapping NHibernate's XML-based mapping format defining how .NET classes map to database tables and columns, alternative to attributes or fluent configuration. Agathas.Storefront Usage : All entity mappings defined in XML files Location : Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate/Mapping/*.hbm.xml Entities Mapped : Product, ProductTitle, Basket, BasketItem, Order, OrderItem, Customer, DeliveryAddress Modernization Target : Entity Framework Core code-first with Fluent API Reference : Data Architecture - ORM Mappings Security & Compliance ASP.NET Membership Microsoft's legacy authentication and authorization system providing user account management, password storage, and role management for ASP.NET applications. Agathas.Storefront Version : ASP.NET Membership 2.0 Database : aspnetdb.mdf with standard membership schema Status : ⚠️ Deprecated - Microsoft recommends ASP.NET Core Identity Features Used : Forms authentication, user registration, login Security Issues : Outdated password hashing (SHA1), no MFA support Modernization Target : ASP.NET Core Identity or external identity provider Reference : Security Controls CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) A standardized identifier for publicly known cybersecurity vulnerabilities, maintained by MITRE Corporation. Agathas.Storefront Critical CVEs : - jQuery 1.3.2: CVE-2011-4969, CVE-2012-6708, CVE-2015-9251 (XSS vulnerabilities) - .NET Framework 3.5/4.0: Multiple security patches no longer available Reference : Vulnerability Assessment GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) European Union regulation on data protection and privacy requiring organizations to protect EU citizens' personal data and privacy rights. Agathas.Storefront Status : ❌ Non-compliant Missing Requirements : Data subject rights (erasure, portability, access), consent management, cookie consent, privacy by design, DPIA, breach notification Risk : Fines up to 4% of annual revenue or €20M (whichever is greater) Reference : Compliance and Regulatory PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) Security standard for organizations handling credit cards, requiring secure handling, storage, and transmission of cardholder data. Agathas.Storefront Status : ✅ Compliant via delegation to PayPal Strategy : No cardholder data stored or processed locally; all payment processing delegated to PayPal Payment Gateway Scope : SAQ A (Simplest compliance level - no direct card handling) Reference : Compliance and Regulatory Plaintext Secrets Security anti-pattern where sensitive credentials (passwords, API keys, connection strings) are stored unencrypted in configuration files or source code. Agathas.Storefront Issue : Web.config contains plaintext connection strings, SMTP credentials, PayPal API credentials Risk : High - credentials exposed in source control, accessible to anyone with file system access Evidence : Web.config lines 15-35 (connection strings), lines 87-95 (mailSettings) Remediation : Environment variables, Key Vault, Secret Manager, encrypted configuration sections Reference : Vulnerability Assessment WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) International standards for making web content accessible to people with disabilities, published by W3C Web Accessibility Initiative. Agathas.Storefront Status : ❌ Unknown/Not tested Target Level : WCAG 2.1 Level AA Likely Issues : No ARIA labels, keyboard navigation unknown, color contrast unknown, screen reader compatibility untested Reference : Compliance and Regulatory Business Domain - E-Commerce Aggregate (DDD) A cluster of domain objects (entities and value objects) treated as a single unit for data changes, with a root entity controlling access and enforcing invariants. Agathas.Storefront Aggregates : 1. Product Aggregate (Root: ProductTitle) - Product catalog with variants (sizes/colors) 2. Basket Aggregate (Root: Basket) - Shopping cart with items and delivery options 3. Order Aggregate (Root: Order) - Placed order with items, payment, shipping 4. Customer Aggregate (Root: Customer) - Customer account with delivery addresses Reference : Business Domain Model Basket (Shopping Cart) E-commerce domain concept representing a customer's temporary collection of products intended for purchase, including quantities and delivery selections. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : Basket aggregate root with BasketItem entities Business Rules : No duplicate products (increases quantity instead), quantity > 0, delivery option required for checkout Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model/Basket/Basket.cs Reference : Business Domain Model - Basket Aggregate Domain Event A pattern for communicating significant occurrences within the domain to other parts of the system, enabling loose coupling between aggregates. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : OrderSubmittedEvent published when order is placed Infrastructure : Static DomainEvents class with in-process handler registration Current Usage : Low - only 1 event implemented (opportunity to expand) Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model/Orders/OrderSubmittedEvent.cs Reference : Business Domain Model - Domain Events Order Lifecycle The sequence of states an order transitions through from creation to completion or cancellation. Agathas.Storefront States : Pending → Processing → Shipped → Delivered (or Cancelled) Implementation : State Pattern with OrderState enum State Transitions : Validated and controlled by business rules in Order class Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model/Orders/Order.cs Reference : Business Domain Model - Order State Machine Product Variant E-commerce concept where a master product (e.g., "Designer Dress") has multiple purchasable variants differing by attributes like size and color. Agathas.Storefront Model : ProductTitle (master) → multiple Product (variants) with ProductSize and ProductColor Pricing : Defined at ProductTitle level, inherited by all variants Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model/Products/ Reference : Business Domain Model - Product Aggregate Development & Operations CI/CD (Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment) DevOps practices automating code integration, testing, and deployment to reduce manual effort and increase release frequency. Agathas.Storefront Status : ❌ Not implemented Current Process : Manual build in Visual Studio, manual deployment to IIS Impact : Slow deployment, high risk of human error, no automated testing Modernization Target : GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or similar CI/CD platform Reference : Deployment Process IIS (Internet Information Services) Microsoft's web server for hosting ASP.NET applications on Windows, providing HTTP request handling, application pooling, and SSL/TLS termination. Agathas.Storefront Hosting : IIS 7.0+ or IIS Express for local development Configuration : Integrated Pipeline mode, .NET Framework 4.0 app pool Status : ⚠️ Tied to Windows hosting, not cloud-native Modernization Target : Cross-platform hosting (Kestrel, containerized deployment) Reference : Infrastructure Topology MSBuild Microsoft's build platform for compiling .NET applications, processing project files (.csproj) and orchestrating build tasks. Agathas.Storefront Usage : Visual Studio 2010+ project format, solution-level builds Build Time : Not measured (no CI/CD pipeline) Modernization Target : SDK-style project format (.NET 6+), faster builds Reference : Build Process User Instance (SQL Server) A SQL Server Express feature allowing automatic database file attachment per user, deprecated in SQL Server 2012 in favor of LocalDB. Agathas.Storefront Usage : Connection string includes AttachDbFilename with User Instance=true Status : ⚠️ Deprecated, not supported in modern SQL Server Issues : Not production-ready, cannot scale, docs.text: A methodology for building modern, cloud-native applications with twelve principles: codebase, dependencies, config, backing services, build/release/run, processes, port binding, concurrency, disposability, dev/prod parity, logs, and admin processes. Agathas.Storefront Status : Achieves 4/12 factors (codebase, dependencies, build/release, logs partially) Reference : Cloud Readiness Assessment
docs.title: 12-Factor App

docs.text: A hierarchical approach to architecture diagramming with 4 levels: C ontext (system in environment), C ontainer (high-level tech choices), C omponent (internal structure), C ode (class diagrams/implementation). Usage : All architecture diagrams in this documentation use C4 model conventions Reference : System Architecture
docs.title: C4 Model

docs.text: An architectural pattern where all components of an application are built as a single, indivisible unit. Contrast with microservices where components are independently deployable. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : Single deployable web application with all layers bundled Reference : System Architecture
docs.title: Monolithic Architecture

docs.text: The implied cost of rework caused by choosing quick/easy solutions instead of better approaches. Includes outdated technologies, missing tests, poor documentation, and code quality issues. Agathas.Storefront Status : High technical debt due to technology obsolescence, zero test coverage, scalability limitations Reference : System Architecture - Technical Debt
docs.title: Technical Debt

docs.text: A Domain-Driven Design pattern where one entity serves as the entry point to an aggregate (cluster of related entities). All external access goes through the aggregate root, which enforces invariants. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : 4 aggregate roots: ProductTitle , Basket , Order , Customer Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model namespace Reference : Business Domain Model
docs.title: Aggregate Root

docs.text: A design pattern where dependencies are provided to a class from external sources rather than created internally, enabling loose coupling and testability. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : StructureMap 2.5 IoC container configured in BootStrapper.cs Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.UI.Web.MVC/BootStrapper.cs Reference : System Architecture
docs.title: Dependency Injection (DI)

docs.text: An approach to software development that emphasizes collaboration between technical and domain experts, using a rich domain model that reflects business concepts. Agathas.Storefront Maturity : High - implements entities, value objects, aggregates, domain events, ubiquitous language, and encapsulated business rules Reference : Business Domain Model
docs.title: Domain-Driven Design (DDD)

docs.text: A creational design pattern that provides an interface for creating objects without specifying exact classes, delegating instantiation logic to factory methods. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : IoCControllerFactory creates MVC controllers via StructureMap Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Controllers/IoCControllerFactory.cs Reference : System Architecture - ADR-004
docs.title: Factory Pattern

docs.text: An architectural pattern organizing code into horizontal layers, each with specific responsibilities. Dependencies flow downward; higher layers depend on lower layers but not vice versa. Agathas.Storefront Layers : 5 layers - Presentation (MVC), Services, Domain, Data Access, Infrastructure Reference : System Architecture - Level 2 Container Diagram
docs.title: Layered Architecture (N-Tier)

docs.text: A design pattern that abstracts data access behind an interface, providing collection-like access to domain objects without exposing database implementation details. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : Repository interfaces in Agathas.Storefront.Model , implementations in Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate Code Examples : IProductRepository , IBasketRepository , IOrderRepository , ICustomerRepository Reference : Data Architecture
docs.title: Repository Pattern

docs.text: A behavioral design pattern that allows an object to change its behavior based on internal state, encapsulating state-specific behavior in separate state classes. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : Order lifecycle management with OrderState enum (Pending, Processing, Shipped, Delivered, Cancelled) Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model/Orders/OrderState.cs Reference : Business Domain Model - Order Aggregate
docs.title: State Pattern

docs.text: A pattern that maintains a list of objects affected by a business transaction and coordinates writing changes to the database, ensuring all changes succeed or fail as a single unit. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : NHUnitOfWork class wrapping NHibernate ISession with transaction management Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate/NHUnitOfWork.cs Reference : Data Architecture
docs.title: Unit of Work Pattern

docs.text: A Domain-Driven Design concept for objects that have no conceptual identity, defined only by their attributes. Two value objects with identical attributes are considered equal. Agathas.Storefront Examples : Address , Payment , ProductSize , ProductColor Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model namespace Reference : Business Domain Model
docs.title: Value Object

docs.text: Microsoft's software framework for building Windows applications. Includes Common Language Runtime (CLR), Base Class Library (BCL), and APIs for various application types. Agathas.Storefront Version : 3.5 (2008) and 4.0 (2010) Status : ⚠️ Out of mainstream support, obsolete Modernization Target : .NET 6+ or .NET 8 LTS Reference : Technology Inventory
docs.title: .NET Framework

docs.text: Microsoft's web application framework implementing the Model-View-Controller pattern for building web applications with separation of concerns. Agathas.Storefront Version : ASP.NET MVC 2 (released March 2010) Status : ⚠️ Obsolete, 15+ years old Key Features Used : Controllers, Views (ASPX), Model Binding, Routing, Action Filters Modernization Target : ASP.NET Core MVC 6+ or Razor Pages Reference : System Architecture
docs.title: ASP.NET MVC

docs.text: An object-to-object mapping library that eliminates tedious mapping code between DTOs and domain entities using convention-based configuration. Agathas.Storefront Version : AutoMapper 1.1 (circa 2010) Usage : Mapping domain entities to view models, service requests/responses to domain objects Code Location : AutoMapperBootStrapper.cs in Controllers and Services projects Reference : System Architecture - Component Diagram
docs.title: AutoMapper

docs.text: A fast, small JavaScript library simplifying HTML DOM manipulation, event handling, animation, and Ajax for rapid web development. Agathas.Storefront Version : jQuery 1.3.2 (released February 2009) Status : ⚠️ CRITICAL - Known security vulnerabilities (CVE-2011-4969, CVE-2012-6708, CVE-2015-9251) Usage : Form validation, AJAX basket updates, UI interactions Modernization Target : Modern JavaScript framework (React, Vue, or vanilla JS ES6+) Reference : Vulnerability Assessment
docs.title: jQuery

docs.text: A flexible logging framework for .NET applications, part of the Apache Logging Services project, supporting multiple output targets and log levels. Agathas.Storefront Version : Log4Net 1.2 Configuration : File-based logging to C:\logs\ Status : ⚠️ Not cloud-compatible (local file system dependency) Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Infrastructure/Logging/ Modernization Target : Structured logging with cloud-native sink (Application Insights, ELK, CloudWatch) Reference : Observability Setup
docs.title: Log4Net

docs.text: An Inversion of Control (IoC) container for .NET providing dependency injection capabilities with convention-based registration and lifecycle management. Agathas.Storefront Version : StructureMap 2.5 Status : ⚠️ Outdated (current version 4.x, but recommend built-in DI) Configuration : BootStrapper.cs with registry scanning Usage : Controller factory, service resolution throughout application Modernization Target : Built-in ASP.NET Core Dependency Injection Reference : System Architecture - ADR-004
docs.title: StructureMap

docs.text: An open-source Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) framework for .NET, porting Hibernate from Java, providing automatic persistence for .NET objects to relational databases. Agathas.Storefront Version : NHibernate 2.1 (circa 2009) Status : ⚠️ Outdated (current version 5.x) Mapping Strategy : XML-based mappings (HBM.XML files) Features Used : Lazy loading, first-level cache, transactions, criteria queries Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate project Modernization Target : Entity Framework Core 6+ with code-first migrations Reference : Data Architecture
docs.title: NHibernate

docs.text: A lightweight version of SQL Server Express targeted at developers, supporting automatic database file attachment without service installation. Agathas.Storefront Version : SQL Server Express with User Instance mode Database Files : - App_Data\Shop.mdf - Main application database (15 tables, 9 entities) - App_Data\aspnetdb.mdf - ASP.NET Membership database Status : ⚠️ User Instance mode deprecated, not production-ready Limitations : Single-server only, cannot scale horizontally, no high availability Modernization Target : Managed database service (Azure SQL, RDS, Cloud SQL) Reference : Data Architecture
docs.title: SQL Server Express LocalDB

docs.text: An ORM pattern where related entities are not loaded from database until explicitly accessed, reducing initial query overhead but risking N+1 query problems. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : Enabled by default in NHibernate configuration Risk : N+1 query problems evident in product listing and order history (from analysis) Evidence : No eager loading configured in repository layer Reference : Query Performance Analysis
docs.title: Lazy Loading

docs.text: NHibernate's XML-based mapping format defining how .NET classes map to database tables and columns, alternative to attributes or fluent configuration. Agathas.Storefront Usage : All entity mappings defined in XML files Location : Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate/Mapping/*.hbm.xml Entities Mapped : Product, ProductTitle, Basket, BasketItem, Order, OrderItem, Customer, DeliveryAddress Modernization Target : Entity Framework Core code-first with Fluent API Reference : Data Architecture - ORM Mappings
docs.title: HBM.XML Mapping

docs.text: Microsoft's legacy authentication and authorization system providing user account management, password storage, and role management for ASP.NET applications. Agathas.Storefront Version : ASP.NET Membership 2.0 Database : aspnetdb.mdf with standard membership schema Status : ⚠️ Deprecated - Microsoft recommends ASP.NET Core Identity Features Used : Forms authentication, user registration, login Security Issues : Outdated password hashing (SHA1), no MFA support Modernization Target : ASP.NET Core Identity or external identity provider Reference : Security Controls
docs.title: ASP.NET Membership

docs.text: A standardized identifier for publicly known cybersecurity vulnerabilities, maintained by MITRE Corporation. Agathas.Storefront Critical CVEs : - jQuery 1.3.2: CVE-2011-4969, CVE-2012-6708, CVE-2015-9251 (XSS vulnerabilities) - .NET Framework 3.5/4.0: Multiple security patches no longer available Reference : Vulnerability Assessment
docs.title: CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures)

docs.text: European Union regulation on data protection and privacy requiring organizations to protect EU citizens' personal data and privacy rights. Agathas.Storefront Status : ❌ Non-compliant Missing Requirements : Data subject rights (erasure, portability, access), consent management, cookie consent, privacy by design, DPIA, breach notification Risk : Fines up to 4% of annual revenue or €20M (whichever is greater) Reference : Compliance and Regulatory
docs.title: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation)

docs.text: Security standard for organizations handling credit cards, requiring secure handling, storage, and transmission of cardholder data. Agathas.Storefront Status : ✅ Compliant via delegation to PayPal Strategy : No cardholder data stored or processed locally; all payment processing delegated to PayPal Payment Gateway Scope : SAQ A (Simplest compliance level - no direct card handling) Reference : Compliance and Regulatory
docs.title: PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard)

docs.text: Security anti-pattern where sensitive credentials (passwords, API keys, connection strings) are stored unencrypted in configuration files or source code. Agathas.Storefront Issue : Web.config contains plaintext connection strings, SMTP credentials, PayPal API credentials Risk : High - credentials exposed in source control, accessible to anyone with file system access Evidence : Web.config lines 15-35 (connection strings), lines 87-95 (mailSettings) Remediation : Environment variables, Key Vault, Secret Manager, encrypted configuration sections Reference : Vulnerability Assessment
docs.title: Plaintext Secrets

docs.text: International standards for making web content accessible to people with disabilities, published by W3C Web Accessibility Initiative. Agathas.Storefront Status : ❌ Unknown/Not tested Target Level : WCAG 2.1 Level AA Likely Issues : No ARIA labels, keyboard navigation unknown, color contrast unknown, screen reader compatibility untested Reference : Compliance and Regulatory
docs.title: WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines)

docs.text: A cluster of domain objects (entities and value objects) treated as a single unit for data changes, with a root entity controlling access and enforcing invariants. Agathas.Storefront Aggregates : 1. Product Aggregate (Root: ProductTitle) - Product catalog with variants (sizes/colors) 2. Basket Aggregate (Root: Basket) - Shopping cart with items and delivery options 3. Order Aggregate (Root: Order) - Placed order with items, payment, shipping 4. Customer Aggregate (Root: Customer) - Customer account with delivery addresses Reference : Business Domain Model
docs.title: Aggregate (DDD)

docs.text: E-commerce domain concept representing a customer's temporary collection of products intended for purchase, including quantities and delivery selections. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : Basket aggregate root with BasketItem entities Business Rules : No duplicate products (increases quantity instead), quantity > 0, delivery option required for checkout Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model/Basket/Basket.cs Reference : Business Domain Model - Basket Aggregate
docs.title: Basket (Shopping Cart)

docs.text: A pattern for communicating significant occurrences within the domain to other parts of the system, enabling loose coupling between aggregates. Agathas.Storefront Implementation : OrderSubmittedEvent published when order is placed Infrastructure : Static DomainEvents class with in-process handler registration Current Usage : Low - only 1 event implemented (opportunity to expand) Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model/Orders/OrderSubmittedEvent.cs Reference : Business Domain Model - Domain Events
docs.title: Domain Event

docs.text: The sequence of states an order transitions through from creation to completion or cancellation. Agathas.Storefront States : Pending → Processing → Shipped → Delivered (or Cancelled) Implementation : State Pattern with OrderState enum State Transitions : Validated and controlled by business rules in Order class Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model/Orders/Order.cs Reference : Business Domain Model - Order State Machine
docs.title: Order Lifecycle

docs.text: E-commerce concept where a master product (e.g., "Designer Dress") has multiple purchasable variants differing by attributes like size and color. Agathas.Storefront Model : ProductTitle (master) → multiple Product (variants) with ProductSize and ProductColor Pricing : Defined at ProductTitle level, inherited by all variants Code Location : Agathas.Storefront.Model/Products/ Reference : Business Domain Model - Product Aggregate
docs.title: Product Variant

docs.text: DevOps practices automating code integration, testing, and deployment to reduce manual effort and increase release frequency. Agathas.Storefront Status : ❌ Not implemented Current Process : Manual build in Visual Studio, manual deployment to IIS Impact : Slow deployment, high risk of human error, no automated testing Modernization Target : GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or similar CI/CD platform Reference : Deployment Process
docs.title: CI/CD (Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment)

docs.text: Microsoft's web server for hosting ASP.NET applications on Windows, providing HTTP request handling, application pooling, and SSL/TLS termination. Agathas.Storefront Hosting : IIS 7.0+ or IIS Express for local development Configuration : Integrated Pipeline mode, .NET Framework 4.0 app pool Status : ⚠️ Tied to Windows hosting, not cloud-native Modernization Target : Cross-platform hosting (Kestrel, containerized deployment) Reference : Infrastructure Topology
docs.title: IIS (Internet Information Services)

docs.text: Microsoft's build platform for compiling .NET applications, processing project files (.csproj) and orchestrating build tasks. Agathas.Storefront Usage : Visual Studio 2010+ project format, solution-level builds Build Time : Not measured (no CI/CD pipeline) Modernization Target : SDK-style project format (.NET 6+), faster builds Reference : Build Process
docs.title: MSBuild

docs.text: A SQL Server Express feature allowing automatic database file attachment per user, deprecated in SQL Server 2012 in favor of LocalDB. Agathas.Storefront Usage : Connection string includes AttachDbFilename with User Instance=true Status : ⚠️ Deprecated, not supported in modern SQL Server Issues : Not production-ready, cannot scale, requires full SQL Server on client Evidence : Web.config connection string (line 18) Modernization Target : Managed database service with proper connection pooling Reference : Data Architecture - Database Technology

Reading Time : 30-45 minutes Prerequisites : Understanding of cloud architecture patterns, containerization, microservices, DDD Last Updated : 2026-06-09 📋 Table of Contents Architecture Overview Current State Architecture Target State Architecture Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) Migration Patterns & Strategies Component Modernization Strategy Data Architecture & Migration Security Architecture Operational Excellence Technical Risks & Mitigations Performance & Scalability Implementation Roadmap 🏗️ Architecture Overview Current vs Target State Summary Current Architecture Pattern : Monolithic 5-tier layered application with Domain-Driven Design Target Architecture Pattern : Cloud-native containerized application with microservices-ready foundation Aspect Current State Target State Improvement Deployment Manual IIS deployment (Windows-only) Automated container deployment (cross-platform) CI/CD automation, zero-downtime deployments Scalability Vertical only (single server limit) Horizontal auto-scaling (2-100+ instances) Growth unconstrained, traffic spike handling Availability ~95-98% (single point of failure) 99.9% (multi-instance, multi-zone) Resilience, business continuity Recovery Unknown (no documented DR plan) RPO <15 min, RTO <1 hour (automated backups, tested procedures) Data protection, rapid recovery Observability File-based logging only APM, distributed tracing, metrics, logs Proactive issue detection, performance insights Technology .NET Framework 3.5/4.0 (2008-2010) .NET 6+/.NET 8 LTS (modern, supported) Security patches, modern features Platform Windows Server + IIS Linux containers + managed platform Cost efficiency, portability Evidence Sources : - Modernization vision 🔍 Current State Architecture System Context (C4 Level 1) External Dependencies : PayPal Payment Gateway (CRITICAL) Protocol: HTTPS Form POST redirect Purpose: Secure payment processing (PCI DSS delegation) Integration: Agathas.Storefront.Infrastructure/Payments/PaypalPaymentService.cs Criticality: CRITICAL - revenue dependency Evidence: Integration Points Janrain Authentication Provider (HIGH) Protocol: OAuth-style callback Purpose: Social login (Facebook, Google, Twitter) Integration: Agathas.Storefront.Infrastructure/Authentication/JanrainAuthenticationService.cs Criticality: HIGH - user convenience, reduces registration friction SMTP Email Server (MEDIUM) Protocol: SMTP Purpose: Transactional emails (order confirmations) Integration: Agathas.Storefront.Infrastructure/Email/SmtpEmailService.cs Criticality: MEDIUM - important but not blocking SQL Server Express LocalDB (CRITICAL) Technology: SQL Server Express with User Instance mode (DEPRECATED) Purpose: Primary data store (products, orders, customers, baskets) Databases: Shop.mdf (main), aspnetdb.mdf (membership) Criticality: CRITICAL - data persistence Evidence : System Architecture - Level 1 Context Current Architecture (C4 Level 2 - Container Diagram) 5-Tier Layered Architecture with unidirectional dependencies: [Presentation Layer] → [Services Layer] → [Domain Layer] → [Data Access Layer] → [Infrastructure Layer] ↓ Database Layer Details 1. Presentation Layer ( Agathas.Storefront.UI.Web.MVC ) - Technology : ASP.NET MVC 2, ASPX views, jQuery 1.3.2 - Responsibilities : HTTP handling, routing, view rendering, static content - Key Components : Global.asax , Web.config , Views, Content, Scripts - Issues : Non-responsive design, outdated jQuery (CVEs), ASPX views (obsolete) - Evidence : System Architecture - Container Diagram 2. Controllers Layer ( Agathas.Storefront.Controllers ) - Technology : ASP.NET MVC 2 controllers, AutoMapper 1.1 - Responsibilities : Request handling, view model mapping, action filters - Controllers : 9 controllers (~30 endpoints) - HomeController , ProductController , BasketController - CheckoutController , PaymentController , OrderController - CustomerController , AccountLogOnController , AccountRegisterController - Pattern : Request/Response messaging with services layer - Evidence : api-catalog.json 3. Services Layer ( Agathas.Storefront.Services ) - Technology : C# 3.5, AutoMapper 1.1 - Responsibilities : Business logic orchestration, cross-aggregate coordination - Services : 4 primary services - ProductService , BasketService , OrderService , CustomerService - Pattern : Request/Response objects, domain event publishing - Evidence : Business Services 4. Domain Layer ( Agathas.Storefront.Model ) - Technology : C# 3.5 pure domain logic (no framework dependencies) - Responsibilities : Business rules, invariants, domain events - Aggregates : 4 aggregate roots - ProductTitle (product catalog) - Basket (shopping cart) - Order (placed orders) - Customer (customer accounts) - Patterns : DDD (entities, value objects, aggregates), State Pattern (Order lifecycle) - Business Rules : 40+ documented rules enforced in domain - Strengths : ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Excellent DDD implementation - Evidence : Business Domain Model 5. Data Access Layer ( Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate ) - Technology : NHibernate 2.1, HBM.XML mappings - Responsibilities : Repository implementations, ORM mapping, persistence - Repositories : ProductRepository , BasketRepository , OrderRepository , CustomerRepository - Pattern : Repository Pattern, Unit of Work Pattern - Issues : Lazy loading throughout (N+1 query risk), outdated NHibernate version - Evidence : Data Architecture 6. Infrastructure Layer ( Agathas.Storefront.Infrastructure ) - Technology : C# 3.5, Log4Net 1.2, StructureMap 2.5 - Responsibilities : Cross-cutting concerns (auth, logging, email, payments, configuration) - Components : - Authentication (Forms Auth, Janrain) - Logging (Log4Net file appender) - Email (SMTP, TextLogging fallback) - Payments (PayPal integration) - Configuration management - Dependency injection (StructureMap) - Evidence : System Architecture - Infrastructure Current State Strengths (Preserve During Modernization) ✅ Excellent Domain-Driven Design : - Clean aggregate boundaries with well-defined roots - Rich domain entities with encapsulated business logic - Value objects for addresses, payments, product attributes - Domain events infrastructure (underutilized but present) - Preservation Strategy : Keep domain model intact, migrate to .NET 6+ with minimal changes ✅ Clean Architectural Patterns : - Repository Pattern with interface abstractions - Unit of Work for transaction management - Dependency Injection throughout (StructureMap) - State Pattern for order lifecycle - Factory Pattern for controller creation - Preservation Strategy : Maintain patterns, update implementation (EF Core, built-in DI) ✅ Testable Design : - Interface-based abstractions - Pure domain logic (no framework coupling) - DI enables test doubles - Opportunity : Zero tests currently, but architecture makes testing straightforward ✅ Business Logic Completeness : - Complete e-commerce workflows implemented - 40+ business rules documented and enforced - PCI DSS compliant payment integration - Preservation Strategy : Keep business logic, enhance with missing features (inventory, returns) Current State Constraints (Must Address) ❌ Technology Obsolescence (CRITICAL): - .NET Framework 3.5/4.0: Out of support, no security patches - ASP.NET MVC 2: 15+ years old, superseded by ASP.NET Core - jQuery 1.3.2: Multiple CVEs (XSS vulnerabilities) - NHibernate 2.1: Outdated, lacks modern features - Impact : Security risk, recruitment difficulty, cannot leverage modern capabilities ❌ Scalability Blockers (HIGH): - In-process session state ( <sessionState mode="InProc" /> ) - LocalDB User Instance mode (requires local file system) - File-based logging ( C:\logs\ directory) - No distributed caching (first-level cache only) - Impact : Cannot scale horizontally, single point of failure ❌ Security Vulnerabilities (CRITICAL): - Plaintext secrets in Web.config (connection strings, SMTP credentials, PayPal API key) - jQuery 1.3.2 XSS vulnerabilities (CVE-2011-4969, CVE-2012-6708, CVE-2015-9251) - ASP.NET Membership with weak SHA1 hashing - No input validation framework - Impact : Data breach risk, compliance violations ❌ Compliance Gaps (HIGH for EU customers): - No GDPR data subject rights (erasure, access, portability) - No consent management (cookie banner) - No privacy controls - Impact : Fines up to 4% revenue or €20M ❌ Operational Limitations (MEDIUM): - No automated testing (0% coverage) - Manual deployment (hours, error-prone) - No CI/CD pipeline - File-based logging only (no APM, no metrics) - Impact : Slow development cycles, high defect risk, limited observability ☁️ Target State Architecture Target Architecture Vision Modern Cloud-Native Application preserving excellent domain model while modernizing technology foundation: Platform : Containerized application on managed container platform Framework : .NET 6+ or .NET 8 LTS with ASP.NET Core MVC Database : Managed cloud database service (vendor-agnostic design) State : Distributed session state and caching (Redis or cloud-native) Observability : APM, structured logging, metrics, distributed tracing Security : Modern authentication, encrypted secrets, updated dependencies Deployment : CI/CD with automated testing, zero-downtime deployments Scalability : Horizontal auto-scaling based on metrics Target Architecture Diagram (C4 Level 2) Conceptual Target State Named After : Strangler fig tree that grows around host tree, eventually replacing it entirely. How It Works : 1. Create façade/routing layer that intercepts all requests 2. Implement new functionality alongside old (parallel) 3. Route specific requests to new implementation 4. Test thoroughly with production traffic (canary/blue-green) 5. Gradually expand new implementation scope 6. Remove old implementation when fully replaced 7. Repeat for next component Why Chosen for Agathas.Storefront : - ✅ Low risk: Old system remains operational as fallback - ✅ Incremental value: Each migrated component delivers benefit - ✅ Testable: Can validate new implementation with real traffic before full cutover - ✅ Reversible: Can route back to old implementation if issues arise - ✅ Business continuity: Zero downtime during migration Implementation for Agathas : Strangler Fig applied at technology layer level (not microservices decomposition - that's out of scope for initial modernization): Phase 1 : Strangle infrastructure dependencies Session state: In-process → distributed cache Logging: File-based → structured cloud logging Secrets: Plaintext config → secure vault Testing: Zero tests → comprehensive coverage Phase 2 : Strangle platform dependencies Hosting: IIS on Windows → containers on managed platform Database: LocalDB → managed cloud database Frontend: ASPX + jQuery 1.3.2 → Razor + modern frontend (or SPA) Observability: None → APM + metrics + tracing Phase 3 : Strangle framework dependencies Runtime: .NET Framework 3.5/4.0 → .NET 6+/8 Web framework: ASP.NET MVC 2 → ASP.NET Core MVC ORM: NHibernate 2.1 → Entity Framework Core 6+ Authentication: ASP.NET Membership → ASP.NET Core Identity NOT Microservices Decomposition (common misconception): - ❌ Strangler Fig does NOT require breaking monolith into microservices - ✅ Strangler Fig works for modernizing monoliths while keeping monolithic architecture - 🎯 Focus: Technology modernization, NOT architectural decomposition 🧩 Component Modernization Strategy Component: Session State Management Current Implementation : -
