Comprehensive Testing : 60%+ test coverage before migration (Phase 1) 2. Incremental Migration : Migrate project by project, test after each 3. API Compatibility Analysis : Use .NET Upgrade Assistant to identify breaking changes 4. Compatibility Shims : Use compatibility packages where possible 5. Team Training : Ensure team familiar with .NET 6+ differences before migration Validation : All automated tests passing, manual regression testing of critical paths Risk 3: Performance Degradation Risk : Cloud deployment or framework changes result in performance degradation Probability : MEDIUM (common in cloud migrations) Impact : HIGH (user experience, potential revenue loss) Severity : MEDIUM-HIGH Mitigation Strategies : 1. Baseline Metrics : Establish current performance baseline before changes (Phase 2 - APM) 2. Load Testing : Performance testing in test environment before production 3. Gradual Rollout : Canary deployment starting with 5-10% traffic 4. Performance Budget : Define acceptable performance thresholds (P95 latency, etc.) 5. Rollback Plan : Automatic rollback if performance SLO breached Validation : APM monitoring showing performance within baseline ±10% Risk 4: Scope Creep During Modernization Risk : Stakeholders request new features during modernization, delaying delivery Probability : HIGH (very common in long-running projects) Impact : MEDIUM (timeline extension, cost increase) Severity : MEDIUM Mitigation Strategies : 1. Phased Approach : Clear phase boundaries with go/no-go decisions 2. Change Control : Formal change request process for scope additions 3. Backlog Management : New features go to backlog for post-modernization 4. Stakeholder Communication : Regular updates on modernization progress and priorities 5. Definition of Done : Clear acceptance criteria for each phase Validation : Phase completion without added scope, timeline adherence 📈 Performance & Scalability Current Performance Characteristics Performance Profile (from static analysis, NOT runtime measurements): - N+1 Query Risk : HIGH - Lazy loading throughout NHibernate configuration - Caching : NONE active (NHibernate second-level cache not configured) - Synchronous Only : No async/await patterns (not supported in .NET 3.5/4.0) - Session State : In-memory (fast but limits scalability) Cannot Measure Without Runtime Data : - Request throughput (req/sec) - Response time (p50/p95/p99 latency) - Concurrent user capacity - Database query performance - Memory consumption Required for Baseline : APM implementation in Phase 2 Evidence : performance-profile.json , query-performance.json Target Performance Architecture Async/Await Throughout : - Pattern : Convert synchronous I/O to async (database, HTTP calls, file I/O) - Benefits : Better resource utilization, higher throughput, improved scalability - Implementation : ASP.NET Core controllers with async actions, EF Core async queries Comprehensive Caching Strategy : - L1: Client-Side Cache : Browser caching for static content (CDN) - L2: Distributed Cache : Redis for application cache (product catalog, categories) - L3: Database Query Cache : EF Core query cache (readonly queries) - L4: Database Result Cache : Database-level result cache if supported - Benefits : Reduced database load, faster response times, lower latency Query Optimization : - Eager Loading : Use .Include() for related entities when needed (prevent N+1) - Projection : Select only required columns with .Select() - Pagination : Implement paging for list queries (prevent large result sets) - Indexing : Add database indexes based on APM query analysis Horizontal Scaling : - Auto-Scaling : Scale out based on CPU/memory/request metrics - Stateless Application : All state in distributed cache or database - Load Balancing : Traffic distribution across instances - Benefits : Handle traffic spikes, high availability, cost optimization 🗺️ Implementation Roadmap Phase-Based Approach with Dependencies Phase 1: Foundation (Duration: TBD - Sprint 0 planning) - Dependencies: NONE (can start immediately) - Objective: Safety net + critical vulnerabilities eliminated - Key Deliverables: - ✅ Automated testing framework (xUnit/NUnit) - ✅ 60%+ test coverage of critical paths - ✅ CI/CD pipeline operational - ✅ jQuery updated to 3.6+ - ✅ Secrets encrypted (Key Vault or environment variables) - ✅ Session state externalized (Redis or cloud-native) - ✅ Structured logging (Serilog + JSON) - ✅ SQL Server User Instance removed Phase 2: Cloud Migration (Duration: TBD - depends on Phase 1 velocity) - Dependencies: Phase 1 complete (tests, CI/CD, distributed session required) - Objective: Cloud-native deployment with scalability - Key Deliverables: - ✅ Application containerized (Docker) - ✅ Health check endpoints implemented - ✅ APM instrumentation (Application Insights, New Relic, or Datadog) - ✅ Distributed caching (Redis) - ✅ Database migrated to managed service - ✅ Responsive design implemented (mobile-first) - ✅ Cloud deployment with auto-scaling Phase 3: Framework Modernization (Duration: TBD - depends on Phase 2 velocity) - Dependencies: Phase 2 complete (containerization, cloud deployment required) - Objective: Modern technology stack, full compliance - Key Deliverables: - ✅ .NET 6+/.NET 8 LTS migration - ✅ ASP.NET Core MVC implementation - ✅ Entity Framework Core 6+ (replace NHibernate) - ✅ Built-in ASP.NET Core DI (replace StructureMap) - ✅ Modern authentication (ASP.NET Core Identity or external IdP) - ✅ GDPR compliance (data subject rights, consent management) Phase 4: Optimization (Duration: TBD - depends on Phase 3 velocity) - Dependencies: Phase 3 complete (modern stack required) - Objective: Performance optimization, feature enhancement - Key Deliverables: - ✅ Advanced caching strategies - ✅ Internationalization (i18n) support - ✅ Comprehensive monitoring dashboards - ✅ Performance optimization based on APM data - ✅ Advanced security features (CSP, HSTS, rate limiting) - ✅ Missing business features (inventory, returns) Critical Path : Phase 1 → Phase 2 → Phase 3 → Phase 4 (sequential dependencies) 📚 References & Resources Architecture Documentation System Architecture (Full C4 Model) Data Architecture API Integration Catalog Project Inventory Business Documentation Business Domain Model Requirements Specification Compliance and Regulatory User Experience Analysis Modernization Strategy Executive Summary Stakeholder Matrix Quick Start Guides QUICK-START-EXECUTIVE.md - docs.text: 1. Presentation Layer ( Agathas.Storefront.UI.Web.MVC ) - Technology : ASP.NET MVC 2, ASPX views, jQuery 1.3.2 - Responsibilities : HTTP handling, routing, view rendering, static content - Key Components : Global.asax , Web.config , Views, Content, Scripts - Issues : Non-responsive design, outdated jQuery (CVEs), ASPX views (obsolete) - Evidence : System Architecture - Container Diagram 2. Controllers Layer ( Agathas.Storefront.Controllers ) - Technology : ASP.NET MVC 2 controllers, AutoMapper 1.1 - Responsibilities : Request handling, view model mapping, action filters - Controllers : 9 controllers (~30 endpoints) - HomeController , ProductController , BasketController - CheckoutController , PaymentController , OrderController - CustomerController , AccountLogOnController , AccountRegisterController - Pattern : Request/Response messaging with services layer - Evidence : api-catalog.json 3. Services Layer ( Agathas.Storefront.Services ) - Technology : C# 3.5, AutoMapper 1.1 - Responsibilities : Business logic orchestration, cross-aggregate coordination - Services : 4 primary services - ProductService , BasketService , OrderService , CustomerService - Pattern : Request/Response objects, domain event publishing - Evidence : Business Services 4. Domain Layer ( Agathas.Storefront.Model ) - Technology : C# 3.5 pure domain logic (no framework dependencies) - Responsibilities : Business rules, invariants, domain events - Aggregates : 4 aggregate roots - ProductTitle (product catalog) - Basket (shopping cart) - Order (placed orders) - Customer (customer accounts) - Patterns : DDD (entities, value objects, aggregates), State Pattern (Order lifecycle) - Business Rules : 40+ documented rules enforced in domain - Strengths : ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Excellent DDD implementation - Evidence : Business Domain Model 5. Data Access Layer ( Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate ) - Technology : NHibernate 2.1, HBM.XML mappings - Responsibilities : Repository implementations, ORM mapping, persistence - Repositories : ProductRepository , BasketRepository , OrderRepository , CustomerRepository - Pattern : Repository Pattern, Unit of Work Pattern - Issues : Lazy loading throughout (N+1 query risk), outdated NHibernate version - Evidence : Data Architecture 6. Infrastructure Layer ( Agathas.Storefront.Infrastructure ) - Technology : C# 3.5, Log4Net 1.2, StructureMap 2.5 - Responsibilities : Cross-cutting concerns (auth, logging, email, payments, configuration) - Components : - Authentication (Forms Auth, Janrain) - Logging (Log4Net file appender) - Email (SMTP, TextLogging fallback) - Payments (PayPal integration) - Configuration management - Dependency injection (StructureMap) - Evidence : System Architecture - Infrastructure

docs.text: Status : ✅ ACCEPTED Date : 2026-06-09 Deciders : Architecture team, executive sponsor Context : Agathas.Storefront requires technology modernization due to obsolete stack (15+ years old). Two primary approaches considered: 1. Big-Bang Rewrite : Complete system replacement from scratch 2. Incremental Modernization : Phased approach preserving domain model Current Problem : - Technology stack obsolete (.NET Framework 3.5/4.0, no security patches) - Cannot scale horizontally (in-process state, LocalDB) - Security vulnerabilities (jQuery CVEs, plaintext secrets) - GDPR non-compliance (if serving EU customers) - Non-responsive design (mobile users 70%+ of traffic) Decision : Incremental Modernization with phased approach Alternatives Considered : Option A: Big-Bang Rewrite - ✅ Pros: Clean slate, no legacy constraints, latest technologies from day one - ❌ Cons: - High risk: Complete replacement with no fallback - Long cycle: 12-18+ months typical for full rewrites - No incremental value: No business benefit until cutover - Knowledge loss: Risk of losing business rules during recreation - Maintenance burden: Must maintain both old and new systems during development - ⚠️ Cost : Higher total cost (dual maintenance, extended timeline, risk mitigation) - ⚠️ Complexity : HIGH - entire system recreation from scratch Option B: Incremental Modernization (SELECTED) - ✅ Pros: - Lower risk: Smaller changes, easier to test and rollback - Incremental value: Each phase delivers business benefit - Preserve assets: Excellent domain model retained (no recreation) - Business continuity: System remains operational throughout - Learn and adapt: Adjust approach based on early phases - ❌ Cons: - Longer overall timeline: Phased approach may extend calendar time - Technical debt: Must live with some legacy during transition - Integration complexity: New and old components coexist temporarily - ⚠️ Cost : Lower total cost (single system maintenance, reduced risk, faster value delivery) - ⚠️ Complexity : MEDIUM - requires careful sequencing and integration Decision Criteria : - Business risk tolerance: MEDIUM (cannot afford complete outage) - Time to first value: HIGH priority (need security fixes soon) - Domain model quality: EXCELLENT (4.5/5 - worth preserving) - Business continuity requirement: CRITICAL Decision Matrix : Criterion Weight Big-Bang Rewrite Incremental Selected Business Risk HIGH (×3) LOW (3) = 9 HIGH (9) = 27 Incremental Time to Value HIGH (×3) LOW (3) = 9 HIGH (9) = 27 Incremental Preserve Domain Model MEDIUM (×2) LOW (3) = 6 HIGH (9) = 18 Incremental Technical Cleanliness LOW (×1) HIGH (9) = 9 MEDIUM (5) = 5 Big-Bang Total 33 77 Incremental Rationale : - Domain Model Excellence : The current domain model (DDD with 4 aggregates, 40+ business rules) is well-implemented and would be costly to recreate. Preservation saves months of effort and reduces risk of business logic loss. - Business Continuity : Incremental approach keeps system operational, avoiding revenue loss during extended rewrite period. - Risk Management : Smaller changes in each phase reduce risk of catastrophic failure. Can rollback individual phases without losing entire investment. - Value Delivery : Early phases (testing, security fixes, scalability) deliver measurable business value within weeks/months, not waiting 12-18+ months for big-bang cutover. Consequences : - ✅ Positive : Lower risk, faster time to first value, preserved domain expertise, business continuity - ❌ Negative : Longer overall calendar time, temporary coexistence of old/new patterns, ongoing refactoring - ⚠️ Risks : Phase dependencies could delay later phases if earlier phases discover unexpected complexity Validation : - Success Metrics : - Phase 1 completion within 2-4 months of start (velocity-dependent) - Zero production incidents caused by modernization changes - Test coverage >60% by Phase 1 end - Critical vulnerabilities eliminated by Phase 1 end - Review Timeline : After each phase completion, assess approach and adjust if needed References : - Strangler Fig Pattern - Martin Fowler - EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY.md - Phased approach details
docs.title: ADR-001: Incremental Modernization vs Big-Bang Rewrite

docs.text: Status : ✅ ACCEPTED (vendor-agnostic architecture) Date : 2026-06-09 Deciders : Architecture team Context : Target architecture requires cloud-native capabilities (managed database, auto-scaling, distributed caching, secrets management, APM). Cloud provider selection will be made by business stakeholders, so architecture must support multiple vendors. Decision : Design vendor-agnostic architecture compatible with Azure, AWS, and GCP Alternatives Considered : Option A: Azure-Specific Design - ✅ Pros: Native Windows/.NET support, seamless integration with existing Microsoft stack - ❌ Cons: Vendor lock-in, migration cost if switching providers, limits negotiation leverage - ⚠️ Cost : Azure pricing competitive for .NET workloads, but locked into Azure pricing model - ⚠️ Complexity : LOW - natural fit for .NET applications Option B: AWS-Specific Design - ✅ Pros: Market leader, broadest service catalog, mature ecosystem - ❌ Cons: .NET support secondary to Java/Node, more AWS-specific services used - ⚠️ Cost : AWS pricing typically higher for equivalent services, negotiable at scale - ⚠️ Complexity : MEDIUM - less .NET-native tooling than Azure Option C: GCP-Specific Design - ✅ Pros: Competitive pricing, excellent Kubernetes support, strong data/ML services - ❌ Cons: Smallest market share, less .NET-specific tooling - ⚠️ Cost : GCP pricing often most competitive, committed use discounts - ⚠️ Complexity : MEDIUM - similar to AWS for .NET workloads Option D: Vendor-Agnostic Design (SELECTED) - ✅ Pros: - Portability: Can switch providers if needed - Negotiation leverage: Multi-cloud strategy enables better pricing - Technology choices: Use best-of-breed services regardless of vendor - Risk mitigation: Not dependent on single vendor viability - ❌ Cons: - Abstraction overhead: Must avoid vendor-specific features - Potential cost premium: May not leverage vendor-specific optimizations - ⚠️ Cost : Comparable across vendors for standard services (compute, database, cache) - ⚠️ Complexity : MEDIUM - requires abstraction layer for provider differences Decision Criteria : - Portability: HIGH priority (avoid lock-in) - Business flexibility: HIGH priority (enable multi-vendor strategy) - Technology choice: MEDIUM priority (prefer open standards) - Optimization: LOW priority (portability > vendor-specific optimizations) Rationale : - Business Strategy : Cloud provider not yet selected by stakeholders. Vendor-agnostic design preserves flexibility for business negotiations and decisions. - Technology Standards : Use open standards (Docker, Kubernetes, Redis, OpenTelemetry, OAuth/OIDC) that work across all major cloud providers. - Risk Mitigation : Avoid dependencies on vendor-specific services (e.g., avoid Azure Functions, AWS Lambda, GCP Cloud Functions - use standard containers instead). - Portability : If business requirements change or pricing becomes unfavorable, can migrate to different provider without architectural redesign. Implementation Approach : Common Services Across Vendors : | Service Type | Open Standard / Common Implementation | Azure | AWS | GCP | |--------------|--------------------------------------|-------|-----|-----| | Containers | Docker, Kubernetes | Azure Container Apps, AKS | ECS, EKS | Cloud Run, GKE | | Database | PostgreSQL or SQL Server | Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Azure SQL | RDS PostgreSQL, RDS SQL Server | Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud SQL SQL Server | | Cache | Redis | Azure Cache for Redis | ElastiCache for Redis | Memorystore for Redis | | Secrets | Environment variables + vault | Azure Key Vault | AWS Secrets Manager | Secret Manager | | Logging | Structured JSON logs | Application Insights | CloudWatch | Cloud Logging | | Monitoring | OpenTelemetry | Application Insights | CloudWatch + X-Ray | Cloud Monitoring + Trace | | CDN | Standard HTTP cache | Azure CDN | CloudFront | Cloud CDN | Consequences : - ✅ Positive : Business flexibility, negotiation leverage, portability, risk mitigation - ❌ Negative : Cannot use vendor-specific optimizations, abstraction overhead - ⚠️ Risks : May miss vendor-specific features that could provide competitive advantage Validation : - Success Metrics : Architecture diagrams and documentation reference generic services, not vendor-specific products - Proof of Concept : Deploy containerized application to 2+ cloud providers to validate portability References : - 12-Factor App - Cloud-native application principles - CNCF Cloud Native Trail Map - Open-source cloud-native technologies
docs.title: ADR-002: Cloud Platform Approach (Vendor-Agnostic)

docs.text: Status : ✅ ACCEPTED Date : 2026-06-09 Deciders : Architecture team Context : Current application uses NHibernate 2.1 (2009) with XML-based HBM mappings. Modernization to .NET 6+ provides opportunity to migrate to Entity Framework Core, which is Microsoft's recommended ORM for .NET Core/.NET 6+. Decision : Migrate to Entity Framework Core 6+ with code-first Fluent API Alternatives Considered : Option A: Keep NHibernate 2.1 - ✅ Pros: No migration effort, existing mappings work - ❌ Cons: Severely outdated (13+ years old), lacks modern features, community support declining - ⚠️ Effort : ZERO - no changes required - ⚠️ Risk : HIGH - outdated ORM limits modernization, potential bugs, no support Option B: Upgrade NHibernate to 5.x - ✅ Pros: Keeps familiar ORM, incremental upgrade path, improved performance - ❌ Cons: Still requires HBM.XML migration to Fluent mapping, not Microsoft-supported, smaller community than EF Core - ⚠️ Effort : MEDIUM - XML→Fluent mapping conversion, testing, NHibernate 2→5 breaking changes - ⚠️ Risk : MEDIUM - Third-party dependency, community support < EF Core Option C: Entity Framework Core 6+ (SELECTED) - ✅ Pros: - Microsoft-supported with active development - Native .NET 6+ integration - Code-first with Fluent API (modern approach) - Excellent tooling (migrations, database scaffolding) - Large community and extensive documentation - Performance on par with NHibernate 5.x - ❌ Cons: - Migration effort required (HBM.XML → Fluent API) - Learning curve for team (if unfamiliar with EF Core) - Some NHibernate features not in EF Core (criteria API differences) - ⚠️ Effort : MEDIUM-HIGH - Mapping conversion, repository updates, query refactoring, comprehensive testing - ⚠️ Risk : MEDIUM - Well-documented migration path, comprehensive testing required Decision Criteria : - Microsoft support: HIGH importance (future-proof) - Community size: MEDIUM importance (resources, troubleshooting) - Modern features: HIGH importance (migrations, tooling) - Migration effort: MEDIUM importance (necessary investment for long-term benefit) Decision Matrix : Criterion Weight Keep NH 2.1 Upgrade NH 5.x EF Core 6+ Selected Microsoft Support HIGH (×3) LOW (1) = 3 LOW (3) = 9 HIGH (9) = 27 EF Core Modern Features HIGH (×3) LOW (1) = 3 MEDIUM (5) = 15 HIGH (9) = 27 EF Core Community/Resources MEDIUM (×2) LOW (3) = 6 MEDIUM (5) = 10 HIGH (9) = 18 EF Core Migration Effort MEDIUM (×2) HIGH (9) = 18 MEDIUM (5) = 10 MEDIUM (5) = 10 NH 2.1 Total 30 44 82 EF Core Rationale : - Microsoft Support : EF Core is first-class citizen in .NET 6+ ecosystem with guaranteed long-term support - Modern Features : Code-first approach with migrations simplifies schema evolution, better tooling integration - Community : Largest .NET ORM community, extensive documentation, Stack Overflow support - Performance : EF Core 6+ performance comparable to NHibernate 5.x (Microsoft benchmarks) - Investment : Migration effort justified by long-term maintainability and modern features Migration Strategy : Phase 1 : Repository Layer Isolation (DONE - current architecture) - Repository Pattern already abstracts ORM from domain - Domain layer has no NHibernate dependencies Phase 2 : Entity Mapping Conversion - Convert HBM.XML mappings → EF Core Fluent API configurations - Maintain identical database schema (no schema changes) - Example mapping translation: // Current: HBM.XML < class name = "Product" table = "Products" > < id name = "Id" column = "ProductId" > < generator class = "identity" /> </ id > < property name = "Name" column = "ProductName" /> </ class > // Target: EF Core Fluent API public class ProductConfiguration : IEntityTypeConfiguration < Product > { public void Configure ( EntityTypeBuilder < Product > builder ) { builder . ToTable ( "Products" ); builder . HasKey ( p => p . Id ); builder . Property ( p => p . Id ). HasColumnName ( "ProductId" ). ValueGeneratedOnAdd (); builder . Property ( p => p . Name ). HasColumnName ( "ProductName" ); } } Phase 3 : Repository Implementation Update - Replace NHibernate ISession with EF Core DbContext - Update repository implementations to use EF Core APIs - Convert NHibernate criteria queries to LINQ (EF Core query provider) Phase 4 : Testing - Unit tests for repository layer - Integration tests against test database - Data integrity validation (query results match NH vs EF Core) Consequences : - ✅ Positive : Modern ORM, Microsoft support, tooling integration, future-proof - ❌ Negative : Migration effort (estimated 2-4 weeks for mapping conversion + testing) - ⚠️ Risks : Query behavior differences between NH and EF Core require thorough testing Validation : - Success Metrics : - All 15 entities successfully mapped in EF Core - All repository integration tests passing - Query performance within 10% of NHibernate baseline - Zero data integrity issues in QA environment - Testing Approach : Side-by-side testing (NH vs EF Core) to validate query results match References : - Entity Framework Core Documentation - EF Core vs NHibernate Comparison
docs.title: ADR-003: Migration from NHibernate to Entity Framework Core

docs.text: Pattern Description : Incrementally replace parts of the legacy system by placing a façade in front, routing requests to either legacy or new implementation, gradually "strangling" the old system until it can be retired. Named After : Strangler fig tree that grows around host tree, eventually replacing it entirely. How It Works : 1. Create façade/routing layer that intercepts all requests 2. Implement new functionality alongside old (parallel) 3. Route specific requests to new implementation 4. Test thoroughly with production traffic (canary/blue-green) 5. Gradually expand new implementation scope 6. Remove old implementation when fully replaced 7. Repeat for next component Why Chosen for Agathas.Storefront : - ✅ Low risk: Old system remains operational as fallback - ✅ Incremental value: Each migrated component delivers benefit - ✅ Testable: Can validate new implementation with real traffic before full cutover - ✅ Reversible: Can route back to old implementation if issues arise - ✅ Business continuity: Zero downtime during migration Implementation for Agathas : Strangler Fig applied at technology layer level (not microservices decomposition - that's out of scope for initial modernization): Phase 1 : Strangle infrastructure dependencies Session state: In-process → distributed cache Logging: File-based → structured cloud logging Secrets: Plaintext config → secure vault Testing: Zero tests → comprehensive coverage Phase 2 : Strangle platform dependencies Hosting: IIS on Windows → containers on managed platform Database: LocalDB → managed cloud database Frontend: ASPX + jQuery 1.3.2 → Razor + modern frontend (or SPA) Observability: None → APM + metrics + tracing Phase 3 : Strangle framework dependencies Runtime: .NET Framework 3.5/4.0 → .NET 6+/8 Web framework: ASP.NET MVC 2 → ASP.NET Core MVC ORM: NHibernate 2.1 → Entity Framework Core 6+ Authentication: ASP.NET Membership → ASP.NET Core Identity NOT Microservices Decomposition (common misconception): - ❌ Strangler Fig does NOT require breaking monolith into microservices - ✅ Strangler Fig works for modernizing monoliths while keeping monolithic architecture - 🎯 Focus: Technology modernization, NOT architectural decomposition
docs.title: Primary Pattern: Strangler Fig Pattern

docs.text: Current Implementation : - Technology : In-process session state ( <sessionState mode="InProc" /> ) - Location : Web.config configuration - Usage : Shopping basket, user preferences, authentication state - Issue : Lost on application restart, prevents horizontal scaling Target Implementation : - Technology : Distributed session state with Redis or cloud-native session store - Provider : Redis cache (vendor-agnostic) OR Azure Cache for Redis / ElastiCache / Memorystore - Configuration : <sessionState mode="Custom" customProvider="RedisSessionStateProvider" /> - Benefits : Persists across restarts, shared across instances, enables horizontal scaling Migration Approach : - Pattern : REPLACE (drop-in replacement with configuration change) - Effort : LOW - configuration change + Redis deployment + testing - Risk : LOW - established pattern, well-tested providers - Testing : Session persistence across app restarts, load-balanced session sharing Estimated Effort : 2-3 days (configuration, deployment, testing) Basis : Simple configuration change, Redis is turnkey service, established pattern
docs.title: Component: Session State Management

docs.text: Current Implementation : - Technology : SQL Server Express LocalDB with User Instance mode - Database Files : App_Data\Shop.mdf , App_Data\aspnetdb.mdf - Connection String : AttachDbFilename=|DataDirectory|\Shop.mdf;User Instance=true - Issue : User Instance deprecated, requires local file system, no HA, no scaling Target Implementation : - Technology : Managed database service (vendor-agnostic SQL Server or PostgreSQL) - Options : - SQL Server: Azure SQL Database, RDS SQL Server, Cloud SQL SQL Server - PostgreSQL: Azure Database for PostgreSQL, RDS PostgreSQL, Cloud SQL PostgreSQL - Benefits : High availability, automated backups, point-in-time restore, scalability, managed patching Migration Approach : - Pattern : REHOST (lift-and-shift database to managed service) - Steps : 1. Export Schema : Generate CREATE scripts from LocalDB (SQL Server Management Studio) 2. Export Data : Generate INSERT scripts or use data export tools (BCP, SSMS) 3. Provision Managed Database : Create cloud database instance with appropriate SKU 4. Import Schema : Execute CREATE scripts on cloud database 5. Import Data : Execute INSERT scripts or use import tools 6. Update Connection Strings : Replace User Instance connection with standard connection string 7. Test : Comprehensive data validation, query performance testing - Effort : MEDIUM - straightforward migration, testing intensive - Risk : LOW - established pattern, no schema changes required Connection String Changes : <!-- BEFORE: User Instance (deprecated) --> <add name= "Shop" connectionString= "Data Source=.\SQLEXPRESS;AttachDbFilename=|DataDirectory|\Shop.mdf;User Instance=true;Integrated Security=SSPI" /> <!-- AFTER: Managed Database (cloud) --> <add name= "Shop" connectionString= "Server=shopdb.database.windows.net;Database=Shop;User Id=shopuser;Password=<from Key Vault>;Encrypt=true;" /> Database Size : Unknown (requires measurement) Estimated Effort : 3-5 days (export, provision, import, test) Basis : Small database (15 tables from analysis), straightforward lift-and-shift
docs.title: Component: Database (SQL Server LocalDB → Managed Database)

docs.text: Current Implementation : - Technology : ASPX views (ASP.NET Web Forms view engine), jQuery 1.3.2 - Location : Views/ folder, Scripts/jquery-1.3.2.js - CSS : Fixed-width layout, no responsive design - Issue : Obsolete view engine, vulnerable jQuery, non-responsive, poor mobile UX Target Implementation Options : Option A: Razor Views + Modern CSS Framework (RECOMMENDED for Phase 1) - Technology : ASP.NET Core Razor views + Bootstrap 5 or Tailwind CSS - Benefits : Server-side rendering (SEO-friendly), responsive design, incremental migration - Effort : MEDIUM - View conversion ASPX→Razor, CSS framework integration - Rationale : Preserves server-side rendering pattern, low risk, fast delivery Option B: Modern SPA Framework (FUTURE - Phase 4) - Technology : React, Vue, or Angular + ASP.NET Core Web API backend - Benefits : Rich interactivity, modern developer experience, componentization - Effort : HIGH - Rewrite frontend as SPA, API layer implementation - Rationale : Future enhancement after core modernization complete Migration Approach (Option A - Razor) : - Pattern : REFACTOR (rewrite views, preserve server-side model) - Steps : 1. Convert ASPX views → Razor views ( .cshtml ) 2. Integrate Bootstrap 5 responsive grid system 3. Update jQuery 1.3.2 → jQuery 3.6+ OR migrate to vanilla JavaScript 4. Implement responsive layouts (mobile-first) 5. Test across devices (desktop, tablet, mobile) - Effort : MEDIUM - 15 views to convert, responsive CSS design - Risk : MEDIUM - Visual design changes require UX review Estimated Effort : 3-4 weeks (view conversion, responsive design, cross-device testing) Basis : 15 views identified from UI inventory, Bootstrap integration is well-documented pattern

docs.text: Approach : REHOST then REFACTOR Phase 1: Rehost (Lift-and-Shift) - Zero schema changes 1. Export Schema : Generate CREATE TABLE scripts from LocalDB 2. Export Data : Generate INSERT scripts or use BCP/SSIS 3. Provision Managed Database : Create cloud database instance 4. Import Schema + Data : Deploy to cloud database 5. Update Connection Strings : Point application to cloud database 6. Validate : Data integrity checks, query performance testing Benefits : Fast migration, low risk, immediate cloud benefits (HA, backups) Phase 2: Refactor (Schema Modernization) - Post-migration optimization 1. Add Missing Indexes : Based on query performance analysis from APM 2. Add Audit Columns : CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, CreatedBy, UpdatedBy (for GDPR audit trail) 3. Add Soft Delete : IsDeleted flag (for GDPR right to erasure without data loss) 4. Schema Normalization : Fix any denormalization issues (analysis shows good normalization already) Benefits : Performance optimization, GDPR readiness, maintainability

docs.text: Mapping Conversion Strategy : Current : XML-based HBM mappings (15 entities) Target : Code-first with Fluent API configurations Migration Process : 1. Create Entity Configurations : One IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> class per entity 2. Convert Mappings : Translate HBM.XML → Fluent API 3. Register Configurations : OnModelCreating in DbContext 4. Generate Migration : EF Core migration for schema validation (should be no-op if schema correct) 5. Test : Integration tests validating query results match Example Conversion : Before (NHibernate HBM.XML) : <!-- Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate/Mapping/Order.hbm.xml --> <hibernate-mapping> <class name= "Agathas.Storefront.Model.Orders.Order, Agathas.Storefront.Model" table= "Orders" > <id name= "Id" column= "OrderId" > <generator class= "identity" /> </id> <property name= "OrderDate" column= "OrderDate" type= "DateTime" not-null= "true" /> <property name= "OrderState" column= "OrderState" type= "Int32" not-null= "true" /> <property name= "TotalAmount" column= "TotalAmount" type= "Decimal" precision= "18" scale= "2" not-null= "true" /> <many-to-one name= "Customer" class= "Agathas.Storefront.Model.Customers.Customer" column= "CustomerId" not-null= "true" /> <bag name= "OrderItems" cascade= "all" lazy= "true" > <key column= "OrderId" /> <one-to-many class= "Agathas.Storefront.Model.Orders.OrderItem" /> </bag> </class> </hibernate-mapping> After (Entity Framework Core Fluent API) : // Data/Configurations/OrderConfiguration.cs public class OrderConfiguration : IEntityTypeConfiguration < Order > { public void Configure ( EntityTypeBuilder < Order > builder ) { builder . ToTable ( "Orders" ); builder . HasKey ( o => o . Id ); builder . Property ( o => o . Id ) . HasColumnName ( "OrderId" ) . ValueGeneratedOnAdd (); builder . Property ( o => o . OrderDate ) . HasColumnName ( "OrderDate" ) . IsRequired (); builder . Property ( o => o . OrderState ) . HasColumnName ( "OrderState" ) . HasConversion < int > () // Enum → int . IsRequired (); builder . Property ( o => o . TotalAmount ) . HasColumnName ( "TotalAmount" ) . HasPrecision ( 18 , 2 ) . IsRequired (); builder . HasOne ( o => o . Customer ) . WithMany () . HasForeignKey ( "CustomerId" ) . IsRequired (); builder . HasMany ( o => o . OrderItems ) . WithOne () . HasForeignKey ( "OrderId" ) . OnDelete ( DeleteBehavior . Cascade ); } } Estimated Effort : 1-2 weeks for all 15 entities + comprehensive testing Basis : 15 entities from analysis, mapping conversion is mechanical, testing is primary effort

docs.text: Authentication : - Forms Authentication ( <authentication mode="Forms" /> ) - ASP.NET Membership with SQL Server provider (SHA1 password hashing - WEAK) - Janrain Social Login (OAuth-style callback for Facebook, Google, Twitter) - Issue : Weak password hashing (SHA1 vulnerable to rainbow tables), no MFA Authorization : - Role-Based Access Control (basic implementation) - Authorization Attributes on controller actions [Authorize(Roles="Admin")] - Issue : Limited granularity, no claims-based authorization Data Protection : - Plaintext Secrets in Web.config (CRITICAL VULNERABILITY) - No Encryption at Rest for sensitive data (database not encrypted) - No Column-Level Encryption for sensitive fields (credit cards not stored, but addresses unencrypted) - Issue : Configuration file exposure risk, no defense-in-depth Network Security : - HTTPS for external communication (PayPal, Janrain) - HTTP for internal communication (assumed - no Load Balancer currently) - Issue : No WAF, no DDoS protection, no rate limiting Input Validation : - Data Annotations on view models (basic validation) - jQuery Validation client-side (vulnerable jQuery 1.3.2) - No Centralized Validation framework - Issue : Inconsistent validation, no anti-forgery tokens globally Evidence : security-controls.json , vulnerability-assessment.json
docs.title: Current Security Posture

docs.text: Authentication (Modern & Secure): - ASP.NET Core Identity with bcrypt/Argon2 password hashing - External Identity Provider (Auth0, Azure AD B2C, Okta) for OAuth/OIDC - Multi-Factor Authentication support (TOTP, SMS, email) - Passwordless Options (Magic links, WebAuthn) - Benefits : Strong hashing, MFA, delegated auth management, industry best practices Authorization (Claims-Based): - Claims-Based Authorization in ASP.NET Core - Policy-Based Authorization for complex rules - JWT Tokens for API authentication (if SPA frontend) - Benefits : Fine-grained control, extensible, standard protocol Data Protection (Defense-in-Depth): - Secrets Management : Azure Key Vault / AWS Secrets Manager / GCP Secret Manager - Encryption at Rest : Database encryption (TDE or vendor-managed) - Encryption in Transit : TLS 1.2+ for all communication - Column-Level Encryption : For highly sensitive data (if applicable) - Benefits : No plaintext secrets, layered security, compliance-ready Network Security (Perimeter Protection): - Web Application Firewall (WAF) at edge - DDoS Protection (Cloud provider native) - Rate Limiting at API gateway / load balancer - HTTPS Everywhere with TLS 1.2+ only - Benefits : Attack surface reduction, traffic filtering, availability protection Input Validation (Comprehensive): - Centralized Validation with Data Annotations + Fluent Validation - Anti-Forgery Tokens on all state-changing operations - Content Security Policy headers to prevent XSS - Parameterized Queries throughout (EF Core default) - Benefits : Injection prevention, XSS mitigation, consistent validation
docs.title: Target Security Architecture

docs.text: Observability (See What's Happening): - APM : Application Performance Monitoring with distributed tracing - Structured Logging : JSON logs with correlation IDs, log levels, contextual information - Metrics : Request rates, response times, error rates, business metrics - Distributed Tracing : End-to-end request flow visualization - Dashboards : Real-time operational dashboards with key metrics - Benefits : Proactive issue detection, performance insights, faster troubleshooting Reliability (Keep It Running): - Health Checks : Liveness and readiness endpoints for orchestrator - Circuit Breakers : Fault tolerance for external dependencies (Polly library) - Retry Policies : Automatic retry with exponential backoff - Graceful Degradation : Continue operation when non-critical services fail - Benefits : Improved uptime, fault tolerance, better user experience Deployment (Ship Fast, Ship Safe): - CI/CD Pipeline : Automated build, test, deploy - Blue-Green Deployment : Zero-downtime deployment with instant rollback - Canary Releases : Gradual rollout with traffic shifting - Automated Rollback : Automatic rollback on health check failure - Benefits : Fast delivery, low risk, rapid rollback if needed Monitoring & Alerting (Know When Things Break): - Proactive Alerts : Notify before users impacted (e.g., high error rate, slow response) - Escalation Policies : On-call rotation, escalation after timeouts - Incident Management : Runbooks for common issues, post-mortem process - SLO Tracking : Service Level Objective monitoring and reporting - Benefits : Faster incident response, reduced MTTR, continuous improvement
docs.title: Target Operational Capabilities

docs.text: Availability SLO : 99.9% uptime (8.76 hours downtime per year) Basis : Multi-instance deployment with load balancer enables "three nines" Latency SLO : - P50: <200ms (50th percentile) - P95: <500ms (95th percentile) - P99: <1000ms (99th percentile) Basis : Industry standard for e-commerce applications, achievable with CDN and caching Error Rate SLO : <0.1% of requests result in 5xx errors Basis : High-quality codebase with comprehensive testing Measurement : APM tool tracking in real-time, alerts when SLO breached
docs.title: SLO (Service Level Objectives) - Target

docs.text: Risk : Data corruption or loss during database migration from LocalDB to cloud database Probability : MEDIUM (complex migrations have 10-20% issue rate) Impact : HIGH (potential data loss, business disruption) Severity : HIGH Mitigation Strategies : 1. Pre-Migration Backup : Full backup of LocalDB before migration start 2. Data Validation : Checksum validation (row counts, critical field sums) 3. Test Migration : Perform migration on test environment first 4. Parallel Running : Keep LocalDB as backup during initial cloud DB operation 5. Rollback Plan : Documented rollback procedure with timing estimates 6. Incremental Cutover : Migrate aspnetdb first (lower risk), then Shop.mdf Validation : Row count matching, foreign key integrity checks, sample data verification
docs.title: Risk 1: Data Migration Failure

docs.text: Risk : .NET Framework → .NET 6+ migration introduces breaking changes causing functionality loss Probability : HIGH (significant API changes between Framework and .NET 6+) Impact : MEDIUM (features broken, may require rework) Severity : MEDIUM-HIGH Mitigation Strategies : 1. Comprehensive Testing : 60%+ test coverage before migration (Phase 1) 2. Incremental Migration : Migrate project by project, test after each 3. API Compatibility Analysis : Use .NET Upgrade Assistant to identify breaking changes 4. Compatibility Shims : Use compatibility packages where possible 5. Team Training : Ensure team familiar with .NET 6+ differences before migration Validation : All automated tests passing, manual regression testing of critical paths
docs.title: Risk 2: Framework Migration Breaking Changes

docs.text: Risk : Cloud deployment or framework changes result in performance degradation Probability : MEDIUM (common in cloud migrations) Impact : HIGH (user experience, potential revenue loss) Severity : MEDIUM-HIGH Mitigation Strategies : 1. Baseline Metrics : Establish current performance baseline before changes (Phase 2 - APM) 2. Load Testing : Performance testing in test environment before production 3. Gradual Rollout : Canary deployment starting with 5-10% traffic 4. Performance Budget : Define acceptable performance thresholds (P95 latency, etc.) 5. Rollback Plan : Automatic rollback if performance SLO breached Validation : APM monitoring showing performance within baseline ±10%
docs.title: Risk 3: Performance Degradation

docs.text: Risk : Stakeholders request new features during modernization, delaying delivery Probability : HIGH (very common in long-running projects) Impact : MEDIUM (timeline extension, cost increase) Severity : MEDIUM Mitigation Strategies : 1. Phased Approach : Clear phase boundaries with go/no-go decisions 2. Change Control : Formal change request process for scope additions 3. Backlog Management : New features go to backlog for post-modernization 4. Stakeholder Communication : Regular updates on modernization progress and priorities 5. Definition of Done : Clear acceptance criteria for each phase Validation : Phase completion without added scope, timeline adherence
docs.title: Risk 4: Scope Creep During Modernization

docs.text: Performance Profile (from static analysis, NOT runtime measurements): - N+1 Query Risk : HIGH - Lazy loading throughout NHibernate configuration - Caching : NONE active (NHibernate second-level cache not configured) - Synchronous Only : No async/await patterns (not supported in .NET 3.5/4.0) - Session State : In-memory (fast but limits scalability) Cannot Measure Without Runtime Data : - Request throughput (req/sec) - Response time (p50/p95/p99 latency) - Concurrent user capacity - Database query performance - Memory consumption Required for Baseline : APM implementation in Phase 2 Evidence : performance-profile.json , query-performance.json
docs.title: Current Performance Characteristics

docs.text: Async/Await Throughout : - Pattern : Convert synchronous I/O to async (database, HTTP calls, file I/O) - Benefits : Better resource utilization, higher throughput, improved scalability - Implementation : ASP.NET Core controllers with async actions, EF Core async queries Comprehensive Caching Strategy : - L1: Client-Side Cache : Browser caching for static content (CDN) - L2: Distributed Cache : Redis for application cache (product catalog, categories) - L3: Database Query Cache : EF Core query cache (readonly queries) - L4: Database Result Cache : Database-level result cache if supported - Benefits : Reduced database load, faster response times, lower latency Query Optimization : - Eager Loading : Use .Include() for related entities when needed (prevent N+1) - Projection : Select only required columns with .Select() - Pagination : Implement paging for list queries (prevent large result sets) - Indexing : Add database indexes based on APM query analysis Horizontal Scaling : - Auto-Scaling : Scale out based on CPU/memory/request metrics - Stateless Application : All state in distributed cache or database - Load Balancing : Traffic distribution across instances - Benefits : Handle traffic spikes, high availability, cost optimization

Developer Quick Start - Agathas.Storefront Modernization Hands-on guide for developers joining the Agathas.Storefront modernization project - from zero to productive quickly Target Audience : Developers, QA Engineers, DevOps Engineers joining the modernization team Prerequisites : C# development experience, basic cloud concepts, git proficiency Est. Setup Time : 2-4 hours (depends on download speeds and machine specs) Last Updated : 2026-06-09 📋 Table of Contents Quick Start Overview Development Environment Setup Codebase Overview Local Development Workflow Understanding the Architecture Common Development Tasks Testing Guidelines Troubleshooting Contributing Guidelines Resources & References 🚀 Quick Start Overview What You'll Be Working On Agathas.Storefront is an e-commerce platform currently undergoing modernization from legacy ASP.NET MVC 2 (.NET Framework 3.5/4.0, circa 2010) to modern .NET 6+/ASP.NET Core with cloud-native capabilities. Current State : - 7 Visual Studio projects in layered architecture (Presentation, Controllers, Services, Domain, Data Access, Infrastructure) - Domain-Driven Design with excellent aggregate boundaries (Product, Basket, Order, Customer) - 6,104 lines of code across 192 classes - Zero automated tests (this is changing - Phase 1 priority!) - Manual deployment to IIS on Windows Modernization Phases : 1. Phase 1 (CURRENT): Establish testing foundation, eliminate critical vulnerabilities 2. Phase 2 : Cloud migration with containerization, managed database, responsive design 3. Phase 3 : Framework modernization (.NET 6+, ASP.NET Core, EF Core) 4. Phase 4 : Optimization and feature enhancement Your Role : Help modernize this well-architected application while preserving its excellent domain model Key Documents for Developers : 1. System Architecture (45 min) - Understand layered architecture and patterns 2. Business Domain Model (30 min) - Understand business logic and aggregates 3. GLOSSARY.md (reference) - Terminology and technology definitions 💻 Development Environment Setup Prerequisites Checklist Install the following tools before proceeding: Required Tools [ ] Visual Studio 2022 (Community, Professional, or Enterprise) Download: https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/ Workloads: ASP.NET and web development, .NET desktop development Verify: Open Visual Studio → Help → About [ ] .NET Framework 3.5 Developer Pack (for current codebase) Download: https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-framework/net35-sp1 Verify: reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\NET Framework Setup\NDP\v3.5" [ ] .NET Framework 4.0 Developer Pack (for current codebase) Download: https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-framework/net40 Verify: reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\NET Framework Setup\NDP\v4\Full" [ ] .NET 6 SDK or .NET 8 SDK (for modernization target) Download: https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download Verify: dotnet --version (should show 6.x or 8.x) [ ] SQL Server Express 2022 (or LocalDB) Download: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/sql-server/sql-server-downloads (Express edition) Purpose: Local database for development Verify: SQL Server Management Studio can connect to localhost\SQLEXPRESS [ ] Git Download: https://git-scm.com/downloads Verify: git --version Recommended Tools [ ] SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) Download: https://aka.ms/ssmsfullsetup Purpose: Database management and query testing [ ] Postman or Insomnia Download: https://www.postman.com/ or https://insomnia.rest/ Purpose: API testing (for future API development) [ ] ReSharper or Rider (optional, but helpful) Purpose: Code analysis, refactoring, navigation Repository Setup 1. Clone Repository # Clone the repository (replace with actual repository URL) git clone https :// github . com / [organization] / Agathas . Storefront . git cd Agathas . Storefront # Verify all files present git status 2. Restore NuGet Packages # Option 1: Visual Studio (recommended) # Open Agathas.Storefront.sln in Visual Studio # Right-click solution → Restore NuGet Packages # Option 2: Command line nuget restore Agathas . Storefront . sln Expected Packages (from analysis): - ASP.NET MVC 2.0 - NHibernate 2.1 - StructureMap 2.5 - AutoMapper 1.1 - Log4Net 1.2 - jQuery 1.3.2 (in Scripts folder) 3. Database Setup Create Local Databases : -- Option 1: Use existing MDF files (if provided) -- Files should be in Agathas.Storefront.UI.Web.MVC/App_Data/ -- Shop.mdf (main database) -- aspnetdb.mdf (membership database) -- User Instance mode will attach these automatically on first run -- Option 2: Create databases manually (if MDF files not provided) -- Open SQL Server Management Studio -- Connect to localhost\SQLEXPRESS CREATE DATABASE Shop ; GO CREATE DATABASE aspnetdb ; GO -- Then run schema creation scripts (if provided in /Database folder) Connection String Configuration : Check Agathas.Storefront.UI.Web.MVC/Web.config : Note : SQL Server User Instance is deprecated. If connection fails, switch to standard connection string and create databases manually. 4. Build Solution # Option 1: Visual Studio # Open Agathas.Storefront.sln # Build → Build Solution (Ctrl+Shift+B) # Option 2: MSBuild command line msbuild Agathas . Storefront . sln / p : Configuration = Debug Expected Build Output : All 7 projects build successfully - Agathas.Storefront.UI.Web.MVC - Agathas.Storefront.Controllers - Agathas.Storefront.Services - Agathas.Storefront.Model - Agathas.Storefront.Repository.NHibernate - Agathas.Storefront.Infrastructure Build Warnings : Some warnings expected due to obsolete framework (ignore for now) 5. Run Application Option 1: IIS Express (Recommended) : 1. Open Agathas.Storefront.sln in Visual Studio 2. Set Agathas.Storefront.UI.Web.MVC as startup project (right-click → Set as Startup Project) 3. Press F5 (Start Debugging) or Ctrl+F5 (Start Without Debugging) 4. Browser should open to http://localhost:[port]/ Option 2: Local IIS : 1. Open IIS Manager 2. Create new application pool (.NET Framework 4.0, Integrated pipeline) 3. Add website pointing to Agathas.Storefront.UI.Web.MVC folder 4. Id ); return new GetOrderHistoryResponse { Orders = orders . Select ( o => Mapper . Map < OrderViewModel > ( o )). ToList () }; } } Add Controller Action in Agathas.Storefront.Controllers/Controllers/OrderController.cs : public class OrderController : BaseController { private readonly IOrderService _orderService ; public OrderController ( IOrderService orderService ) { _orderService = orderService ; } public ActionResult History ( int customerId ) { var request = new GetOrderHistoryRequest { CustomerId = customerId }; var response = _orderService . CreateCriteria < Product > () . CreateAlias ( "ProductTitle" , "pt" ) . CreateAlias ( "pt.Category" , "cat" ) . Add ( Restrictions . Eq ( "cat.Id" , categoryId )) . True ); } } Testing Framework : xUnit or NUnit (to be decided in Phase 1) 🐛 Troubleshooting Issue 1: SQL Server User Instance Not Supported Symptom : Error on startup: "User Instance feature is not supported on this version of SQL Server" Cause : SQL Server User Instance mode deprecated in SQL Server 2012+ Solution : Create databases manually in SQL Server: CREATE DATABASE Shop ; CREATE DATABASE aspnetdb ; Update connection strings in Web.config : Run database schema scripts (if provided in /Database folder) Issue 2: NuGet Package Restore Fails Symptom : Error: "Unable to find version '2.1.0' of package 'NHibernate'" Cause : Old NuGet package versions may not be available on default NuGet.org feed Solution : Add fallback package source in Visual Studio: Tools → NuGet Package Manager → Package Manager Settings Package Sources → Add new source Name: "NuGet v2", Source: https://packages.nuget.org/api/v2/ Manually download packages (last resort): Search https://www.nuget.org/packages for specific versions Download .nupkg files Place in local folder, add as package source Issue 3: Build Warnings About Obsolete APIs Symptom : Warnings like "System.Web.Mvc.Html.LinkExtensions.ActionLink is obsolete" Cause : .NET Framework 3.5/4.0 APIs have obsolete warnings in modern Visual Studio Solution : Ignore for now - these warnings are expected in legacy codebase. docs.text: Agathas.Storefront is an e-commerce platform currently undergoing modernization from legacy ASP.NET MVC 2 (.NET Framework 3.5/4.0, circa 2010) to modern .NET 6+/ASP.NET Core with cloud-native capabilities. Current State : - 7 Visual Studio projects in layered architecture (Presentation, Controllers, Services, Domain, Data Access, Infrastructure) - Domain-Driven Design with excellent aggregate boundaries (Product, Basket, Order, Customer) - 6,104 lines of code across 192 classes - Zero automated tests (this is changing - Phase 1 priority!) - Manual deployment to IIS on Windows Modernization Phases : 1. Phase 1 (CURRENT): Establish testing foundation, eliminate critical vulnerabilities 2. Phase 2 : Cloud migration with containerization, managed database, responsive design 3. Phase 3 : Framework modernization (.NET 6+, ASP.NET Core, EF Core) 4. Phase 4 : Optimization and feature enhancement Your Role : Help modernize this well-architected application while preserving its excellent domain model Key Documents for Developers : 1. System Architecture (45 min) - Understand layered architecture and patterns 2. Business Domain Model (30 min) - Understand business logic and aggregates 3. GLOSSARY.md (reference) - Terminology and technology definitions

docs.text: Symptom : Error on startup: "User Instance feature is not supported on this version of SQL Server" Cause : SQL Server User Instance mode deprecated in SQL Server 2012+ Solution : Create databases manually in SQL Server: CREATE DATABASE Shop ; CREATE DATABASE aspnetdb ; Update connection strings in Web.config : <!-- BEFORE --> <add name= "Shop" connectionString= "Data Source=.\SQLEXPRESS;AttachDbFilename=|DataDirectory|\Shop.mdf;User Instance=true;Integrated Security=SSPI" /> <!-- AFTER --> <add name= "Shop" connectionString= "Data Source=.\SQLEXPRESS;Initial Catalog=Shop;Integrated Security=SSPI" /> Run database schema scripts (if provided in /Database folder)

docs.text: Executive Quick Start - Agathas.Storefront Modernization Strategic overview of Agathas.Storefront modernization initiative for executive leadership and decision makers Reading Time : 5 minutes Last Updated : 2026-06-09 ⚠️ CRITICAL DISCLAIMER - READ FIRST This document provides strategic direction WITHOUT firm timeline or cost commitments. What This Document Contains ✅ Evidence-Based Findings : - Current state analysis from comprehensive codebase review (7 projects, 6,104 LOC, 192 classes) - Critical security vulnerabilities identified through dependency analysis - Compliance gaps assessed against regulatory requirements - Technology obsolescence verified through version identification ✅ Strategic Recommendations : - Logical sequencing of modernization priorities - Risk mitigation strategies with evidence - Architectural patterns for cloud-native deployment - Business value opportunities What This Document Does NOT Contain ❌ Firm Timeline Commitments : - Cannot estimate duration without: confirmed team capacity, task decomposition, velocity baseline - Required for timeline : Sprint 0 planning with assigned technical team ❌ Cost Projections : - Cannot calculate costs without: production usage patterns, cloud provider selection, resource planning - Required for costing : Usage analytics, cloud pricing quotes, team skill assessment ❌ Resource Allocation Decisions : - Cannot determine team size without: detailed task breakdown, organizational constraints - Required for staffing : Phase 1 detailed planning, skill availability assessment Recommended Use Use this document for : - ✅ Initial strategic planning discussions - ✅ Understanding relative priorities and logical sequencing - ✅ Identifying order-of-magnitude challenges - ✅ Triggering detailed planning investment DO NOT use for : - ❌ Budget allocation (requires detailed estimation) - ❌ Contract negotiations (requires confirmed scope) - ❌ Performance commitments (requires validation) - ❌ Resource headcount decisions (requires capacity planning) 🎯 Executive Summary (2 minutes) Current Situation Agathas.Storefront is a well-architected e-commerce platform built in 2010 with excellent Domain-Driven Design principles, BUT running on critically obsolete technology that poses significant business risks . Platform Profile : - Technology : .NET Framework 3.5/4.0 (2008-2010), ASP.NET MVC 2, jQuery 1.3.2 - Architecture : Clean 5-layer DDD architecture with strong design patterns - Capabilities : Complete e-commerce (catalog, cart, checkout, payment, orders) - Deployment : Single-server monolithic deployment on IIS Critical Issues : 🔴 Technology Obsolescence - CRITICAL - Issue : .NET Framework 3.5/4.0 out of mainstream support since 2016 (no security patches) - Business Impact : Security vulnerabilities, inability to recruit developers familiar with 15-year-old stack - Evidence : technology-inventory.json shows all major technologies 10-15+ years old 🔴 Security Vulnerabilities - CRITICAL - Issue : jQuery 1.3.2 has known XSS vulnerabilities (CVE-2011-4969, CVE-2012-6708, CVE-2015-9251); plaintext secrets in configuration - Business Impact : Data breach risk, regulatory non-compliance - Evidence : vulnerability-assessment.json identifies 6 critical/high vulnerabilities 🔴 GDPR Non-Compliance - CRITICAL - Issue : No data subject rights (erasure, access, portability), no consent management, no privacy controls - Business Impact : Fines up to 4% of annual revenue or €20M (whichever is greater) if serving EU customers - Evidence : compliance-status.json shows 0% GDPR compliance 🔴 Non-Responsive Design - CRITICAL - Issue : Fixed-width desktop-only design, unusable on mobile devices - Business Impact : Lost sales from 70%+ of traffic (mobile users), poor SEO ranking - Evidence : layout-patterns.json confirms CSS-based fixed layout 🟡 Cannot Scale Horizontally - HIGH - Issue : In-process session state, LocalDB file database, file-based logging - Business Impact : Growth limited to single server capacity, no resilience (single point of failure) - Evidence : state-management.json , capacity-analysis.json 🟡 Zero Automated Testing - HIGH - Issue : No unit, integration, or E2E tests in solution - Business Impact : High risk of bugs during modernization, slow development cycles - Evidence : test-coverage.json shows 0% coverage Business Impact if No Action : Security Breach Risk : - Threat : Unpatched vulnerabilities exploited by attackers - Evidence Basis : Industry data (IBM 2022 Cost of Data Breach Report: average breach cost $4.35M) - Agathas-Specific Risk : Unknown - requires security audit and penetration testing GDPR Fine Risk : - Threat : Regulatory enforcement action if serving EU customers - Evidence Basis : GDPR Article 83 - fines up to 4% annual revenue or €20M - Agathas-Specific Risk : Depends on: revenue, EU customer base, data processing activities (requires legal review) Competitive Disadvantage : - Threat : Modern competitors provide superior mobile experience and scalability - Evidence Basis : Industry standard (70%+ e-commerce traffic is mobile - Google Commerce Research 2023) - Agathas-Specific Impact : Requires traffic analytics to quantify lost mobile conversions Talent Scarcity : - Threat : Developers with .NET Framework 3.5 expertise are rare and expensive - Evidence Basis : Technology Stack Trends (Stack Overflow Developer Survey shows <5% .NET Framework usage) - Agathas-Specific Impact : Recruitment difficulty, maintenance cost increase ✅ Recommendation: Incremental Modernization to Cloud-Native Platform Strategic Direction Phased Modernization (NOT Big-Bang Rewrite) with logical sequencing: Phase 1 : Establish Foundation (safety net, eliminate critical vulnerabilities) ↓ (depends on Phase 1) Phase 2 : Cloud Migration Preparation (containerization, observability, scalability) ↓ (depends on Phase 2) Phase 3 : Framework Modernization (.NET 6+, ASP.NET Core, GDPR compliance) ↓ (depends on Phase 3) Phase 4 : Optimization & Enhancement (performance, internationalization, features) Why Incremental Approach? ✅ Preserves Business Continuity : - System remains operational throughout modernization - No "big bang" cutover with high failure risk - Can pause/adjust based on business priorities ✅ Delivers Value Incrementally : - Phase 1 eliminates critical vulnerabilities immediately - Phase 2 enables scalability and cloud benefits - Phase 3 completes technology modernization - Each phase delivers measurable business value ✅ Reduces Risk : - Smaller changes are easier to test and validate - Learn and adapt between phases - Rollback easier if issues arise ✅ Preserves Excellent Domain Model : - No need to recreate rich business logic - Domain-Driven Design architecture remains intact - Business rules (40+ documented) preserved Why Incremental Approach? (continued) Alternative Considered: Big-Bang Rewrite ❌ Why NOT Recommended : - Risk : Complete system replacement with no fallback - Duration : Long delivery cycle (9-18+ months typical for rewrites) - Value : No business value until final cutover - Cost : Higher total cost due to maintaining both systems - Knowledge : Risk of losing business rules during recreation Decision Rationale : Agathas.Storefront has excellent architecture and complete business logic. Incremental approach preserves these assets while modernizing technology foundation. 💰 Business Case Benefits of Modernization Benefit Category Description Expected Value 1. Risk Mitigation - Security Eliminate critical vulnerabilities, update to supported frameworks Avoid data breach costs (industry avg: $4.35M per breach - IBM 2022 report). Agathas-specific risk requires security audit. 2. Compliance Achievement Implement GDPR requirements (data subject rights, consent) Avoid GDPR fines (up to 4% revenue or €20M). Agathas-specific exposure depends on EU customer base. 3. Revenue Protection - Mobile Responsive design enables mobile shopping experience Improve mobile conversion . Industry shows 70%+ traffic is mobile. Agathas baseline requires analytics implementation. 4. Scalability & Growth Horizontal scaling enables business expansion Remove growth bottleneck . Current single-server limit unknown (requires capacity testing). 5. Operational Efficiency CI/CD automation reduces deployment time and errors Faster time-to-market . Current manual deployment (estimated 2-4 hours) → automated (<15 min) is standard industry practice. 6. Developer Productivity Modern tools and frameworks improve development speed Strategic capability . Quantification requires baseline velocity measurement. 7. Cloud Capabilities Auto-scaling, managed services, global reach Strategic capability . Enables future innovation (AI/ML, advanced analytics, global expansion). ⚠️ Benefit Quantification Disclaimer : - Security/Compliance : Risk avoidance values based on industry benchmarks, NOT Agathas-specific calculations - Revenue Impact : Requires baseline measurement through analytics implementation (Phase 2) - Operational Efficiency : Time savings measurable post-implementation, ROI requires team capacity costs - Strategic Capabilities : Qualitative benefits enabling future opportunities Cost Avoidance Risks Mitigated by Modernization : Risk Avoided Assessment Basis Data Breach HIGH risk Multiple critical vulnerabilities identified (jQuery CVEs, plaintext secrets, outdated .NET). Industry avg cost: $4.35M (IBM 2022). Agathas-specific: Requires security audit. GDPR Fines HIGH risk (if EU customers) Non-compliant with all major GDPR requirements. Max fine: 4% revenue or €20M. Agathas-specific: Requires legal review of data processing and customer base. Service Outage MEDIUM risk Single point of failure architecture, no high availability. Impact: Lost revenue during downtime. Quantification requires: Average revenue/hour × MTTR. Technology Lock-In HIGH risk (increasing) Obsolete stack limits vendor options, cloud migration. Cost: Opportunity cost of cloud efficiencies, recruitment premium for legacy skills. ⚠️ Risk Quantification Disclaimer : - Probabilities : Based on industry patterns and architecture analysis, NOT Agathas-specific incident history - Costs : Based on industry benchmarks, NOT Agathas-specific financial data - Validation Required : Actual risk profile depends on threat modeling, security assessment, business impact analysis Investment Required Investment Estimation : Cannot be calculated without detailed planning because: Team Capacity Unknown : How many developers available? What skill levels (junior/mid/senior)? What percentage of time dedicated to modernization vs. maintenance? Internal team vs. external contractors vs. hybrid? Task Complexity Uncertain : Each phase requires detailed technical spike to estimate effort Integration complexity with external systems (PayPal, Janrain, SMTP) Testing scope and validation requirements Deployment risk and rollback procedures Organizational Factors : Change approval process duration Stakeholder availability for decisions Testing/QA requirements and cycles Deployment windows and blackout periods Cloud Provider Selection : Azure, AWS, GCP pricing varies significantly Usage patterns determine actual costs (not determinable from static analysis) Reserved capacity vs. on-demand pricing strategy Recommended Approach for Budgeting : Step 1 : Sprint 0 Investment (Planning Sprint) - Assemble technical team (2-3 architects, 1-2 senior developers) - Conduct detailed Phase 1 task breakdown - Create estimation baseline - Duration: 2 weeks - Cost: Team capacity cost for 2 weeks (calculable once team assigned) Step 2 : Establish Velocity Baseline (First 2-3 Sprints) - Execute initial Phase 1 work - Measure actual velocity (story points or features completed per sprint) - Identify unforeseen complexities - Duration: 4-6 weeks - Cost: Team capacity cost + any required tools/licenses Step 3 : Forecast Remaining Work - Use measured velocity to project Phase 1 completion - Refine Phase 2 estimates based on learnings - Create confidence intervals (best case/expected/worst case) - Update regularly based on continued velocity measurements Step 4 : Iterative Budget Refinement - Re-plan and re-estimate each subsequent phase - Adjust based on discovered complexity - Decision points before each phase commitment Alternative Estimation Approaches Considered : ❌ Industry Benchmarks ("similar projects cost $X"): - Why not used: Every codebase, team, and organization is different - Risk: Under/over-estimation by 100-300% is common with generic benchmarks - Agathas-specific factors: Excellent architecture reduces effort, but zero tests increases risk ❌ Function Point Analysis : - Why not used: Requires detailed functional requirements for each change - Effort: Analysis itself requires significant investment - Accuracy: ±50% typical for modernization projects (too wide for commitment) ❌ Vendor Fixed-Price Quote : - Why not used: Vendors price in significant risk premium (often 30-50% contingency) - Risk: Change orders for unforeseen work add cost - Quality: Fixed-price incentivizes minimum viable work 🎯 Modernization Priorities Phase 1: Establish Foundation (PREREQUISITE FOR ALL OTHER WORK) Strategic Objective : Create safety net and eliminate critical vulnerabilities Key Technical Tasks (WHAT, not WHEN): 1a. Testing Infrastructure - HIGHEST PRIORITY - Implement unit testing framework (xUnit/NUnit) - Create test data factories for domain entities - Write tests for 40+ documented business rules - Integration tests for repository layer - E2E tests for critical workflows (checkout, order placement) - Target: 60%+ coverage of critical paths Why This First : Without tests, all subsequent modernization work carries unacceptable regression risk. The excellent domain model architecture makes testing straightforward. 1b. CI/CD Pipeline - Automated build on every commit - Automated test execution - Build artifact generation - Deployment to test environment Why This Second : Enables rapid feedback on code changes, required for iterative modernization approach. 1c. Security Vulnerabilities - Update jQuery 1.3.2 → 3.6+ (eliminates XSS CVEs) - Encrypt secrets in Web.config (move to Key Vault or environment variables) - Remove SQL Server User Instance mode (use standard connection strings) - Implement secure password hashing (migrate ASP.NET Membership) Why This Third : Eliminates immediate security threats, can be done with test safety net in place. 1d. Scalability Enablement - Externalize session state (SQL Server Session State Provider or Redis) - Implement distributed caching foundation - Add health check endpoints - Structured logging (Serilog with JSON format) Why This Fourth : Removes technical blockers for horizontal scaling, prerequisite for cloud migration. Expected Outcomes (Phase 1) : - ✅ Automated test safety net operational - ✅ CI/CD pipeline running - ✅ Critical XSS vulnerabilities eliminated - ✅ Secrets encrypted - ✅ Horizontal scaling capability enabled - ✅ Modern logging in place Phase 2: Cloud Migration Preparation (Depends on Phase 1) Strategic Objective : Enable cloud deployment with scalability and observability Key Technical Tasks : - Containerize application (Docker) - Implement comprehensive health checks - Add APM instrumentation (Application Insights / New Relic / Datadog) - Implement distributed caching (Redis or cloud-native) - Migrate database to managed service (Azure SQL / RDS / Cloud SQL) - Implement responsive design (mobile-first) Expected Outcomes (Phase 2) : - ✅ Application runs in containers - ✅ Production observability enabled (APM, metrics, tracing) - ✅ Database cloud-compatible - ✅ Horizontal auto-scaling functional - ✅ Mobile experience dramatically improved Business Value Delivery (Phase 2) : - Revenue protection: Mobile conversion improvement (measurable post-implementation) - Scalability: Growth no longer constrained by single-server limits - Resilience: High availability architecture (99.9% SLA achievable) - Operational visibility: APM enables proactive issue detection Phase 3: Framework Modernization (Depends on Phase 2) Strategic Objective : Eliminate technology debt, achieve full compliance Key Technical Tasks : - Migrate to .NET 6+ or .NET 8 LTS (latest Long-Term Support) - Migrate ASP.NET MVC 2 → ASP.NET Core MVC - Migrate NHibernate → Entity Framework Core - Replace StructureMap with built-in ASP.NET Core DI - Implement modern authentication (ASP.NET Core Identity or external IdP) - Implement GDPR compliance (data subject rights, consent management) Expected Outcomes (Phase 3) : - ✅ Modern, fully supported technology stack - ✅ Cross-platform capability (Linux containers) - ✅ GDPR compliance achieved (EU customer support) - ✅ All security vulnerabilities eliminated - ✅ Recruitment feasibility improved (modern stack attracts developers) Business Value Delivery (Phase 3) : - Compliance: GDPR fine risk eliminated - Security: All vulnerabilities addressed - Operational: Ongoing security patch support restored - Strategic: Modern platform enables innovation Phase 4: Optimization & Enhancement (Depends on Phase 3) Strategic Objective : Maximize performance and expand capabilities Key Technical Tasks : - Performance optimization based on APM data - Advanced caching strategies (output cache, distributed cache) - Internationalization (i18n) support for global expansion - Comprehensive monitoring dashboards - Advanced security features (CSP, HSTS, rate limiting) - Missing business capabilities (inventory management, returns processing) Expected Outcomes (Phase 4) : - ✅ Performance optimized (measured via APM) - ✅ International expansion capability (multi-language, multi-currency) - ✅ Comprehensive operational dashboards - ✅ Enhanced security posture (defense-in-depth) - ✅ Feature completeness for competitive differentiation 📊 Success Metrics How We'll Measure Success Security Metrics : - Critical vulnerabilities: 6 identified → Target: 0 - Dependency CVEs: 3 (jQuery) → Target: 0 - GDPR compliance: 0% → Target: 100% (Phase 3) Operational Metrics : - Deployment time: Manual (hours) → Target: Automated (<15 min) - Scalability: 1 server max → Target: Auto-scale 2-10+ instances - Uptime SLA: ~95-98% (single server estimate) → Target: 99.9% (Phase 2) Technical Metrics : - Automated test coverage: 0% → Target: 60%+ (Phase 1), 80%+ (Phase 3) - Technology stack age: 15+ years → Target: <2 years (current LTS) - 12-Factor compliance: 3/12 (25%) → Target: 11/12 (92%) Business Metrics (Measurable Post-Implementation): - Mobile conversion rate: Baseline TBD → Target: 30-50% improvement (industry benchmark) - Page load time: Baseline TBD → Target: <2 seconds (industry best practice) - Deployment frequency: Monthly (manual) → Target: Daily or multiple/day ⚠️ Metrics Disclaimer : - Current Baselines : Most baselines unknown (require monitoring implementation in Phase 2) - Target Rationale : Based on industry best practices and cloud provider capabilities - Validation : Actual results will vary based on implementation quality and usage patterns 🎬 Recommended Next Steps For Executive Leadership Immediate Actions : 1. ✅ Review full documentation suite : - EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY.md for comprehensive findings (15 min) - Modernization Executive Summary for detailed strategy (25 min) ✅ Assess business priorities : Is mobile conversion improvement a priority? docs.text: Strategic Objective : Create safety net and eliminate critical vulnerabilities Key Technical Tasks (WHAT, not WHEN): 1a. Testing Infrastructure - HIGHEST PRIORITY - Implement unit testing framework (xUnit/NUnit) - Create test data factories for domain entities - Write tests for 40+ documented business rules - Integration tests for repository layer - E2E tests for critical workflows (checkout, order placement) - Target: 60%+ coverage of critical paths Why This First : Without tests, all subsequent modernization work carries unacceptable regression risk. The excellent domain model architecture makes testing straightforward. 1b. CI/CD Pipeline - Automated build on every commit - Automated test execution - Build artifact generation - Deployment to test environment Why This Second : Enables rapid feedback on code changes, required for iterative modernization approach. 1c. Security Vulnerabilities - Update jQuery 1.3.2 → 3.6+ (eliminates XSS CVEs) - Encrypt secrets in Web.config (move to Key Vault or environment variables) - Remove SQL Server User Instance mode (use standard connection strings) - Implement secure password hashing (migrate ASP.NET Membership) Why This Third : Eliminates immediate security threats, can be done with test safety net in place. 1d. Scalability Enablement - Externalize session state (SQL Server Session State Provider or Redis) - Implement distributed caching foundation - Add health check endpoints - Structured logging (Serilog with JSON format) Why This Fourth : Removes technical blockers for horizontal scaling, prerequisite for cloud migration. Expected Outcomes (Phase 1) : - ✅ Automated test safety net operational - ✅ CI/CD pipeline running - ✅ Critical XSS vulnerabilities eliminated - ✅ Secrets encrypted - ✅ Horizontal scaling capability enabled - ✅ Modern logging in place

docs.text: System Architecture - Agathas.Storefront This document provides a comprehensive architectural overview using the C4 model (Context, Container, Component, Code), detailing the system's structure, design patterns, quality attributes, and architectural decisions. Table of Contents Executive Summary C4 Architecture Diagrams Level 1: System Context Diagram Level 2: Container Diagram Level 3: Component Diagram Level 4: Code Structure Architectural Patterns Architectural Characteristics Technology Stack Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) Technical Debt Analysis Appendix Executive Summary Agathas.Storefront is a classic ASP.NET MVC 2 e-commerce web application built on .NET Framework 3.5/4.0, representing a well-architected monolithic system following Domain-Driven Design principles and layered architecture patterns. The system was designed and implemented circa 2010, demonstrating mature software engineering practices for that era. The application implements a complete online storefront with product catalog browsing, shopping basket functionality, customer account management, order processing, and payment integration with PayPal. The architecture exhibits excellent separation of concerns through a 5-layer structure: Presentation (ASP.NET MVC), Business Logic (Services), Domain Model, Data Access (NHibernate), and Infrastructure (cross-cutting concerns). Despite being built with now-legacy technologies, the codebase demonstrates high-quality architectural patterns including Repository pattern, Unit of Work, Dependency Injection (StructureMap), Domain Events, Factory pattern, and State pattern. The strong architectural foundation provides a solid base for modernization efforts, though significant technology upgrades are required to address obsolescence and security concerns. Technology Stack Summary: - Platform: .NET Framework 3.5 / 4.0 - Language: C# 3.5 / 4.0 - Architecture Style: Layered Architecture with Domain-Driven Design (N-Tier Monolith) - Database: SQL Server Express LocalDB (User Instance mode) - ORM: NHibernate 2.1 with HBM.XML mappings - Client Technology: ASP.NET MVC 2, ASPX Views, jQuery 1.3.2 - Integration: HTTP POST (PayPal), OAuth-style callback (Janrain), SMTP (Email) - Dependency Injection: StructureMap 2.5 C4 Architecture Diagrams Level 1: System Context Diagram Shows the system's relationship with users and external systems C4Context
