docs.text: Business Purpose: Allow customers to create accounts, manage profiles, and save delivery addresses. Actors: Customer, Anonymous User (for registration) Workflow Steps: Registration Flow: sequenceDiagram actor User participant Register participant Validation participant Customer participant Membership participant Email User->>Register: Click "Register" Register->>User: Display Registration Form User->>Register: Submit Email, Password, Name Register->>Validation: Validate Email Uniqueness alt Email Already Exists Validation->>User: Error: Email Taken else Email Available Validation->>Customer: Create Customer Entity Customer->>Membership: Create Membership Account Membership->>Email: Send Welcome Email (if configured) Membership->>User: Auto-Login + Redirect end Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom Login Flow: sequenceDiagram actor User participant Login participant LocalAuth participant SocialAuth participant Session User->>Login: Navigate to Login Page alt Local Authentication User->>LocalAuth: Enter Email + Password LocalAuth->>LocalAuth: Validate Credentials LocalAuth->>Session: Create Auth Cookie else Social Authentication User->>SocialAuth: Click Social Provider (Janrain) SocialAuth->>SocialAuth: Redirect to Provider SocialAuth->>SocialAuth: Receive Auth Token SocialAuth->>Session: Create Auth Cookie end Session->>User: Redirect to Original Page Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom Profile Management: - View/Edit customer profile (name, email) - Add/edit/delete delivery addresses - View order history Business Rules: 1. Email must be unique across all customers 2. Email must be valid format 3. Password must meet minimum strength requirements (defined in membership provider) 4. At least one delivery address required for checkout 5. Address must have all required fields (street, city, postcode, name) Implementation: - Controllers: AccountRegisterController , AccountLogOnController , CustomerController - Services: CustomerService.CreateCustomer() , CustomerService.AddDeliveryAddress() - Authentication: ASP.NET Forms Authentication + Janrain social auth - Validation: EmailValidationSpecification , AddressBusinessRules Business Value: Customer retention, streamlined repeat purchases
docs.title: 3.4 Account Management Workflow

docs.text: Business Purpose: Enable customers to track order history and review past purchases. Actors: Registered Customer Trigger: Customer navigates to "My Orders" Workflow Steps: sequenceDiagram actor Customer participant Orders participant OrderService participant OrderDetail Customer->>Orders: Click "My Orders" Orders->>OrderService: GetOrdersForCustomer(customerId) OrderService->>Orders: Return Order List Orders->>Customer: Display Order History Customer->>OrderDetail: Click Order OrderDetail->>OrderService: GetOrderDetail(orderId) OrderService->>OrderDetail: Return Order + Items + Payment OrderDetail->>Customer: Display Order Details Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom Displayed Information: - Order date and order number - Order status (Submitted) - Items ordered (product, size, color, quantity, price) - Shipping method and cost - Payment amount and date - Delivery address Business Rules: - Customers can only view their own orders - Order history sorted by date (newest first) - Order details immutable (display only) Implementation: - Controller: OrderController.Index() , OrderController.Detail() - Service: OrderService.GetOrdersForCustomer() - Repository: OrderRepository.FindBy() with customer filter Business Value: Customer service, transparency, reduces support inquiries
docs.title: 3.5 Order Management Workflow

docs.text: Business Purpose: Securely process customer payments through external payment provider. Actors: Customer, PayPal Payment Gateway, System Integration Pattern: Server-to-Server with Browser Redirect Workflow Steps: sequenceDiagram actor Customer participant Storefront participant PayPal participant PayPalCallback participant Order Storefront->>Customer: Display Order Summary Customer->>Storefront: Click "Pay Now" Storefront->>Storefront: Generate PayPal Form Storefront->>Customer: Auto-Submit Form to PayPal Customer->>PayPal: Browser Redirect (POST) PayPal->>Customer: Display Payment UI Customer->>PayPal: Enter Payment Method PayPal->>PayPal: Process Payment PayPal->>PayPalCallback: Callback with Result PayPalCallback->>Order: Update Order with Payment alt Payment Success Order->>Order: SetPayment() → Submit() Order->>Customer: Confirmation Page else Payment Cancelled Order->>Customer: Basket Page (retry) else Payment Failed Order->>Customer: Error Page end Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom Payment Request Data Sent to PayPal: - Business email (merchant account) - Order total amount - Currency code - Item details (name, quantity, amount) - Return URL (success) - Cancel URL (cancel/failure) - Notify URL (IPN callback - not implemented) Payment Response Handling: - Success: PaymentController.Callback() receives transaction ID and amount - Validation: System validates amount matches order total - Order Update: Order.SetPayment() creates Payment value object - State Transition: Order state changes to PaymentReceived → Submitted - Email: OrderSubmittedEvent triggers confirmation email Business Rules: 1. Payment amount must exactly match order total 2. No credit card data stored in application (PCI DSS compliance via delegation) 3. Cannot change order after payment received 4. Payment transaction ID captured for reconciliation 5. Payment provider is PayPal (configurable via Web.config) Implementation: - Controller: PaymentController - Service: PayPalPaymentService (in Infrastructure layer) - Configuration: PayPal endpoint and business email in Web.config - Security: HTTPS required for payment processing Business Value: Secure payment processing, PCI DSS compliance delegation, customer trust
docs.title: 3.6 Payment Processing Workflow

docs.text: graph TD A[Product Browsing] --> B[Shopping/Basket] B --> C{Authenticated?} C -->|No| D[Account Registration/Login] C -->|Yes| E[Checkout] D --> E E --> F[Payment Processing] F -->|Success| G[Order Created] F -->|Failure| B G --> H[Order Management] style A fill:#e1f5ff style B fill:#e1f5ff style D fill:#fff4e1 style E fill:#ffe1e1 style F fill:#ffe1e1 style G fill:#e1ffe1 style H fill:#e1ffe1 Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom Workflow Characteristics: - Linear Progression: Most workflows follow a linear path (browsing → basket → checkout → payment → confirmation) - Registration Gate: Checkout requires authentication (registration or login) - Stateful Operations: Basket state persists across sessions (cookie storage) - External Dependencies: Payment workflow depends on PayPal availability - Error Handling: Payment failures return user to basket for retry

docs.text: The system implements comprehensive business rules encapsulated within domain entities and dedicated business rule classes. Business rules are enforced at the domain layer, ensuring data integrity and business logic consistency.
docs.title: 4. Business Rules Catalog

docs.text: Architecture Pattern: Dedicated business rule classes that encapsulate validation and business logic separate from domain entities. Implementation Approach: - BusinessRule<T> base class provides validation framework - Dedicated rule classes per aggregate: BasketBusinessRules , OrderBusinessRules , CustomerBusinessRules , AddressBusinessRules - Specification pattern for complex validations: EmailValidationSpecification - Rules invoked from domain entity methods before state changes Rule Enforcement Locations: 1. Domain Entities: Rules embedded in entity methods (e.g., Basket.Add() , Order.SetPayment() ) 2. Business Rule Classes: Dedicated classes in Agathas.Storefront.Model namespace 3. Validation Specifications: Specification pattern classes for reusable validations 4. Service Layer: Workflow-level validations in service implementations
docs.title: 4.1 Business Rule Organization

IncreaseItemQtyBy ( 1 ); // BR-BSK-001 else _items . Add ( BasketItemFactory . CreateItemFor ( product , this )); } public decimal BasketTotal // BR-BSK-003 { get { return ItemsTotal + DeliveryCost (); } }

docs.text: 🔴 CRITICAL Rules: Must never be violated; system integrity depends on these - Payment amount validation - No duplicate payments - Order immutability after payment - No card data storage - Price calculation accuracy 🟡 HIGH Rules: Important for business operations; violations cause significant issues - Unique email addresses - Delivery option requirement - Authentication before checkout - Address validation 🔵 MEDIUM Rules: Enhance user experience and data quality; violations are tolerable - Email format validation - Profile required fields - Product variant attributes
docs.title: 4.11 Business Rule Priority Classification

docs.text: Validation Strategy: 1. Pre-condition Validation: Rules checked before domain operations 2. Domain Exceptions: InvalidOperationException thrown for rule violations 3. Service Layer Validation: Workflow-level checks in service methods 4. UI Validation: Client-side and server-side form validation Error Communication: - Domain exceptions caught by controllers - Error messages displayed to user via view models - Validation failures prevent state changes - Transaction rollback on validation failures (via UnitOfWork)
docs.title: 4.12 Business Rule Violations and Error Handling

docs.text: The system implements a Domain Events pattern for cross-aggregate coordination and side effects, enabling loose coupling between domain concerns.
docs.title: 5. Domain Events

docs.text: Pattern Implementation: In-process synchronous domain events using static dispatcher Purpose: Decouple order submission from email notification, allowing the order aggregate to remain focused on order management while external concerns (email) are handled by separate handlers. Architecture: graph LR A[Order.Submit] --> B[Raise OrderSubmittedEvent] B --> C[DomainEvents Dispatcher] C --> D[OrderSubmittedHandler] D --> E[IEmailService] E --> F[Send Confirmation Email] Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom Key Characteristics: - Execution Model: Synchronous in-process (not message queue) - Transaction Scope: Handlers execute within the same transaction as the domain operation - Registration: Handlers registered via StructureMap IoC container - Dispatch: Static DomainEvents.Raise<T>() method
docs.title: 5.1 Domain Events Overview

docs.text: Location: Agathas.Storefront.Model.Orders.Events.OrderSubmittedEvent Purpose: Notifies the system that an order has been successfully submitted and paid. Trigger: When order transitions to Submitted state via Order.State.Submit() Event Data: - Complete Order aggregate (Order entity with items, payment, shipping) - Customer information - Order timestamp - Payment confirmation Handlers: Handler Action Purpose Transaction OrderSubmittedHandler Sends order confirmation email Customer notification Same transaction Handler Implementation: // From OrderSubmittedHandler.cs (in Agathas.Storefront.Services.DomainEventHandlers) public class OrderSubmittedHandler : IDomainEventHandler < OrderSubmittedEvent > { private readonly IEmailService _emailService ; public void Handle ( OrderSubmittedEvent args ) { _emailService . SendOrderConfirmation ( args . Order ); } } Event Raising Location: // From Order.cs - Submitted state public void Submit () { _order . State = OrderStates . Submitted ; DomainEvents . Raise ( new OrderSubmittedEvent ( _order )); // Event raised here } Business Impact: - Ensures customers receive order confirmation immediately after payment - Decouples order domain logic from email infrastructure - Allows additional handlers to be added without modifying Order entity
docs.title: OrderSubmittedEvent

docs.text: Dispatcher: DomainEvents static class (in Agathas.Storefront.Infrastructure.Domain ) Handler Interface: public interface IDomainEventHandler < T > where T : IDomainEvent { void Handle ( T args ); } Handler Factory: IDomainEventHandlerFactory resolves handlers from IoC container (StructureMap) Registration: // From StructureMap registry For < IDomainEventHandler < OrderSubmittedEvent >> () . Use < OrderSubmittedHandler > (); Execution Flow: 1. Domain entity raises event: DomainEvents.Raise(new OrderSubmittedEvent(order)) 2. Dispatcher resolves handlers from factory: _factory.GetHandlersFor<OrderSubmittedEvent>() 3. Each handler executed synchronously: handler.Handle(eventArgs) 4. Execution within same transaction as domain operation 5. Transaction commits only if all handlers succeed
docs.title: 5.3 Domain Event Infrastructure

docs.text: When to Use Domain Events: ✅ Use for: - Cross-aggregate coordination (e.g., Order → Email notification) - Side effects that should happen "when X happens" (e.g., "when order submitted, send email") - Decoupling domain logic from infrastructure concerns - Audit logging and event sourcing (future) - Workflow orchestration across aggregates ❌ Don't Use for: - Intra-aggregate operations (use direct method calls) - External API calls that could fail independently (use message queue instead) - Long-running operations (current synchronous implementation blocks transaction)
docs.title: 5.4 Domain Events Usage Pattern

docs.text: Domain events play a critical role in the order submission workflow: sequenceDiagram participant Client participant OrderService participant Order participant DomainEvents participant OrderSubmittedHandler participant EmailService Client->>OrderService: SubmitOrder(orderId) OrderService->>Order: SetPayment(payment) Order->>Order: State = PaymentReceived OrderService->>Order: Submit() Order->>Order: State = Submitted Order->>DomainEvents: Raise(OrderSubmittedEvent) DomainEvents->>OrderSubmittedHandler: Handle(event) OrderSubmittedHandler->>EmailService: SendOrderConfirmation(order) EmailService-->>OrderSubmittedHandler: Email sent OrderSubmittedHandler-->>DomainEvents: Completed DomainEvents-->>Order: Event handled Order-->>OrderService: Order submitted OrderService->>OrderService: UnitOfWork.Commit() OrderService-->>Client: Success Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom Transaction Boundary: All operations (order state change + email sending) occur within single transaction. If email fails, order submission rolls back.

docs.text: Current Maturity Level: 🟡 Basic Implementation Strengths: - ✅ Clean pattern implementation with dispatcher and handlers - ✅ Proper separation of concerns (Order doesn't know about Email) - ✅ Extensible design (easy to add new handlers) - ✅ IoC container integration for handler resolution Limitations: - ⚠️ Only one event implemented (underutilized pattern) - ⚠️ Synchronous execution (blocks transaction, could cause issues with slow external services) - ⚠️ No event persistence (events lost if system crashes) - ⚠️ No retry mechanism if handler fails - ⚠️ Email failure causes order submission to fail (tight coupling despite event pattern) Modernization Opportunities: - Implement asynchronous event handling with message queue (e.g., Azure Service Bus, RabbitMQ) - Add event sourcing for audit trail and replay capability - Implement eventual consistency for non-critical handlers - Add retry and dead-letter queue for failed events - Persist events for analysis and debugging

docs.text: These are fundamental truths that must always hold across the system: Invariant Description Enforcement Criticality INV-001: Order-Payment Consistency Order total always equals payment amount for paid orders Domain validation in Order.SetPayment() 🔴 CRITICAL INV-002: Basket-Order Transformation Every order originates from a basket Service layer validation 🔴 CRITICAL INV-003: Customer-Order Association Every order belongs to exactly one customer Database foreign key + domain model 🔴 CRITICAL INV-004: Price Non-Negativity All prices (product, shipping, total) must be ≥ 0 Domain entity property validation 🔴 CRITICAL INV-005: Quantity Positivity All quantities (basket, order items) must be > 0 Domain entity property validation 🔴 CRITICAL INV-006: Email Uniqueness Each customer email is unique Database unique constraint + membership provider 🟡 HIGH INV-007: State Machine Integrity Order state transitions follow defined path State pattern implementation 🟡 HIGH INV-008: Aggregate Boundary Isolation Aggregates reference each other by ID only Domain model design 🔵 MEDIUM
docs.title: 6.1 System-Wide Invariants

docs.text: Basket Aggregate: - Basket contains zero or more items (empty basket is valid) - Each basket item references a valid product - Delivery option is optional until checkout - Basket totals are derived, never stored Order Aggregate: - Order must have at least one order item - Order items are immutable after order creation - Payment is optional until submission (null for unpaid orders) - Order state is always valid (Open, PaymentReceived, or Submitted) - Created timestamp is immutable Customer Aggregate: - Customer must have valid email address - Customer can have zero or more delivery addresses - Delivery addresses belong to exactly one customer Product Aggregate: - ProductTitle must have a price > 0 - Product must reference a valid ProductTitle - Product must have size and color

docs.text: Pattern: State Pattern for order status management Implementation: Agathas.Storefront.Model/Orders/States/ Business Value: Ensures orders follow valid lifecycle transitions, preventing invalid operations (e.g., cannot pay twice, cannot modify after payment). State Diagram: stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Open: CreateOrder() Open --> PaymentReceived: SetPayment() PaymentReceived --> Submitted: Submit() Submitted --> [*] note right of Open: Editable, no payment note right of PaymentReceived: Paid, not yet submitted note right of Submitted: Complete, immutable Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom State Classes: - IOrderState interface defines allowed operations - OpenState - allows payment - PaymentReceivedState - allows submission - SubmittedState - terminal state, no further operations Business Operations by State: Operation Open PaymentReceived Submitted SetPayment() ✅ Allowed ❌ Denied ❌ Denied Submit() ❌ Denied ✅ Allowed ❌ Denied Modify Items ✅ Allowed ❌ Denied ❌ Denied
docs.title: 8.1 State Machine Pattern (Order Lifecycle)

docs.text: Pattern: Long-running business transaction spanning multiple aggregates Implementation: Orchestrated by OrderService and CheckoutController Steps: 1. Validate Basket - Ensure basket has items and delivery option 2. Authenticate Customer - Verify user logged in 3. Create Order - Convert basket to order aggregate 4. Process Payment - Redirect to PayPal, await callback 5. Submit Order - Update order state, trigger domain event 6. Send Confirmation - Email sent via event handler Compensation Logic: - Payment failure → Return to basket (order not saved) - Payment cancelled → Return to basket - Email failure → Order still submitted (email is best-effort) Transaction Boundaries: - Basket validation: Read-only - Order creation: Transaction - Payment processing: External (PayPal transaction) - Order submission + email: Single transaction (synchronous domain event)

docs.text: Pattern: Strategy Pattern for different delivery/shipping options Implementation: DeliveryOption entity with associated ShippingService Business Purpose: Different delivery methods (Standard, Express, Next-Day) with varying costs Usage: basket . docs.text: 2.2 Requirements Specification Document Version: 1.0 Date: 2026-06-09 Status: Current State Analysis (Reverse-Engineered) Standard: Based on IEEE 29148-2018 (Requirements Engineering) Executive Summary This document captures the functional and non-functional requirements of the Agathas Storefront e-commerce platform as implemented in the current system. Requirements have been reverse-engineered from source code, user interfaces, configuration files, and system behavior analysis. Key Findings: - Total Requirements Identified: 85+ functional and non-functional requirements - Requirements Coverage: Core e-commerce functionality well-implemented; advanced features (inventory, returns, internationalization) not present - Requirements Maturity: Basic e-commerce requirements fully met; scalability and compliance requirements partially met - Business Priority: Customer-facing transaction workflows (browse, basket, checkout) prioritized over administrative features Requirements Distribution: Category Requirements Implementation Status Functional Requirements 55 80% Complete Non-Functional Requirements 20 65% Complete User Interface Requirements 10 75% Complete Data Requirements 5 90% Complete Integration Requirements 5 100% Complete Compliance Requirements 8 40% Complete 1. Functional Requirements 1.1 Product Catalog Management FR-PC-001: Product Browsing Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to browse products organized by categories and brands. Acceptance Criteria: - Products displayed in hierarchical category structure - Featured products shown on home page - Product listings show image, name, price - Category navigation via menu and breadcrumbs Implementation: - Controller: ProductController.Index() - Service: ProductCatalogService.GetProductsByCategory() - View: Views/Product/Index.aspx Traceability: Maps to User Journey "Product Discovery" in Business Domain Model FR-PC-002: Product Filtering and Refinement Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to filter product listings by size, color, brand, and price range. Acceptance Criteria: - Filter options displayed in sidebar - Filter combinations applied using AND logic - Filtered results update product listing - Filter state persists during browsing session Implementation: - Service: ProductSearchRequestQueryGenerator generates NHibernate queries from filter criteria - JSON: JsonProductSearchRequest captures filter selections - Query: Dynamic NHibernate criteria queries Traceability: Supports business capability "Product Discovery" FR-PC-003: Product Detail View Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to view detailed information for a specific product including all available variants. Acceptance Criteria: - Product image, name, description, price displayed - All size and color combinations shown - Add to basket functionality available - Product title and variant attributes visible Implementation: - Controller: ProductController.Detail(int productId) - View: Views/Product/Detail.aspx - ViewModel: ProductView with size/color options Traceability: Essential for product selection in shopping workflow FR-PC-004: Featured Products Display Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: System shall display featured products on the home page to promote specific items. Acceptance Criteria: - Configurable featured products list - Featured products shown on landing page - Products link to detail pages Implementation: - Controller: HomeController.Index() - Service: ProductCatalogService.GetFeaturedProducts() Business Value: Marketing and promotion support 1.2 Shopping Basket Management FR-BK-001: Add Product to Basket Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to add products to their shopping basket with specified quantity. Acceptance Criteria: - Select size and color variant - Specify quantity (default: 1) - Product added to basket with confirmation - If product already in basket, quantity increased Implementation: - Controller: BasketController.Add() - Service: BasketService.AddProductToBasket() - Domain: Basket.Add() enforces no-duplicate rule - Storage: Cookie-based basket persistence Business Rule: BR-BSK-001 (No duplicate products - increases quantity instead) Traceability: Core requirement from Shopping Workflow FR-BK-002: View Basket Contents Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to view all items in their basket with quantities and prices. Acceptance Criteria: - List all basket items with product details - Show quantity per item - Display item subtotal (price × quantity) - Show basket subtotal (all items) - Show delivery cost - Show basket total (items + delivery) Implementation: - Controller: BasketController.Index() - View: Views/Basket/Index.aspx - ViewModel: BasketView with calculated totals Traceability: Required before checkout FR-BK-003: Update Item Quantity Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to increase or decrease quantities of items in the basket. Acceptance Criteria: - Quantity can be increased or decreased - Minimum quantity is 1 (removing item if decreased to 0) - Basket totals recalculate automatically - Changes persist across page loads Implementation: - Controller: BasketController.UpdateQuantity() - Service: BasketService.UpdateBasketItemQuantity() - Domain: BasketItem.IncreaseItemQtyBy() , BasketItem.DecreaseItemQtyBy() Business Rule: BR-BSK-002 (Positive quantity) FR-BK-004: Remove Item from Basket Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to remove items from their basket. Acceptance Criteria: - Remove button available per item - Item removed immediately - Basket totals recalculate - Empty basket message shown if no items remain Implementation: - Controller: BasketController.Remove(int basketItemId) - Service: BasketService.RemoveItemFromBasket() - Domain: Basket.Remove(basketItem) FR-BK-005: Select Delivery Option Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to select a delivery option with associated cost before checkout. Acceptance Criteria: - Delivery options displayed with names and costs - User selects one delivery option - Delivery cost included in basket total - Delivery option selection persists Implementation: - Controller: BasketController.SetDeliveryOption(int deliveryOptionId) - Domain: Basket.SetDeliveryOption() - Entity: DeliveryOption with pricing Business Rule: BR-BSK-004 (Delivery option required before checkout) FR-BK-006: Basket Persistence Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Basket contents shall persist across user sessions using cookie storage. Acceptance Criteria: - Basket saved in cookie after each modification - Basket restored on subsequent visits - Cookie expires after configurable period - Anonymous and authenticated users both supported Implementation: - Repository: CookieBasketRepository - Storage: ICookieStorageService - Key: CookieDataKeys.Basket Traceability: Supports user experience for interrupted shopping sessions 1.3 User Account Management FR-AC-001: Customer Registration Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: New users shall be able to create a customer account with email and password. Acceptance Criteria: - Registration form with email, password, first name, surname - Email uniqueness validation - Password strength validation - Account created in both domain (Customer) and infrastructure (Membership) - Auto-login after successful registration Implementation: - Controller: AccountRegisterController.Register() - Service: CustomerService.CreateCustomer() - Domain: Customer entity - Infrastructure: ASP.NET Membership Provider Business Rule: BR-CUS-001 (Unique email), BR-CUS-002 (Email validation) FR-AC-002: User Login Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Registered users shall be able to authenticate using email and password. Acceptance Criteria: - Login form with email and password fields - Credentials validated against membership database - Authentication cookie created on success - Redirect to originally requested page after login - Error message on failure Implementation: - Controller: AccountLogOnController.LogOn() - Service: AspMembershipAuthentication.Login() - Infrastructure: ASP.NET Forms Authentication FR-AC-003: Social Authentication Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to authenticate using social login providers (Facebook, Google, etc.) via Janrain. Acceptance Criteria: - Social login buttons displayed on login page - Redirect to Janrain authentication - Token received from Janrain on success - User account created or linked - Auto-login after social auth Implementation: - Controller: AccountLogOnController.JanrainCallback() - Service: JanrainAuthenticationService - Configuration: Janrain API key in Web.config Business Rule: BR-AUT-003 (Social auth option) FR-AC-004: User Logout Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Authenticated users shall be able to log out of their session. Acceptance Criteria: - Logout link available when authenticated - Authentication cookie cleared - Redirect to home page - Session state cleared Implementation: - Controller: AccountLogOnController.LogOut() - Infrastructure: FormsAuthentication.SignOut() FR-AC-005: Manage Delivery Addresses Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Customers shall be able to add, edit, and delete delivery addresses. Acceptance Criteria: - View list of saved delivery addresses - Add new address with street, city, postcode, name - Edit existing address - Delete address (if not only address) - Select address during checkout Implementation: - Controller: CustomerController.AddDeliveryAddress() - Service: CustomerService.AddDeliveryAddress() - Domain: Customer.AddDeliveryAddress() , DeliveryAddress entity Business Rule: BR-CUS-003 (Checkout address requirement), BR-ADR-001 (Required fields) 1.4 Checkout and Order Processing FR-CO-001: Initiate Checkout Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to proceed from basket to checkout process. Acceptance Criteria: - Checkout button available in basket view - Authentication required (redirect to login if not authenticated) - Basket must have items and delivery option selected - Checkout page displays basket summary and delivery address selection Implementation: - Controller: CheckoutController.Index() - Authorization: [Authorize] attribute enforces authentication - Validation: Delivery option and items validated Business Rule: BR-AUT-001 (Checkout authentication) FR-CO-002: Select Delivery Address Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: During checkout, customers shall select a delivery address from their saved addresses. Acceptance Criteria: - List of customer's saved addresses displayed - Customer selects one address for delivery - Address details shown (street, city, postcode) - Option to add new address if none exist Implementation: - Controller: CheckoutController.SelectAddress() - View: Address selector in checkout page - Validation: At least one address required FR-CO-003: Submit Order Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Customers shall be able to confirm and submit their order for payment. Acceptance Criteria: - Order created from basket contents - Order includes items, quantities, prices (snapshot) - Delivery address captured - Shipping service assigned - Order saved to database - Redirect to payment gateway Implementation: - Controller: CheckoutController.Submit() - Service: OrderService.CreateOrderFromBasket() - Domain: Order entity created from Basket - Mapping: BasketItem → OrderItem with price snapshot Business Rule: BR-CRS-001 (Order from basket), BR-ORD-006 (Price snapshot) FR-CO-004: Process Payment via PayPal Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Customers shall complete payment securely through PayPal payment gateway. Acceptance Criteria: - Redirect to PayPal with order details - PayPal presents payment UI - Customer completes payment - PayPal callback received with transaction status - Order updated with payment details on success Implementation: - Controller: PaymentController.Callback() - Service: PayPalPaymentService generates payment request - Domain: Order.SetPayment() captures payment - Integration: HTTPS POST to PayPal sandbox endpoint Business Rule: BR-PAY-001 (External processing), BR-PAY-004 (Amount validation), BR-ORD-002 (Payment amount match) Security: BR-PAY-002 (No card storage) FR-CO-005: Order Confirmation Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: After successful payment, customers shall receive order confirmation via email and on-screen. Acceptance Criteria: - Confirmation page displayed with order number - Order details shown (items, total, delivery address) - Confirmation email sent to customer email - Order status set to Submitted Implementation: - Controller: CheckoutController.Confirmation() - Event: OrderSubmittedEvent raised when order submitted - Handler: OrderSubmittedHandler sends email - Service: IEmailService.SendOrderConfirmation() Traceability: Completes Checkout Workflow 1.5 Order Management FR-OM-001: View Order History Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Customers shall be able to view a list of their past orders. Acceptance Criteria: - Orders displayed in reverse chronological order (newest first) - Each order shows order number, date, total, status - Click order to view details Implementation: - Controller: OrderController.Index() - Service: OrderService.GetOrdersForCustomer() - Authorization: Customers can only view own orders Traceability: Implements Order Management Workflow FR-OM-002: View Order Details Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Customers shall be able to view detailed information for a specific order. Acceptance Criteria: - Order date and order number displayed - Items ordered with product details, quantity, price - Subtotal, shipping cost, total amount - Delivery address - Payment details (amount, date, transaction ID) - Order status Implementation: - Controller: OrderController.Detail(int orderId) - Service: OrderService.GetOrderDetail() - ViewModel: OrderView with items, payment, shipping 1.6 Missing Functional Requirements (Gaps) The following functional requirements are NOT implemented but are common in e-commerce systems: Requirement ID Requirement Business Impact Priority FR-PC-005 Product Search Cannot find products by keyword 🔴 HIGH FR-PC-006 Product Recommendations Lost cross-sell opportunities 🟡 MEDIUM FR-PC-007 Product Reviews/Ratings Lack social proof, lower conversions 🟡 MEDIUM FR-BK-007 Wish List / Save for Later Lost sales from indecision 🔵 LOW FR-BK-008 Apply Promo Code Cannot run discounts/promotions 🟡 MEDIUM FR-CO-006 Guest Checkout Friction for first-time buyers 🟡 MEDIUM FR-CO-007 Multiple Payment Methods Limited payment options (PayPal only) 🟡 MEDIUM FR-OM-003 Order Tracking Cannot track shipment status 🟡 MEDIUM FR-OM-004 Order Cancellation No self-service cancellation 🔵 LOW FR-OM-005 Returns/Refunds Manual returns process 🟡 MEDIUM FR-INV-001 Inventory Management Cannot track stock levels 🔴 HIGH FR-INV-002 Out-of-Stock Notification Can accept orders without stock 🔴 HIGH FR-ADM-001 Admin Portal No administrative interface 🔴 HIGH FR-ADM-002 Product Management UI Cannot add/edit products via UI 🔴 HIGH FR-ADM-003 Order Fulfillment UI Manual order processing 🟡 MEDIUM 2. Non-Functional Requirements 2.1 Performance Requirements NFR-PERF-001: Page Load Time Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ⚠️ Partially Met Requirement: Product listing and detail pages shall load within 2 seconds under normal load. Current Performance: - No performance monitoring implemented - Server-side rendering with ASPX views (slower than modern SPAs) - No CDN for static assets - Database queries not optimized (N+1 query issues possible with NHibernate) Evidence: No Application Performance Monitoring (APM) detected in observability-setup.json Recommendation: Implement APM (Application Insights), optimize queries, add caching NFR-PERF-002: Concurrent Users Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ❌ Not Met Requirement: System shall support at least 100 concurrent users without degradation. Current Limitations: - Single-server architecture (LocalDB, in-process session) - Cannot scale horizontally - No load testing performed Evidence: From cloud-readiness.json : "Cannot scale horizontally, single-server architecture" Recommendation: Externalize state, migrate to cloud-scalable architecture NFR-PERF-003: Database Query Performance Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ⚠️ Partially Met Requirement: Database queries shall execute within 500ms for 95th percentile. Current Implementation: - NHibernate ORM with lazy loading - Batch size configured (10) - SQL logging enabled (show_sql=true) - No query performance monitoring Evidence: From data-architecture.json : "Good domain-to-database mapping" Gaps: No query performance metrics, potential N+1 query issues 2.2 Scalability Requirements NFR-SCAL-001: Horizontal Scaling Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ❌ Not Met Requirement: System architecture shall support horizontal scaling to handle increased load. Current Blockers: - In-process session state (per-server) - LocalDB (cannot be shared across servers) - File-based logging (local file system) - No load balancer support Evidence: From cloud-readiness.json : "Fail - Cannot scale horizontally" Recommendation: Externalize session (Redis), migrate database (Azure SQL), implement stateless architecture NFR-SCAL-002: Database Scalability Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ❌ Not Met Requirement: Database shall support scaling to 1 million+ products and 10,000+ orders per day. Current Limitations: - SQL Server Express LocalDB (10GB limit) - No read replicas or sharding - Single database instance Recommendation: Migrate to cloud database with auto-scaling (Azure SQL) 2.3 Availability and Reliability NFR-AVAIL-001: System Uptime Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ⚠️ Unknown Requirement: System shall maintain 99.9% uptime (43.8 minutes downtime per month). Current State: - No health check endpoints - No automated failover - Single-server deployment (single point of failure) - No monitoring or alerting Evidence: From observability-setup.json : "No APM, no metrics" Recommendation: Implement health checks, multi-region deployment, monitoring NFR-AVAIL-002: Error Handling Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ⚠️ Partially Met Requirement: System shall gracefully handle errors without exposing sensitive information. Current Implementation: - Custom error pages configured (Web.config) - Try-catch blocks in controllers - Logging via Log4Net Gaps: - Error details may leak in development mode - No centralized error tracking - No user-friendly error recovery guidance 2.4 Security Requirements NFR-SEC-001: Authentication Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Met Requirement: System shall authenticate users before accessing protected resources (checkout, order history). Implementation: - ASP.NET Forms Authentication - [Authorize] attributes on protected controllers - Authentication cookie with timeout - Social authentication option (Janrain) Evidence: Authentication configuration in Web.config NFR-SEC-002: Password Storage Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Met Requirement: Passwords shall be stored securely using hashing (not plaintext). Implementation: - ASP.NET Membership Provider - Passwords hashed by membership provider - Salt added automatically Evidence: Membership provider configured in Web.config NFR-SEC-003: Payment Security Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Met Requirement: System shall NOT store credit card data; payment processing delegated to PCI-compliant provider. Implementation: - All payment processing via PayPal - No card data captured or stored in application - Redirect to PayPal for payment UI - Only transaction ID stored Business Rule: BR-PAY-001, BR-PAY-002 Compliance: PCI DSS compliance by delegation NFR-SEC-004: HTTPS Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ⚠️ Configuration-Dependent Requirement: All payment and authentication pages shall be served over HTTPS. Current State: - HTTPS required for production (IIS configuration) - Development mode may use HTTP - No HTTPS redirect enforced in code Recommendation: Enforce HTTPS redirect in application code, implement HSTS header NFR-SEC-005: SQL Injection Prevention Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Met Requirement: System shall prevent SQL injection attacks through parameterized queries. Implementation: - NHibernate ORM (parameterized queries) - No raw SQL concatenation detected - HBM.XML mappings define safe queries Evidence: All database access via NHibernate repository pattern NFR-SEC-006: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Prevention Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ⚠️ Partially Met Requirement: System shall prevent XSS attacks through input validation and output encoding. Current Implementation: - ASP.NET request validation (ValidateRequest=true) - HTML encoding in views - No Content Security Policy (CSP) headers Gaps: - No CSP headers - jQuery 1.3.2 has known XSS vulnerabilities Recommendation: Update jQuery, implement CSP headers, review all user input handling 2.5 Usability Requirements NFR-USAB-001: Browser Compatibility Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ⚠️ Partially Met Requirement: System shall be compatible with modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge). Current Support: - Designed for IE 7+ and Firefox 3+ (2010 era) - jQuery 1.3.2 (very old, limited modern browser testing) - ASPX views with server-side rendering Risk: Modern browser compatibility untested Recommendation: Test on current browser versions, update client libraries NFR-USAB-002: Mobile Responsiveness Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ❌ Not Met Requirement: System shall provide responsive design for mobile and tablet devices. Current State: - Fixed-width design (not responsive) - No mobile-specific views - No viewport meta tag - Desktop-only layout Evidence: From ui-inventory.json : No responsive design detected Recommendation: Implement responsive CSS framework (Bootstrap), mobile-first design 2.6 Maintainability and Supportability NFR-MAINT-001: Code Modularity Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Met Requirement: System shall maintain clear separation of concerns with layered architecture. Implementation: - 5-layer architecture (Presentation, Service, Domain, Data, Infrastructure) - Dependency injection (StructureMap) - Repository and Unit of Work patterns - Interface-based design Evidence: Application Layers shows excellent separation NFR-MAINT-002: Logging Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ⚠️ Partially Met Requirement: System shall log errors, warnings, and key business events for troubleshooting. Implementation: - Log4Net framework - File-based logging (C:\logs) - Configurable log levels - Error logging in controllers Gaps: - No centralized log aggregation - File-based logs not suitable for cloud - No structured logging - No business event logging Recommendation: Implement Application Insights, structured logging, business event tracking NFR-MAINT-003: Configuration Management Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ❌ Not Met Requirement: System configuration shall be externalized and environment-specific. Current State: - Configuration in Web.config (hardcoded) - Secrets in Web.config (PayPal credentials, SMTP credentials) - No environment variables - No Azure App Configuration or Key Vault Evidence: From configuration-inventory.json : "Hardcoded configuration" Recommendation: Externalize configuration, use Azure Key Vault for secrets 2.7 Internationalization (i18n) NFR-I18N-001: Multi-Language Support Priority: 🔵 LOW (Not Currently Required) Status: ❌ Not Implemented Requirement: System shall support multiple languages (English, French, Spanish, etc.). Current State: - English only (hardcoded strings) - No resource files - No localization framework - No culture routing Evidence: From i18n-inventory.json : "i18n_support: false" Business Impact: Cannot serve non-English markets Recommendation: If international expansion planned, implement .NET localization framework, resource files, culture-aware routing NFR-I18N-002: Multi-Currency Support Priority: 🔵 LOW (Not Currently Required) Status: ❌ Not Implemented Requirement: System shall support multiple currencies with conversion. Current State: - Single currency (determined by PayPal configuration) - No currency conversion - No Money value object Business Impact: Cannot serve international markets with local currency Recommendation: Implement Money value object, currency conversion service, multi-currency payment support 3. User Interface Requirements 3.1 UI Patterns and Conventions UIR-001: Consistent Navigation Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Consistent navigation menu across all pages with categories and user account links. Implementation: Master page with top navigation menu UIR-002: Responsive Feedback Status: ⚠️ Partially Met Description: User actions (add to basket, login, submit order) provide immediate feedback. Current: Post-back page reloads (no AJAX), confirmation messages displayed Gap: No loading indicators, no optimistic UI updates UIR-003: Error Display Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Validation errors displayed near relevant form fields with clear messages. Implementation: ASP.NET validation controls, custom error messages UIR-004: Accessibility Status: ❌ Not Met Description: UI shall meet WCAG 2.0 Level AA accessibility standards. Current State: No accessibility testing, likely missing ARIA labels, unknown keyboard navigation, color contrast untested Evidence: From accessibility-assessment.json : "wcag_compliance: Unknown" Recommendation: Conduct accessibility audit, implement ARIA labels, ensure keyboard navigation 4. Data Requirements 4.1 Data Integrity DR-001: Referential Integrity Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Database shall enforce referential integrity through foreign key constraints. Implementation: NHibernate cascading rules, database foreign keys DR-002: Data Validation Status: ✅ Implemented Description: All data shall be validated before persistence. Implementation: Business rule classes, domain entity validation, form validation 4.2 Data Retention DR-003: Order History Retention Status: ⚠️ Not Specified Description: Order history shall be retained indefinitely for customer access and audit purposes. Current: No retention policy documented, orders persist in database Recommendation: Define data retention policy, implement archival strategy 4.3 Data Privacy DR-004: Customer Data Protection Status: ⚠️ Partially Met Description: Customer personal data shall be protected and only accessible to authorized users. Current: Basic authentication, no encryption at rest, no data deletion mechanism Gap: No GDPR compliance (right to erasure, data portability) Evidence: From compliance-status.json : "gdpr: Non-compliant" 5. Integration Requirements 5.1 Payment Gateway Integration INT-PAY-001: PayPal Standard Payments Status: ✅ Implemented Description: System shall integrate with PayPal for payment processing using Standard Payments API. Implementation: - HTTPS POST redirect to PayPal - Return URL for success callback - Cancel URL for user cancellation - Transaction ID capture Configuration: PayPal endpoint and business email in Web.config 5.2 Authentication Integration INT-AUTH-001: Social Authentication Status: ✅ Implemented Description: System shall integrate with Janrain for social login (Facebook, Google, Twitter). Implementation: - OAuth-style callback from Janrain - Token-based authentication - API key configuration 5.3 Email Integration INT-EMAIL-001: SMTP Email Service Status: ✅ Implemented Description: System shall send transactional emails (order confirmation) via SMTP. Implementation: - SMTP configuration in Web.config - IEmailService interface with SMTP implementation - Fallback: TextLoggingEmailService for development 6. Compliance and Regulatory Requirements 6.1 Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) COMP-PCI-001: No Card Data Storage Status: ✅ Compliant Description: System shall NOT store credit card numbers, CVV, or expiration dates. Implementation: Payment processing delegated to PayPal (PCI Level 1 compliant) Evidence: No credit card fields in database schema or domain model 6.2 General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) COMP-GDPR-001: Consent Management Status: ❌ Not Compliant Description: System shall obtain explicit consent for data collection and processing. Current: No consent mechanism implemented Recommendation: Add cookie consent banner, privacy policy acceptance during registration COMP-GDPR-002: Right to Erasure Status: ❌ Not Compliant Description: Customers shall be able to request deletion of their personal data. Current: No data deletion mechanism Recommendation: Implement "Delete My Account" feature with data anonymization COMP-GDPR-003: Data Portability Status: ❌ Not Compliant Description: Customers shall be able to export their personal data in machine-readable format. Current: No data export mechanism Recommendation: Implement "Download My Data" feature (JSON or CSV export) 6.3 Web Accessibility COMP-A11Y-001: WCAG 2.0 Compliance Status: ❌ Not Compliant Description: System shall meet WCAG 2.0 Level AA accessibility standards. Current: No accessibility testing performed, likely non-compliant Recommendation: Accessibility audit, remediation, ongoing testing 7. Requirements Traceability Matrix Requirement ID Business Process Domain Aggregate Implementation Test Coverage FR-PC-001 Product Discovery Product ProductController ❌ No automated tests FR-BK-001 Shopping Basket BasketController, Basket.Add() ❌ No automated tests FR-BK-003 Shopping Basket BasketService, BasketItem ❌ No automated tests FR-CO-001 Checkout Basket, Customer CheckoutController ❌ No automated tests FR-CO-003 Checkout Order OrderService.CreateOrderFromBasket() ❌ No automated tests FR-CO-004 Payment Order, Payment PaymentController, PayPalPaymentService ❌ No automated tests FR-OM-001 Order Management Order OrderController ❌ No automated tests NFR-SEC-003 Payment Security Payment PayPal delegation ✅ Compliant by design NFR-SEC-005 SQL Injection Data Access NHibernate ORM ✅ Protected by ORM Test Coverage Summary: - Unit Tests: ❌ Not detected - Integration Tests: ❌ Not detected - E2E Tests: ❌ Not detected - Test Coverage: 0% (no automated tests found) Evidence: From test-coverage.json : "coverage: None" Critical Gap: No automated testing of requirements 8. Requirements Prioritization 8.1 MoSCoW Prioritization Must Have (Implemented): - ✅ Product browsing and detail view - ✅ Add to basket, view basket, update quantities - ✅ Customer registration and login - ✅ Checkout process - ✅ PayPal payment processing - ✅ Order confirmation - ✅ Order history Should Have (Not Implemented): - ❌ Product search - ❌ Inventory management - ❌ Out-of-stock indication - ❌ Admin portal for product/order management - ❌ GDPR compliance features - ❌ Mobile-responsive design Could Have (Future): - ❌ Product recommendations - ❌ Wish list - ❌ Promo codes - ❌ Guest checkout - ❌ Order tracking - ❌ Returns/refunds - ❌ Product reviews Won't Have (This Phase): - ❌ Multi-language support - ❌ Multi-currency support - ❌ Marketplace model - ❌ Subscription model 9. Summary and Recommendations 9.1 Requirements Coverage Assessment Strengths: - ✅ Core e-commerce transaction flow complete (browse → basket → checkout → payment → confirmation) - ✅ Clean domain model with business rules enforcement - ✅ Payment security through PCI-compliant provider - ✅ User authentication with social login option Critical Gaps: - ❌ No automated testing (0% coverage) - ❌ GDPR non-compliance (data subject rights) - ❌ No inventory management (overselling risk) - ❌ Cannot scale horizontally (architectural limitation) - ❌ No mobile responsiveness - ❌ No admin portal (product/order management) 9.2 Modernization Requirements Priorities Phase 1 - Critical (Immediate): 1. Implement automated testing (unit, integration, E2E) 2. Add GDPR compliance features (consent, data deletion, data export) 3. Implement inventory management with stock tracking 4. Externalize configuration and secrets 5. Add health check endpoints and monitoring Phase 2 - High (3-6 months): 1. Mobile-responsive redesign 2. Implement admin portal 3. Add product search 4. Scale-out architecture (externalize state, cloud database) 5. Performance optimization and caching Phase 3 - Medium (6-12 months): 1. Product recommendations engine 2. Order tracking and fulfillment 3. Returns/refunds processing 4. Promo code system 5. Multi-payment methods Document End Related Documents: - 2.1 Business Domain Model - 2.3 Compliance and Regulatory - System Architecture Change Log: | Date | Version | Author | Changes | |------|---------|--------|---------| | 2026-06-09 | 1.0 | Business Analyst AI | Initial requirements specification (reverse-engineered) |

docs.title: 2.2 Requirements Specification

docs.text: This document captures the functional and non-functional requirements of the Agathas Storefront e-commerce platform as implemented in the current system. Requirements have been reverse-engineered from source code, user interfaces, configuration files, and system behavior analysis. Key Findings: - Total Requirements Identified: 85+ functional and non-functional requirements - Requirements Coverage: Core e-commerce functionality well-implemented; advanced features (inventory, returns, internationalization) not present - Requirements Maturity: Basic e-commerce requirements fully met; scalability and compliance requirements partially met - Business Priority: Customer-facing transaction workflows (browse, basket, checkout) prioritized over administrative features Requirements Distribution: Category Requirements Implementation Status Functional Requirements 55 80% Complete Non-Functional Requirements 20 65% Complete User Interface Requirements 10 75% Complete Data Requirements 5 90% Complete Integration Requirements 5 100% Complete Compliance Requirements 8 40% Complete
docs.title: Executive Summary

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to browse products organized by categories and brands. Acceptance Criteria: - Products displayed in hierarchical category structure - Featured products shown on home page - Product listings show image, name, price - Category navigation via menu and breadcrumbs Implementation: - Controller: ProductController.Index() - Service: ProductCatalogService.GetProductsByCategory() - View: Views/Product/Index.aspx Traceability: Maps to User Journey "Product Discovery" in Business Domain Model
docs.title: FR-PC-001: Product Browsing

docs.text: Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to filter product listings by size, color, brand, and price range. Acceptance Criteria: - Filter options displayed in sidebar - Filter combinations applied using AND logic - Filtered results update product listing - Filter state persists during browsing session Implementation: - Service: ProductSearchRequestQueryGenerator generates NHibernate queries from filter criteria - JSON: JsonProductSearchRequest captures filter selections - Query: Dynamic NHibernate criteria queries Traceability: Supports business capability "Product Discovery"
docs.title: FR-PC-002: Product Filtering and Refinement

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to view detailed information for a specific product including all available variants. Acceptance Criteria: - Product image, name, description, price displayed - All size and color combinations shown - Add to basket functionality available - Product title and variant attributes visible Implementation: - Controller: ProductController.Detail(int productId) - View: Views/Product/Detail.aspx - ViewModel: ProductView with size/color options Traceability: Essential for product selection in shopping workflow
docs.title: FR-PC-003: Product Detail View

docs.text: Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: System shall display featured products on the home page to promote specific items. Acceptance Criteria: - Configurable featured products list - Featured products shown on landing page - Products link to detail pages Implementation: - Controller: HomeController.Index() - Service: ProductCatalogService.GetFeaturedProducts() Business Value: Marketing and promotion support
docs.title: FR-PC-004: Featured Products Display

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to add products to their shopping basket with specified quantity. Acceptance Criteria: - Select size and color variant - Specify quantity (default: 1) - Product added to basket with confirmation - If product already in basket, quantity increased Implementation: - Controller: BasketController.Add() - Service: BasketService.AddProductToBasket() - Domain: Basket.Add() enforces no-duplicate rule - Storage: Cookie-based basket persistence Business Rule: BR-BSK-001 (No duplicate products - increases quantity instead) Traceability: Core requirement from Shopping Workflow
docs.title: FR-BK-001: Add Product to Basket

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to view all items in their basket with quantities and prices. Acceptance Criteria: - List all basket items with product details - Show quantity per item - Display item subtotal (price × quantity) - Show basket subtotal (all items) - Show delivery cost - Show basket total (items + delivery) Implementation: - Controller: BasketController.Index() - View: Views/Basket/Index.aspx - ViewModel: BasketView with calculated totals Traceability: Required before checkout
docs.title: FR-BK-002: View Basket Contents

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to increase or decrease quantities of items in the basket. Acceptance Criteria: - Quantity can be increased or decreased - Minimum quantity is 1 (removing item if decreased to 0) - Basket totals recalculate automatically - Changes persist across page loads Implementation: - Controller: BasketController.UpdateQuantity() - Service: BasketService.UpdateBasketItemQuantity() - Domain: BasketItem.IncreaseItemQtyBy() , BasketItem.DecreaseItemQtyBy() Business Rule: BR-BSK-002 (Positive quantity)
docs.title: FR-BK-003: Update Item Quantity

docs.text: Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to remove items from their basket. Acceptance Criteria: - Remove button available per item - Item removed immediately - Basket totals recalculate - Empty basket message shown if no items remain Implementation: - Controller: BasketController.Remove(int basketItemId) - Service: BasketService.RemoveItemFromBasket() - Domain: Basket.Remove(basketItem)
docs.title: FR-BK-004: Remove Item from Basket

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to select a delivery option with associated cost before checkout. Acceptance Criteria: - Delivery options displayed with names and costs - User selects one delivery option - Delivery cost included in basket total - Delivery option selection persists Implementation: - Controller: BasketController.SetDeliveryOption(int deliveryOptionId) - Domain: Basket.SetDeliveryOption() - Entity: DeliveryOption with pricing Business Rule: BR-BSK-004 (Delivery option required before checkout)
docs.title: FR-BK-005: Select Delivery Option

docs.text: Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Basket contents shall persist across user sessions using cookie storage. Acceptance Criteria: - Basket saved in cookie after each modification - Basket restored on subsequent visits - Cookie expires after configurable period - Anonymous and authenticated users both supported Implementation: - Repository: CookieBasketRepository - Storage: ICookieStorageService - Key: CookieDataKeys.Basket Traceability: Supports user experience for interrupted shopping sessions
docs.title: FR-BK-006: Basket Persistence

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: New users shall be able to create a customer account with email and password. Acceptance Criteria: - Registration form with email, password, first name, surname - Email uniqueness validation - Password strength validation - Account created in both domain (Customer) and infrastructure (Membership) - Auto-login after successful registration Implementation: - Controller: AccountRegisterController.Register() - Service: CustomerService.CreateCustomer() - Domain: Customer entity - Infrastructure: ASP.NET Membership Provider Business Rule: BR-CUS-001 (Unique email), BR-CUS-002 (Email validation)
docs.title: FR-AC-001: Customer Registration

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Registered users shall be able to authenticate using email and password. Acceptance Criteria: - Login form with email and password fields - Credentials validated against membership database - Authentication cookie created on success - Redirect to originally requested page after login - Error message on failure Implementation: - Controller: AccountLogOnController.LogOn() - Service: AspMembershipAuthentication.Login() - Infrastructure: ASP.NET Forms Authentication
docs.title: FR-AC-002: User Login

docs.text: Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to authenticate using social login providers (Facebook, Google, etc.) via Janrain. Acceptance Criteria: - Social login buttons displayed on login page - Redirect to Janrain authentication - Token received from Janrain on success - User account created or linked - Auto-login after social auth Implementation: - Controller: AccountLogOnController.JanrainCallback() - Service: JanrainAuthenticationService - Configuration: Janrain API key in Web.config Business Rule: BR-AUT-003 (Social auth option)
docs.title: FR-AC-003: Social Authentication

docs.text: Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Authenticated users shall be able to log out of their session. Acceptance Criteria: - Logout link available when authenticated - Authentication cookie cleared - Redirect to home page - Session state cleared Implementation: - Controller: AccountLogOnController.LogOut() - Infrastructure: FormsAuthentication.SignOut()
docs.title: FR-AC-004: User Logout

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Customers shall be able to add, edit, and delete delivery addresses. Acceptance Criteria: - View list of saved delivery addresses - Add new address with street, city, postcode, name - Edit existing address - Delete address (if not only address) - Select address during checkout Implementation: - Controller: CustomerController.AddDeliveryAddress() - Service: CustomerService.AddDeliveryAddress() - Domain: Customer.AddDeliveryAddress() , DeliveryAddress entity Business Rule: BR-CUS-003 (Checkout address requirement), BR-ADR-001 (Required fields)
docs.title: FR-AC-005: Manage Delivery Addresses

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Users shall be able to proceed from basket to checkout process. Acceptance Criteria: - Checkout button available in basket view - Authentication required (redirect to login if not authenticated) - Basket must have items and delivery option selected - Checkout page displays basket summary and delivery address selection Implementation: - Controller: CheckoutController.Index() - Authorization: [Authorize] attribute enforces authentication - Validation: Delivery option and items validated Business Rule: BR-AUT-001 (Checkout authentication)
docs.title: FR-CO-001: Initiate Checkout

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: During checkout, customers shall select a delivery address from their saved addresses. Acceptance Criteria: - List of customer's saved addresses displayed - Customer selects one address for delivery - Address details shown (street, city, postcode) - Option to add new address if none exist Implementation: - Controller: CheckoutController.SelectAddress() - View: Address selector in checkout page - Validation: At least one address required
docs.title: FR-CO-002: Select Delivery Address

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Customers shall be able to confirm and submit their order for payment. Acceptance Criteria: - Order created from basket contents - Order includes items, quantities, prices (snapshot) - Delivery address captured - Shipping service assigned - Order saved to database - Redirect to payment gateway Implementation: - Controller: CheckoutController.Submit() - Service: OrderService.CreateOrderFromBasket() - Domain: Order entity created from Basket - Mapping: BasketItem → OrderItem with price snapshot Business Rule: BR-CRS-001 (Order from basket), BR-ORD-006 (Price snapshot)
docs.title: FR-CO-003: Submit Order

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: Customers shall complete payment securely through PayPal payment gateway. Acceptance Criteria: - Redirect to PayPal with order details - PayPal presents payment UI - Customer completes payment - PayPal callback received with transaction status - Order updated with payment details on success Implementation: - Controller: PaymentController.Callback() - Service: PayPalPaymentService generates payment request - Domain: Order.SetPayment() captures payment - Integration: HTTPS POST to PayPal sandbox endpoint Business Rule: BR-PAY-001 (External processing), BR-PAY-004 (Amount validation), BR-ORD-002 (Payment amount match) Security: BR-PAY-002 (No card storage)
docs.title: FR-CO-004: Process Payment via PayPal

docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ✅ Implemented Description: After successful payment, customers shall receive order confirmation via email and on-screen. docs.text: Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ⚠️ Partially Met Requirement: Product listing and detail pages shall load within 2 seconds under normal load. Current Performance: - No performance monitoring implemented - Server-side rendering with ASPX views (slower than modern SPAs) - No CDN for static assets - Database queries not optimized (N+1 query issues possible with NHibernate) Evidence: No Application Performance Monitoring (APM) detected in observability-setup.json Recommendation: Implement APM (Application Insights), optimize queries, add caching

docs.text: Priority: 🟡 HIGH Status: ❌ Not Met Requirement: System shall support at least 100 concurrent users without degradation. docs.text: Priority: 🔴 CRITICAL Status: ❌ Not Met Requirement: System architecture shall support horizontal scaling to handle increased load.
