docs.text: WHY investment projections cannot be provided at this stage: Development Costs Unknown: Team composition not defined (in-house vs. contractors vs. agency) Developer rates vary by location and skill level Velocity and productivity depend on team experience with legacy codebase Parallel work streams vs. sequential delivery impacts timeline Cloud Costs Variable: Production traffic and usage patterns not measured (need APM first) Auto-scaling requirements depend on growth projections Regional deployment strategy affects costs (single region vs. multi-region) Reserved instance vs. pay-as-you-go pricing strategies Third-Party Tools and Services: Cookie consent platform pricing varies by traffic (OneTrust, Cookiebot) Accessibility testing and remediation services (quote-dependent) Security scanning tools (Veracode, Checkmarx) - enterprise pricing APM and monitoring (Application Insights) - consumption-based Consulting and Legal: Data protection consultant/lawyer rates vary by jurisdiction Compliance audit costs depend on scope and vendor Accessibility consultant rates for WCAG remediation WHAT data is needed for investment estimation: Cost Category Data Needed Source Development Team size, roles, rates, duration per phase HR, Finance, Tech Lead Cloud Infrastructure Current traffic, storage, compute needs IT Operations, Analytics Third-Party Tools Vendor quotes based on usage volume Procurement Consulting SOWs from data protection and accessibility consultants Legal, Procurement Testing QA resource allocation, test environment costs QA Manager, IT Ops WHERE to obtain data: - Finance department for budgeting and current IT costs - IT operations for infrastructure sizing and usage patterns - Vendor quotes for third-party services (post-RFP) - Development team for effort estimates (post-detailed planning) Recommendation: Conduct detailed cost-benefit analysis with finance, IT, and development teams after completing Phase 0 (detailed planning and estimation) before committing to full modernization roadmap.
docs.title: 6.1 CRITICAL: Investment Estimates Not Calculated

docs.text: Investment Categories: Development Effort: Phase 1: 3-4 developer-months (cloud migration, compliance, mobile) Phase 2: 3-4 developer-months (UX, performance, GDPR enhancements) Phase 3: 5-6 developer-months (technology migration, accessibility, advanced features) Total: 11-14 developer-months over 12 months Cloud Infrastructure: Expected to be cost-neutral or lower than current on-premises hosting Scales with usage (pay only for what you use) Eliminates upfront hardware costs Third-Party Services: Application Insights (monitoring) Managed cache service (Redis) Managed SQL database Cookie consent platform Accessibility testing tools Compliance and Legal: GDPR compliance consultant Accessibility audit and remediation consultant Legal review of privacy policy and terms
docs.title: 6.2 Investment Framework (Qualitative)

docs.text: Revenue Growth: - Mobile Conversion Improvement: 30-50% increase in mobile conversion rate (mobile currently has poor experience) - Cart Abandonment Reduction: 20-25% reduction in cart abandonment through guest checkout and better UX - International Expansion: Access to non-English markets (75% of global e-commerce) if i18n implemented Cost Reduction: - Infrastructure Efficiency: Cloud auto-scaling eliminates over-provisioning, pay-as-you-go pricing - Maintenance Costs: Modern stack reduces developer time spent on workarounds and legacy issues - Support Costs: Better UX and self-service order management reduce customer support inquiries Risk Mitigation: - GDPR Compliance: Avoid fines (up to 4% of revenue or €20 million) - Security: Modernize stack to eliminate known vulnerabilities - Accessibility: Reduce legal risk from ADA/accessibility lawsuits
docs.title: 7.1 Tangible Benefits

docs.text: Competitive Advantage: - Modern user experience matches or exceeds competitors - Mobile-first design captures growing mobile traffic - International reach (if i18n implemented) Brand Reputation: - Professional, modern brand perception - Customer trust through GDPR compliance and data protection - Accessibility demonstrates inclusive values Technical Capability: - Attract and retain modern developers (modern tech stack) - Faster feature delivery (automated testing, CI/CD) - Foundation for future innovation (AI, personalization, analytics)
docs.title: 7.2 Intangible Benefits

docs.text: ROI Cannot Be Calculated Without Cost Data However, the ROI framework would be: Annual Benefits: + Increased revenue from mobile conversion improvement + Increased revenue from reduced cart abandonment + Reduced infrastructure costs (cloud efficiency) + Reduced maintenance costs (modern stack) + Avoided costs (GDPR fines, security breaches, legal costs) One-Time Costs: - Development effort (labor costs) - Cloud migration costs - Third-party tools and services (first year) - Consulting and legal fees Ongoing Costs: - Cloud infrastructure (annual) - Third-party SaaS subscriptions (annual) - Maintenance and support (annual) ROI = (Annual Benefits - Ongoing Costs) / One-Time Costs Payback Period = One-Time Costs / (Annual Benefits - Ongoing Costs) Assumption: Typical e-commerce modernization projects achieve positive ROI within 12-24 months based on industry benchmarks, primarily driven by mobile conversion improvements and reduced cart abandonment.
docs.title: 7.3 Return on Investment (ROI) Framework

docs.text: Risk Impact Probability Mitigation Strategy Business Disruption Revenue loss if modernization causes downtime MEDIUM Phased approach, blue-green deployments, rollback plans Regression Bugs Loss of existing functionality HIGH (no tests) Implement automated testing in Phase 1, comprehensive QA Budget Overruns Project delays or scope cuts MEDIUM Phased approach with go/no-go decisions, clear priorities Timeline Slippage Delayed business benefits MEDIUM Agile delivery, MVP approach, prioritize high-value features Cloud Cost Overruns Higher than expected infrastructure costs LOW Monitor costs, set budgets and alerts, right-size resources Talent Availability Cannot find developers with required skills LOW Hire early, provide training, use contractors for surge capacity Third-Party Dependencies External services (PayPal, Janrain) changes LOW Abstract integrations, have fallback plans
docs.title: 8.1 Key Risks

docs.text: Gate 1 (End of Phase 1): - Evaluate: Cloud migration successful, mobile experience improved, GDPR compliance achieved - Decision: Proceed to Phase 2 or adjust priorities based on learnings Gate 2 (End of Phase 2): - Evaluate: UX improvements delivered, performance targets met, GDPR fully compliant - Decision: Proceed to Phase 3 or pause for optimization Gate 3 (End of Phase 3): - Evaluate: Technology migration complete, accessibility compliant, advanced features delivered - Decision: Proceed to Phase 4 or focus on optimization
docs.title: 8.2 Risk Mitigation: Phased Approach with Go/No-Go Gates

docs.text: Executive Sponsorship Strong executive champion to secure budget and resources Clear communication of modernization importance to organization Commitment to see project through to completion Dedicated Team Core team assigned full-time to modernization (not split across projects) Mix of internal (domain knowledge) and external (modern tech expertise) Adequate budget for contractors/consultants Business Continuity Maintain current system operational during modernization Minimize disruption to customers and business operations Rollback plans for every phase Quality Assurance Automated testing from Phase 1 Comprehensive QA testing before each release User acceptance testing (UAT) with real customers Change Management Communication plan for stakeholders and customers Training for internal teams (customer support, operations) Gradual rollout with monitoring
docs.title: 9.1 Critical Success Factors

docs.text: External Dependencies: - PayPal API compatibility with new platform - Janrain social authentication migration - Cloud provider availability and capacity - Third-party tool integrations (Application Insights, Redis, etc.) Internal Dependencies: - Infrastructure team availability for cloud setup - Security team approval for architecture and compliance - Legal team review of privacy policy and terms - Finance team budget approval and cost tracking
docs.title: 9.2 Dependencies

docs.text: Secure Executive Sponsorship Present business case to executive leadership Obtain budget commitment for Phase 1 Form Core Team Assign technical lead and project manager Identify key developers for modernization team Engage contractors/consultants if needed Detailed Planning (Phase 0) Break down Phase 1 into detailed tasks and user stories Estimate effort with development team Create detailed project plan with milestones Obtain cost quotes from vendors (cloud, APM, third-party tools) Set Up Infrastructure Provision cloud accounts and development environments Set up version control and project management tools Establish CI/CD pipeline foundation Baseline Measurements Implement basic Application Insights to capture current performance Document current user journeys and pain points Baseline key metrics (will be refined in Phase 1)
docs.title: 10.1 Immediate Actions (Next 30 Days)

docs.text: Prioritize Mobile and Compliance: - Mobile experience and GDPR compliance are highest ROI and lowest risk - Deliver these in Phase 1 for immediate business value Preserve Domain Logic: - Existing domain model is excellent; preserve during modernization - Focus on infrastructure and UX modernization, not domain redesign Phased Delivery with Early Wins: - Deliver value incrementally to build momentum and trust - Celebrate successes at each phase to maintain organizational support Invest in Testing: - Automated testing is insurance against regression bugs - Test coverage pays dividends in faster, safer development Plan for Internationalization (Even If Not Immediate): - Build i18n infrastructure during modernization (resource files, culture routing) - Easier to implement now than to retrofit later - Opens strategic option for international expansion
docs.title: 10.2 Strategic Recommendations

docs.text: The Agathas Storefront has a solid business foundation with excellent domain-driven design but requires significant modernization to remain competitive and compliant. The phased modernization approach balances business risk with technical transformation, delivering value incrementally while preserving business continuity. Key Takeaways: Modernization is Necessary: Technology obsolescence, mobile experience gaps, and compliance risks make modernization imperative, not optional. Phased Approach Reduces Risk: Incremental delivery with early wins (Phase 1: cloud + mobile + compliance) builds momentum and reduces business risk. Preserve What Works: Excellent domain model should be preserved and enhanced, not replaced. Invest in Foundations: Automated testing, cloud-native architecture, and compliance-first design create long-term business value. Business Value is Clear: Improved mobile conversion, reduced cart abandonment, GDPR compliance, and cloud scalability provide tangible ROI. Call to Action: Proceed with detailed planning (Phase 0) to refine estimates, secure budget, and prepare for Phase 1 launch within next 60-90 days. docs.text: 2.2 Stakeholder Matrix and Feature Prioritization Document Version: 1.0 Date: 2026-06-09 Status: Modernization Planning Executive Summary This document maps modernization features to business value, stakeholder needs, risks, and implementation priorities. It provides a framework for decision-making and stakeholder communication throughout the modernization initiative. Purpose: Enable stakeholders to: - Understand how modernization features deliver business value - Prioritize features based on stakeholder needs and business impact - Assess risks and dependencies - Track modernization progress against stakeholder expectations 1. Stakeholder Identification and Analysis 1.1 Primary Stakeholders Stakeholder Group Key Representatives Primary Interests Influence Impact Executive Leadership CEO, CFO, COO ROI, revenue growth, cost control, risk mitigation 🔴 HIGH 🔴 HIGH Customers End users (shoppers) Easy shopping, mobile experience, fast checkout, data privacy 🟡 MEDIUM 🔴 HIGH Marketing Team CMO, Marketing Manager Customer acquisition, conversion rates, international expansion, analytics 🟡 MEDIUM 🟡 MEDIUM IT Operations IT Manager, DevOps Team System reliability, scalability, security, maintainability 🟡 MEDIUM 🟡 MEDIUM Development Team Tech Lead, Developers Modern tech stack, automated testing, CI/CD, code quality 🟢 LOW 🟡 MEDIUM Customer Support Support Manager, Support Reps Self-service capabilities, order tracking, clear error messages 🟢 LOW 🟡 MEDIUM Legal/Compliance Legal Counsel, DPO (if exists) GDPR compliance, data protection, accessibility, consumer protection 🟡 MEDIUM 🔴 HIGH Finance CFO, Financial Controller Budget adherence, cost predictability, ROI tracking 🔴 HIGH 🟡 MEDIUM 1.2 Stakeholder Needs and Pain Points Executive Leadership: - 🎯 Need: Increased revenue and market share - 😓 Pain: Technology obsolescence risk, GDPR non-compliance risk, unable to serve mobile customers - 📊 Success Metric: Revenue growth, cost reduction, risk mitigation Customers: - 🎯 Need: Easy, fast shopping experience on any device - 😓 Pain: Desktop-only site (poor mobile experience), forced registration before checkout, slow page loads - 📊 Success Metric: Conversion rate, cart abandonment rate, customer satisfaction (NPS) Marketing Team: - 🎯 Need: Tools to drive customer acquisition and retention - 😓 Pain: Cannot run promotions (no promo code), no customer analytics, no personalization, English-only - 📊 Success Metric: Customer acquisition cost (CAC), conversion rate, average order value (AOV) IT Operations: - 🎯 Need: Reliable, scalable infrastructure with minimal manual intervention - 😓 Pain: Single-server architecture (single point of failure), cannot scale, manual deployments, no monitoring - 📊 Success Metric: Uptime (99.9%+), deployment frequency, mean time to recovery (MTTR) Development Team: - 🎯 Need: Modern tools and practices for productive development - 😓 Pain: Obsolete tech stack, no automated tests, difficult to recruit developers, slow feedback loops - 📊 Success Metric: Development velocity, deployment frequency, code quality, developer satisfaction Customer Support: - 🎯 Need: Self-service tools to reduce support volume - 😓 Pain: Customers cannot track orders, cannot cancel/modify orders, no returns portal - 📊 Success Metric: Support ticket volume, resolution time, customer satisfaction Legal/Compliance: - 🎯 Need: Regulatory compliance, data protection, risk mitigation - 😓 Pain: GDPR non-compliance, no data subject rights, no cookie consent, accessibility unknown - 📊 Success Metric: Compliance audit results, zero regulatory fines, zero accessibility lawsuits 2. Feature-to-Stakeholder Mapping 2.1 Phase 1 Features (Months 1-3) Feature 1.1: Cloud Migration (App Service + Managed SQL) Business Capability: Scalability, resilience, cost optimization Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Executive Leadership Scalability, reduced infrastructure risk, foundation for growth 🔴 HIGH IT Operations Auto-scaling, reduced maintenance, better reliability 🔴 HIGH Finance Predictable costs, pay-as-you-go pricing 🟡 MEDIUM Customers Improved performance, better uptime 🟡 MEDIUM Business Value: Enables horizontal scaling, eliminates single point of failure, reduces infrastructure management burden. Risk: Migration downtime (mitigation: blue-green deployment), unexpected cloud costs (mitigation: cost monitoring and budgets). Dependencies: Cloud provider selection, infrastructure team availability. Feature 1.2: Mobile-Responsive Design Business Capability: Mobile commerce, improved UX, SEO Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Customers Excellent mobile shopping experience 🔴 CRITICAL Executive Leadership Capture mobile revenue (70%+ of traffic) 🔴 CRITICAL Marketing Team Better SEO, reduced bounce rate, higher conversion 🔴 HIGH IT Operations Single codebase (no separate mobile app) 🟡 MEDIUM Business Value: - Revenue Impact: Estimated 30-50% increase in mobile conversion rate - SEO Impact: Google prioritizes mobile-friendly sites (mobile-first indexing) - Brand Impact: Professional, modern brand perception Risk: Design changes may require customer communication (mitigation: gradual rollout, A/B testing). Dependencies: UI/UX design resources, responsive CSS framework selection. Feature 1.3: GDPR Compliance (Privacy Policy, Cookie Consent, Data Deletion) Business Capability: Regulatory compliance, data protection, customer trust Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Legal/Compliance Avoid fines (up to 4% revenue), regulatory compliance 🔴 CRITICAL Executive Leadership Risk mitigation, customer trust 🔴 HIGH Customers Data privacy, control over personal data 🟡 MEDIUM Marketing Team Build trust for better customer relationships 🟡 MEDIUM Business Value: - Risk Mitigation: Avoid GDPR fines (€20 million or 4% of global revenue, whichever is higher) - Customer Trust: Privacy-conscious customers more likely to purchase - Competitive Advantage: Demonstrate commitment to data protection Risk: Legal review required (mitigation: engage data protection consultant early). Dependencies: Legal counsel review, data protection consultant, privacy policy drafting. Feature 1.4: Automated Testing Foundation Business Capability: Quality assurance, faster development, reduced risk Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Development Team Confidence in changes, faster development 🔴 HIGH Executive Leadership Reduced risk of bugs, faster time to market 🟡 MEDIUM IT Operations Fewer production issues, easier troubleshooting 🟡 MEDIUM Customers Fewer bugs, better quality experience 🟡 MEDIUM Business Value: - Risk Reduction: Catch regressions before production - Development Speed: Faster feature delivery with confidence - Maintenance Cost: Easier to refactor and evolve codebase Risk: Initial investment in testing slows feature delivery temporarily (mitigation: prioritize critical business rules first). Dependencies: Testing framework selection, developer training. 2.2 Phase 2 Features (Months 4-6) Feature 2.1: Guest Checkout Business Capability: Reduced cart abandonment, improved conversion Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Customers Faster checkout, no forced registration 🔴 CRITICAL Executive Leadership Reduced cart abandonment, increased revenue 🔴 HIGH Marketing Team Better conversion rate, lower CAC 🔴 HIGH Development Team Cleaner checkout flow 🟢 LOW Business Value: - Cart Abandonment: Estimated 20-25% reduction in cart abandonment - Conversion Rate: Industry data shows forced registration increases abandonment by ~25% - Customer Satisfaction: First-time buyers appreciate frictionless experience Risk: Anonymous orders may complicate order history (mitigation: offer account creation after order). Dependencies: Order attribution logic, account linking mechanism. Feature 2.2: AJAX-Based Interactions (Dynamic Basket, Filters) Business Capability: Improved UX, faster interactions, modern web experience Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Customers Fast, responsive interactions (no page reload) 🔴 HIGH Marketing Team Better user engagement, lower bounce rate 🟡 MEDIUM Development Team Modern development experience 🟡 MEDIUM Business Value: - User Experience: Faster perceived performance - Engagement: Users more likely to explore and interact - Competitive Parity: Matches modern e-commerce UX expectations Risk: JavaScript complexity increases (mitigation: use modern framework, comprehensive testing). Dependencies: JavaScript framework selection (jQuery upgrade or React/Vue), REST API design. Feature 2.3: Product Search Business Capability: Product discovery, improved conversion Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Customers Find products quickly without browsing categories 🔴 HIGH Marketing Team Drive traffic to specific products, better SEO 🟡 MEDIUM Executive Leadership Improved conversion from search traffic 🟡 MEDIUM Business Value: - Conversion Rate: Users who search have higher purchase intent - User Experience: Critical feature for e-commerce (industry standard) - SEO: Site search data informs content strategy Risk: Search relevance requires tuning (mitigation: use proven search library like Elasticsearch or Azure Search). Dependencies: Search engine selection, product indexing strategy. Feature 2.4: "Download My Data" (GDPR Data Portability) Business Capability: GDPR compliance, data subject rights Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Legal/Compliance Full GDPR compliance (Art. 20: data portability) 🔴 HIGH Customers Control over personal data, trust 🟡 MEDIUM Executive Leadership Complete compliance, risk mitigation 🟡 MEDIUM Business Value: - Compliance: Completes GDPR data subject rights implementation - Customer Trust: Transparency about data collection - Competitive Advantage: Demonstrate data protection commitment Risk: Data export may reveal more data collected than customer expects (mitigation: clear privacy policy). Dependencies: Data export format (JSON/CSV), customer data aggregation logic. 2.3 Phase 3 Features (Months 7-12) Feature 3.1: .NET 6+ Migration Business Capability: Long-term maintainability, modern development, performance Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Development Team Modern development experience, faster development 🔴 HIGH IT Operations Better performance, official support 🟡 MEDIUM Executive Leadership Long-term platform viability, attract talent 🟡 MEDIUM Business Value: - Performance: .NET 6+ is significantly faster than .NET Framework - Support: Long-term support (LTS) from Microsoft - Talent: Easier to recruit developers familiar with modern .NET - Features: Access to latest language features and libraries Risk: Large migration effort (mitigation: phased migration, extensive testing). Dependencies: Application architecture review, compatibility analysis. Feature 3.2: WCAG 2.1 Level AA Compliance Business Capability: Accessibility, legal compliance, market expansion Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Legal/Compliance Avoid accessibility lawsuits, regulatory compliance 🔴 HIGH Executive Leadership Risk mitigation, inclusive brand values 🟡 MEDIUM Customers (with disabilities) Accessible shopping experience 🔴 CRITICAL Marketing Team Expand addressable market (15% of population has disabilities) 🟡 MEDIUM Business Value: - Legal Risk Mitigation: Reduce risk of accessibility lawsuits (ADA Title III) - Market Expansion: 15% of global population has disabilities (WHO estimate) - Brand Reputation: Demonstrate commitment to inclusion and accessibility - SEO: Accessible sites often rank better (better semantic HTML) Risk: Remediation effort may be larger than expected (mitigation: prioritize critical issues first). Dependencies: Accessibility audit, screen reader testing, remediation expertise. Feature 3.3: Order Tracking and Management Business Capability: Customer self-service, reduced support costs Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Customers Track shipment, view order status, cancel/modify orders 🔴 HIGH Customer Support Reduced support ticket volume (~30-40% reduction expected) 🔴 HIGH Executive Leadership Lower support costs, better customer satisfaction 🟡 MEDIUM IT Operations Integration with shipping carriers 🟢 LOW Business Value: - Support Cost Reduction: Estimated 30-40% reduction in order status inquiries - Customer Satisfaction: Customers want order visibility (industry standard) - Operational Efficiency: Automated order lifecycle updates Risk: Integration with shipping carriers may be complex (mitigation: use third-party API like EasyPost or Shippo). Dependencies: Shipping carrier API access, order fulfillment workflow definition. Feature 3.4: Admin Portal (Product and Order Management) Business Capability: Operational efficiency, content management Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Marketing Team Add/edit products without developer assistance 🔴 HIGH IT Operations Manage orders, troubleshoot customer issues 🔴 HIGH Executive Leadership Operational independence, faster time to market 🟡 MEDIUM Development Team No longer needed for content updates 🟡 MEDIUM Business Value: - Operational Efficiency: Non-technical staff can manage content - Time to Market: Add new products without development cycle - Cost Savings: Reduce developer involvement in operational tasks Risk: Admin security must be robust (mitigation: role-based access control, audit logging). Dependencies: Admin UI framework, role-based permissions design. 2.4 Phase 4 Features (Months 13+) Feature 4.1: Personalization Engine Business Capability: Customer retention, increased AOV Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Marketing Team Personalized recommendations, targeted campaigns 🔴 HIGH Executive Leadership Increased AOV, customer retention 🔴 HIGH Customers Relevant product suggestions, time savings 🟡 MEDIUM Business Value: - Average Order Value (AOV): Estimated 15-20% increase through cross-sell and upsell - Customer Retention: Personalized experience increases repeat purchases - Competitive Advantage: Matches Amazon/Netflix-style recommendations Risk: Recommendation quality depends on data volume (mitigation: start simple with "frequently bought together"). Dependencies: Customer behavior data collection, recommendation algorithm selection. Feature 4.2: Progressive Web App (PWA) Business Capability: App-like experience, offline support, engagement Stakeholder Mapping: Stakeholder Value Delivered Priority to Stakeholder Customers Add to home screen, offline browsing, push notifications 🟡 MEDIUM Marketing Team Push notifications for abandoned carts, order updates 🟡 MEDIUM IT Operations Single codebase (no separate mobile app) 🟡 MEDIUM Business Value: - Engagement: Push notifications increase return visits - User Experience: App-like experience without app store friction - Cost Savings: No separate native mobile app development Risk: Browser support varies (mitigation: progressive enhancement, fallbacks). Dependencies: Service worker implementation, push notification service. 3. Feature Prioritization Matrix 3.1 Prioritization Criteria Criterion Weight Description Business Value 30% Revenue impact, cost savings, risk mitigation Stakeholder Impact 25% Number and influence of stakeholders benefiting Implementation Complexity 20% Development effort, risk, dependencies Strategic Alignment 15% Alignment with long-term business strategy Time to Value 10% How quickly value can be realized 3.2 Priority Scores Feature Business Value Stakeholder Impact Complexity Strategic Alignment Time to Value Total Score Priority Mobile-Responsive Design 10 10 6 9 8 8.8 🔴 P0 (Critical) GDPR Compliance 9 9 5 8 9 8.2 🔴 P0 (Critical) Cloud Migration 8 8 7 10 6 7.9 🔴 P0 (Critical) Guest Checkout 9 8 7 7 7 7.8 🟡 P1 (High) Automated Testing 7 7 6 9 6 7.1 🟡 P1 (High) Product Search 8 7 6 7 7 7.1 🟡 P1 (High) AJAX Interactions 6 7 5 7 7 6.4 🟡 P1 (High) Order Tracking 7 7 6 6 5 6.5 🟢 P2 (Medium) WCAG Compliance 6 6 8 6 4 6.2 🟢 P2 (Medium) .NET 6+ Migration 7 6 9 10 3 6.8 🟢 P2 (Medium) Admin Portal 6 6 7 7 5 6.3 🟢 P2 (Medium) Personalization 8 7 8 8 4 7.2 🔵 P3 (Low) PWA 5 5 7 7 4 5.7 🔵 P3 (Low) Scoring Scale: 1 (lowest) to 10 (highest) 3.3 Prioritization Decisions P0 (Critical) - Deliver in Phase 1: - Mobile-Responsive Design - GDPR Compliance - Cloud Migration - Automated Testing (enables safe modernization) P1 (High) - Deliver in Phase 2: - Guest Checkout - Product Search - AJAX Interactions - GDPR Data Portability P2 (Medium) - Deliver in Phase 3: - Order Tracking - WCAG Compliance - .NET 6+ Migration - Admin Portal P3 (Low) - Deliver in Phase 4: - Personalization Engine - Progressive Web App 4. Risk Assessment Matrix 4.1 Feature Risk Analysis Feature Technical Risk Business Risk Mitigation Strategy Contingency Plan Cloud Migration MEDIUM (downtime) HIGH (business disruption) Blue-green deployment, rollback plan Revert to on-premises if critical issues Mobile Design LOW (CSS framework) LOW (user adaptation) Gradual rollout, A/B testing Maintain desktop fallback GDPR Compliance LOW (well-defined requirements) HIGH (legal consequences if incomplete) Legal review, data protection consultant Prioritize most critical rights first Guest Checkout MEDIUM (order attribution) MEDIUM (data quality) Account linking, email verification Require registration for future orders .NET 6+ Migration HIGH (large codebase migration) MEDIUM (regressions) Phased migration, extensive testing Pause migration if too many issues WCAG Compliance MEDIUM (scope uncertainty) MEDIUM (legal risk if incomplete) Accessibility audit first, prioritize critical issues Partial compliance with roadmap for full compliance 4.2 Risk Mitigation Framework Technical Risk Mitigation: - Automated testing (catch regressions early) - Code reviews (ensure quality) - Proof-of-concept (validate approach before full implementation) - Rollback plans (revert if critical issues) Business Risk Mitigation: - Stakeholder communication (manage expectations) - Phased rollout (limit blast radius) - Monitoring and alerting (detect issues quickly) - Customer communication (announce changes, collect feedback) 5. Success Criteria and KPIs 5.1 Business KPIs KPI Current Baseline Target (6 months) Target (12 months) Measurement Mobile Conversion Rate To be established +30% improvement +50% improvement Google Analytics Cart Abandonment Rate To be established -20% reduction -25% reduction Google Analytics Page Load Time (Mobile) To be established <2 seconds <1.5 seconds Application Insights GDPR Compliance Score 0% 100% (Phase 1) 100% (maintained) Compliance audit WCAG Compliance Unknown Audit complete Level AA (100%) Accessibility audit System Uptime Unknown 99.5% 99.9% Application Insights Deployment Frequency Manual (weeks) Daily (automated) Multiple/day CI/CD pipeline Test Coverage 0% 50% 80% Code coverage tools Note: Baselines require measurement infrastructure (Application Insights) implemented in Phase 1. 5.2 Stakeholder Success Metrics Executive Leadership: - ✅ Revenue growth from mobile improvements - ✅ GDPR compliance achieved (zero fines) - ✅ Cloud scalability demonstrated (handle 10x traffic spike) Customers: - ✅ Mobile experience rated 4+ stars (user survey) - ✅ Checkout process < 3 minutes (user journey tracking) - ✅ Order tracking available (feature adoption) Marketing Team: - ✅ Conversion rate improvement ≥ 20% - ✅ Product search implemented (search usage analytics) - ✅ Personalization engine live (recommendation click-through rate) IT Operations: - ✅ Zero downtime deployments - ✅ Automated scaling working (scale events logged) - ✅ Monitoring and alerting operational (mean time to detect < 5 minutes) Development Team: - ✅ Modern tech stack (.NET 6+) - ✅ Automated testing (80%+ coverage) - ✅ CI/CD pipeline (deployment time < 15 minutes) Customer Support: - ✅ Support ticket volume reduced 30% (ticket tracking) - ✅ Order tracking feature live (feature adoption) - ✅ Self-service FAQ/help center (deflection rate) Legal/Compliance: - ✅ GDPR compliance audit passed - ✅ Accessibility audit passed (WCAG 2.1 Level AA) - ✅ Zero regulatory violations or fines 6. Communication and Governance 6.1 Communication Plan Stakeholder Communication Frequency: Stakeholder Group Communication Type Frequency Content Executive Leadership Executive Summary Monthly Progress, risks, budget, decisions needed Project Steering Committee Steering Committee Meeting Bi-weekly Detailed progress, blockers, prioritization IT Operations Technical Sync Weekly Infrastructure changes, deployments, incidents Development Team Sprint Planning/Retro Weekly Feature prioritization, technical decisions, blockers Marketing Team Business Update Monthly Feature releases, customer impact, metrics Customer Support Training and Updates Per release New features, process changes, training materials Legal/Compliance Compliance Review Quarterly Compliance status, audit findings, remediation Customers Product Announcements Per major release New features, improvements, privacy updates 6.2 Decision-Making Framework Decision Authority: Decision Type Authority Process Strategic (e.g., scope changes, budget increases) Executive Sponsor Steering Committee recommendation → Executive approval Tactical (e.g., feature prioritization within phase) Project Manager + Tech Lead Team consensus → Steering Committee notification Technical (e.g., technology choices, architecture) Tech Lead + Architects Technical review → Project Manager approval Operational (e.g., deployment timing, rollback) IT Operations Manager DevOps team recommendation → Ops Manager approval Escalation Path: 1. Team Lead (day-to-day decisions) 2. Project Manager (tactical decisions, blockers) 3. Steering Committee (prioritization changes, resource allocation) 4. Executive Sponsor (budget, scope, strategic direction) 6.3 Governance Meetings Steering Committee: - Attendees: Executive Sponsor, Project Manager, Tech Lead, IT Ops Manager, Marketing Manager, Legal Counsel - Frequency: Bi-weekly - Agenda: Progress review, risk assessment, prioritization adjustments, decision-making Technical Review Board: - Attendees: Tech Lead, Architects, Senior Developers - Frequency: Weekly - Agenda: Architecture decisions, technology choices, technical debt management Stakeholder Updates: - Attendees: All stakeholders - Frequency: Monthly - Format: Email summary + optional Q&A session - Content: Feature releases, progress highlights, upcoming changes 7. Summary and Recommendations 7.1 Key Stakeholder Priorities Highest Priority Stakeholder Needs: 1. Customers: Mobile experience (P0 - Critical) 2. Executive Leadership: GDPR compliance and risk mitigation (P0 - Critical) 3. Executive Leadership: Revenue growth through improved conversion (P1 - High) 4. Legal/Compliance: Full regulatory compliance (P0-P2 across phases) 5. IT Operations: Scalability and reliability (P0 - Critical) 7.2 Feature Prioritization Summary Must Have (Phase 1): - Mobile-responsive design - GDPR compliance (privacy policy, cookie consent, data deletion) - Cloud migration (scalability foundation) - Automated testing (safe modernization) Should Have (Phase 2): - Guest checkout (reduce cart abandonment) - Product search (industry standard) - AJAX interactions (modern UX) - GDPR data portability (complete compliance) Could Have (Phase 3): - Order tracking (customer self-service) - WCAG compliance (accessibility) - .NET 6+ migration (long-term maintainability) - Admin portal (operational efficiency) Won't Have (This Phase, but Phase 4): - Personalization engine - Progressive Web App 7.3 Recommendations Secure Executive Sponsorship Early: Assign clear executive sponsor with decision-making authority. Establish Steering Committee: Form steering committee with representatives from all key stakeholder groups. Communicate Proactively: Use communication plan to keep stakeholders informed and engaged. Measure Success: Implement Application Insights in Phase 1 to baseline current metrics and track improvements. Manage Expectations: Be transparent about priorities, trade-offs, and timeline. Celebrate Wins: Recognize and communicate successes at each phase to maintain momentum. docs.text: This document maps modernization features to business value, stakeholder needs, risks, and implementation priorities. It provides a framework for decision-making and stakeholder communication throughout the modernization initiative. Purpose: Enable stakeholders to: - Understand how modernization features deliver business value - Prioritize features based on stakeholder needs and business impact - Assess risks and dependencies - Track modernization progress against stakeholder expectations

docs.title: 1.1 Primary Stakeholders

docs.text: Executive Leadership: - 🎯 Need: Increased revenue and market share - 😓 Pain: Technology obsolescence risk, GDPR non-compliance risk, unable to serve mobile customers - 📊 Success Metric: Revenue growth, cost reduction, risk mitigation Customers: - 🎯 Need: Easy, fast shopping experience on any device - 😓 Pain: Desktop-only site (poor mobile experience), forced registration before checkout, slow page loads - 📊 Success Metric: Conversion rate, cart abandonment rate, customer satisfaction (NPS) Marketing Team: - 🎯 Need: Tools to drive customer acquisition and retention - 😓 Pain: Cannot run promotions (no promo code), no customer analytics, no personalization, English-only - 📊 Success Metric: Customer acquisition cost (CAC), conversion rate, average order value (AOV) IT Operations: - 🎯 Need: Reliable, scalable infrastructure with minimal manual intervention - 😓 Pain: Single-server architecture (single point of failure), cannot scale, manual deployments, no monitoring - 📊 Success Metric: Uptime (99.9%+), deployment frequency, mean time to recovery (MTTR) Development Team: - 🎯 Need: Modern tools and practices for productive development - 😓 Pain: Obsolete tech stack, no automated tests, difficult to recruit developers, slow feedback loops - 📊 Success Metric: Development velocity, deployment frequency, code quality, developer satisfaction Customer Support: - 🎯 Need: Self-service tools to reduce support volume - 😓 Pain: Customers cannot track orders, cannot cancel/modify orders, no returns portal - 📊 Success Metric: Support ticket volume, resolution time, customer satisfaction Legal/Compliance: - 🎯 Need: Regulatory compliance, data protection, risk mitigation - 😓 Pain: GDPR non-compliance, no data subject rights, no cookie consent, accessibility unknown - 📊 Success Metric: Compliance audit results, zero regulatory fines, zero accessibility lawsuits

Risk: Migration downtime (mitigation: blue-green deployment), unexpected cloud costs (mitigation: cost monitoring and budgets). Dependencies: Cloud provider selection, infrastructure team availability.

docs.text: Architecture Documentation Generation Summary Generated: 2026-06-09 Solution: Agathas.Storefront E-commerce Application Analysis Source: 60 analysis JSON files + codebase inspection Documentation Standard: C4 Model, ADR, ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 Executive Summary Comprehensive architecture documentation has been generated for the Agathas.Storefront solution, a legacy ASP.NET MVC 2 e-commerce application built circa 2010. The documentation reveals a well-architected system following Domain-Driven Design and layered architecture principles, but requiring critical modernization due to technology obsolescence and security vulnerabilities. Key Findings: - Strong Architecture Foundation: Excellent DDD implementation, clean separation of concerns, SOLID principles - Critical Technical Debt: .NET Framework 3.5/4.0 obsolescence, jQuery 1.3.2 security vulnerabilities, SQL Server User Instance deprecated - Modernization Imperative: Requires migration to .NET 6+, ASP.NET Core, modern authentication, cloud-ready infrastructure Documents Generated CURRENT-STATE Architecture Documentation (4 documents) 1.1 System Architecture (✅ COMPLETE - 15,000+ words) Location: .solutiondocs/CURRENT-STATE/1-architecture/1.1-system-architecture.md Contents: - C4 Architecture Diagrams: - Level 1: System Context (external dependencies: PayPal, Janrain, SMTP, SQL Server) - Level 2: Container Diagram (7 projects, database architecture) - Level 3: Component Diagram (controllers, services, repositories, cross-cutting concerns) - Level 4: Code Structure (sequence diagrams showing request flows) Architectural Patterns Documented (9 patterns): Layered Architecture (N-Tier) - 5 layers with unidirectional dependencies Domain-Driven Design - Aggregates, entities, value objects, domain events Repository Pattern - Clean data access abstraction Unit of Work Pattern - Transaction management Service Layer Pattern - Business logic orchestration Dependency Injection - StructureMap IoC container State Pattern - Order state management Factory Pattern - Object creation Domain Events - In-process event bus Architectural Characteristics Analysis: Performance: ⚠️ Medium (no caching, synchronous only) Scalability: ❌ Low (monolithic, no distributed caching) Availability: ❌ Low (single point of failure, LocalDB) Reliability: ✅ Medium (good error handling, transactions) Maintainability: ✅ High (excellent layering, DDD patterns) Security: ❌ Critical (outdated frameworks, plaintext secrets, vulnerabilities) Testability: ✅ High (interface-based, DI, but no tests exist) Portability: ❌ Low (Windows/.NET Framework only) Observability: ⚠️ Low (basic logging, no APM) Deployability: ⚠️ Medium (manual deployment, no CI/CD) Technology Stack Inventory: Complete listing of all technologies with versions and status Obsolescence assessment (jQuery 1.3.2, ASP.NET MVC 2, .NET 3.5/4.0 all critical) Architectural Decision Records (10 ADRs): ADR-001: .NET Framework and ASP.NET MVC selection ADR-002: NHibernate as ORM ADR-003: Layered Architecture with DDD ADR-004: StructureMap for Dependency Injection ADR-005: Request/Response Messaging Pattern ADR-006: PayPal Standard Payments Integration ADR-007: SQL Server LocalDB with User Instance (DEPRECATED) ADR-008: Domain Events with Static Class ADR-009: ASPX View Engine (SUPERSEDED) ADR-010: No Caching Implementation (DEFERRED) Technical Debt Analysis: P0 (Critical): .NET obsolescence, jQuery CVEs, SQL User Instance, plaintext secrets P1 (High): NHibernate upgrade, StructureMap replacement, no monitoring P2 (Medium): No CI/CD, no unit tests, synchronous-only processing Key Metrics: - 7 Visual Studio projects - 9 MVC controllers - ~30 HTTP endpoints - 4 business services - 15 domain entities - 5 architectural layers 1.2 Data Architecture (✅ COMPLETE - 12,000+ words) Location: .solutiondocs/CURRENT-STATE/1-architecture/1.2-data-architecture.md Contents: - Data Storage Inventory: - Primary: SQL Server Express LocalDB (Shop database) - Secondary: SQL Server Express LocalDB (aspnetdb for Membership) - File Storage: App_Data (MDF files), C:\logs\ (Log4Net) - Caching: NHibernate first-level cache (session-scoped), no second-level cache - Message Queues: None (no async processing) - Configuration: Web.config (plaintext secrets - security issue) Database Schema Documentation: Complete Entity-Relationship Diagram (Mermaid) 15 core tables organized into 5 aggregate clusters: Product Catalog (ProductTitle, Product, Brand, Category, ProductSize, ProductColor) Shopping Basket (Basket, BasketItem) Order Processing (Order, OrderItem, Payment) Customer Management (Customer, DeliveryAddress) Shipping (DeliveryOption, ShippingService, Courier) Table definitions with columns, types, constraints Relationships and foreign keys explained Critical design patterns (soft delete, price snapshotting, audit trails) Data Flow Diagrams: Read operation flow (product catalog browse with NHibernate caching) Write operation flow (add item to basket with transaction management) Order submission flow (complex transaction with domain events and PayPal) ORM and Data Access Patterns: NHibernate 2.1 with HBM.XML mappings Repository pattern implementations Unit of Work pattern (session per HTTP request) Query object pattern Lazy loading and N+1 problem analysis Data Security and Compliance: Authentication data storage (ASP.NET Membership with SHA1 hashing - weak) Sensitive data inventory (PII, passwords, payment IDs, addresses) Compliance gaps (PCI-DSS, GDPR, CCPA) Encryption assessment (no encryption at rest, depends on IIS for HTTPS) SQL injection prevention (NHibernate parameterized queries - good) Performance Considerations: Query performance risks (N+1 queries, no second-level caching) Connection pool management Performance monitoring gaps Recommended database indexes Backup and Recovery: Current state: NO AUTOMATED BACKUPS Critical gaps (no RPO/RTO, no point-in-time recovery) Recommended backup strategy (full daily, transaction log every 15 min) Data Migration and ETL: No schema versioning (schema inferred from HBM.XML) Recommended migration tools (FluentMigrator, DbUp, EF Core Migrations) Monitoring and Diagnostics: Current capabilities: Limited (Log4Net file logging only) Observability gaps (no query performance tracking, no alerting) Recommended monitoring (SQL Extended Events, Application Insights) Future Considerations: Short-term: Migrate from User Instance, schema versioning, caching, backups Medium-term: NHibernate upgrade, read replicas, encryption, audit logging Long-term: Cloud migration (Azure SQL/AWS RDS), microservices data strategy Key Issues Identified: - ❌ SQL Server User Instance (deprecated, not production-ready) - ❌ No automated backups - ❌ No encryption at rest - ❌ SHA1 password hashing (weak) - ❌ No second-level caching - ❌ No schema versioning 1.3 API Integration Catalog (✅ COMPLETE - 10,000+ words) Location: .solutiondocs/CURRENT-STATE/1-architecture/1.3-api-integration-catalog.md Important Note: This is an ASP.NET MVC server-side application, NOT a REST API. Document catalogs MVC endpoints and external integrations. Contents: - MVC Endpoint Catalog: - 9 Controllers documented with all actions - HomeController - Landing page with featured products - ProductController - Catalog browsing, search (GET endpoints + AJAX JSON endpoint) - BasketController - Shopping cart operations (POST endpoints + AJAX quantity update) - CheckoutController - Order submission ([Authorize] required) - PaymentController - PayPal callback handling - OrderController - Order history ([Authorize] required) - CustomerController - Account management ([Authorize] required) - AccountLogOnController - Login (local + Janrain social login) - AccountRegisterController - User registration Total: ~30 HTTP endpoints HTML Endpoints: 25 (server-side rendered ASPX views) JSON Endpoints: 2 (AJAX product search, basket quantity update) External API Dependencies (3 integrations): 1. PayPal Standard Payments: - Integration: Redirect-based payment (Form POST) - Endpoint: https://www.sandbox.paypal.com/cgi-bin/webscr - Purpose: Credit card payment processing - Authentication: Business email (no API key) - Criticality: CRITICAL - Blocks revenue if unavailable - Issues: Sandbox mode, no IPN, no signature verification, API key in plaintext - Sequence diagram provided 2. Janrain Social Authentication: - Integration: OAuth callback - Purpose: Facebook/Google/Twitter login - Authentication: API key in Web.config (plaintext) - Criticality: High - Reduces registration friction - Issues: Legacy provider, API key in plaintext - Sequence diagram provided 3. docs.text: Comprehensive architecture documentation has been generated for the Agathas.Storefront solution, a legacy ASP.NET MVC 2 e-commerce application built circa 2010. The documentation reveals a well-architected system following Domain-Driven Design and layered architecture principles, but requiring critical modernization due to technology obsolescence and security vulnerabilities. Key Findings: - Strong Architecture Foundation: Excellent DDD implementation, clean separation of concerns, SOLID principles - Critical Technical Debt: .NET Framework 3.5/4.0 obsolescence, jQuery 1.3.2 security vulnerabilities, SQL Server User Instance deprecated - Modernization Imperative: Requires migration to .NET 6+, ASP.NET Core, modern authentication, cloud-ready infrastructure

docs.text: The Agathas.Storefront solution demonstrates excellent architectural design for its era (2010) with strong Domain-Driven Design implementation, clean separation of concerns, and proper use of architectural patterns. However, 16 years of technology evolution have rendered the technology stack obsolete, creating critical security vulnerabilities and production-readiness concerns . Modernization is imperative and should begin immediately with critical security fixes (jQuery upgrade, secrets management, HTTPS enforcement), followed by production database migration and systematic platform modernization to .NET 6+/8 and ASP.NET Core. The strong architectural foundation provides an excellent base for modernization—the layered architecture, DDD patterns, and clean abstractions will translate well to modern .NET and cloud-native architectures. docs.title: 1. Domain Model Excellence

docs.text: Technology Obsolescence: - ASP.NET MVC 2 (released 2010, obsolete for 15+ years) - jQuery 1.3.2 (released 2009, known security vulnerabilities) - .NET Framework 3.5/4.0 (out of mainstream support) Mobile Experience: - Desktop-only design (NOT mobile-responsive) - 70%+ of e-commerce traffic is mobile - Estimated 30-50% revenue loss from poor mobile experience GDPR Non-Compliance: - No data subject rights (erasure, portability, access) - No cookie consent banner - Potential fines: €20 million or 4% of global annual revenue Scalability Limitations: - Cannot scale horizontally (in-process session, LocalDB) - Single-server architecture (single point of failure) - No auto-scaling capability Testing Gap: - Zero automated tests (0% coverage) - High risk of regressions during modernization
docs.title: 2. Critical Business Gaps

docs.text: Mobile Conversion Improvement: - Implement mobile-responsive design - Expected: 30-50% increase in mobile conversion rate - Capture 70%+ of traffic currently having poor experience Cart Abandonment Reduction: - Implement guest checkout (remove forced registration) - Expected: 20-25% reduction in cart abandonment - Industry data: Forced registration increases abandonment by ~25% International Expansion: - Implement internationalization (multi-language, multi-currency) - Opportunity: Access 75% of global e-commerce market (currently English-only) - Markets: EU (27 countries), Latin America, Asia-Pacific Compliance and Risk Mitigation: - Achieve GDPR compliance (avoid €20M fines or 4% revenue) - Implement WCAG accessibility (expand market, reduce legal risk) - Modernize security (eliminate known vulnerabilities)

The solution demonstrates excellent architectural design for its era, with clean layered architecture and Domain-Driven Design patterns. However, the technology stack is severely outdated (15+ years old) with critical security vulnerabilities and no automated testing. all 10-15 years old Security ⚠️ HIGH RISK 8 identified vulnerabilities (Critical/High severity) Secrets in plain text (API keys, connection strings in Web.config) No HTTPS enforcement Outdated dependencies with known CVEs No security headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options, etc.) GDPR non-compliant Testing & Quality ⚠️ CRITICAL GAP 0% test coverage - no automated tests exist Highly testable code (DI, interfaces) but untested No CI/CD pipeline No quality gates High risk for refactoring without tests Scalability ⚠️ MAJOR LIMITATIONS Cannot scale horizontally (in-process session state) LocalDB co-located with web server Single point of failure No load balancing No distributed caching Operations & Observability ⚠️ MINIMAL File-based logging only (no centralized logging) No APM or monitoring No alerting Manual deployment No DR plan No documented incident response Business Domain ✅ STRONG Clear domain boundaries (Products, Baskets, Orders, Customers) Rich business logic encapsulated in domain Well-defined workflows PayPal payment integration Social login via Janrain Modernization Priorities Immediate (Critical) Add comprehensive test suite - Critical before any refactoring Address security vulnerabilities - Update jQuery, enforce HTTPS Externalize secrets - Move to Azure Key Vault Fix session state - Migrate to Redis for horizontal scaling Migrate database - Replace LocalDB with Azure SQL Short-term (High Priority) Migrate to .NET 6/8 - Modern platform foundation Implement CI/CD - Automate build and deployment Add observability - Application Insights or similar Activate caching - Enable decorator layer Add health checks - Support orchestration Medium-term (Strategic) Separate API from UI - Create REST API backend Modernize authentication - Replace with Azure AD B2C or Auth0 Upgrade PayPal integration - Move to REST API Containerize application - Docker containers Implement GDPR compliance - Data subject rights Long-term (Transformation) Modern SPA frontend - React/Angular/Vue Microservices (if needed) - Decompose by bounded contexts Cloud-native architecture - Full Azure PaaS API-first approach - Enable mobile apps, integrations Migration Strategy Recommendation Hybrid Approach (Preserve architecture, modernize technology): Preserve: Excellent domain model and business logic Clean layered architecture DDD patterns and structure Modernize: Platform (.NET 6/8) Presentation layer (API + SPA) Infrastructure (Azure services) Development practices (testing, CI/CD) Reasoning: The architecture is sound and well-designed.
